functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function determines the file permissions (mode) applied when creating the UNIX socket. The default mode is set in the function body.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A local user connects to the UNIX socket created with overly permissive default permissions.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insecure default permissions on a sensitive IPC object.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function's default socket_mode was set to 0666 (world-readable and world-writable) if no explicit listen_mode configuration was provided.
required_preconditions: The PHP-FPM process runs and creates a UNIX socket.
The configuration does not specify a 'listen_mode' to override the default.

fix.strategy: Tighten the default permissions to be more restrictive.
changed_operations: Changed the default assignment to wp->socket_mode from 0666 to 0660.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The default socket mode is 0660 (owner and group read/write), unless explicitly overridden by configuration.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse Wave64 file headers to extract audio configuration parameters and validate file structure
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted file input containing chunk headers and audio metadata, with validation checks for file format correctness

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a maliciously crafted Wave64 file with a data chunk appearing before the format chunk
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use of uninitialized structure field
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The WaveHeader structure was declared but not initialized before use. When the data chunk is encountered before the format chunk, WaveHeader.NumChannels is uninitialized but used in calculations
required_preconditions: Malicious Wave64 file with data chunk placed before format chunk
Program attempts to parse the file

fix.strategy: Explicit initialization of the WaveHeader structure before any conditional use
changed_operations: Added CLEAR(WaveHeader) call to zero-initialize the structure
fix.post_fix_invariant: WaveHeader fields are guaranteed to be initialized (zero) before any conditional code paths that might read them

functional_semantics.purpose: The function _6502_op analyzes 6502 processor opcodes to determine instruction size, type, and generate ESIL (Intermediate Language) expressions for emulation/simulation.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function processes raw binary data from a ROM file without validating that sufficient bytes are available for multi-byte opcodes, leading to out-of-bounds memory reads.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted iNES ROM binary file containing an opcode that requires additional bytes (like a branch instruction) but providing insufficient input data.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check before accessing array elements.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: In the branch instruction case (0x10, 0x30, etc.), the code accesses data[1] to compute a relative jump address without first verifying that len > 1. This causes an out-of-bounds read when the input buffer is too short.
required_preconditions: The function receives a len parameter indicating available data bytes.
The opcode corresponds to a branch instruction (0x10, 0x30, 0x50, 0x70, 0x90, 0xb0, 0xd0, 0xf0).
The provided len is 1 or less, meaning data[1] is out of bounds.

fix.strategy: Add a length check before accessing potentially out-of-bounds array elements.
added_guards: if (len > 1) { ... } else { op->jump = addr; }
changed_operations: The branch instruction case now guards the access to data[1] with a length check.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The function now ensures that multi-byte opcodes only access data within the bounds provided by the len parameter.

functional_semantics.purpose: Execute regular expression matching with backtracking using a stack-based approach.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes input data against compiled regex opcodes, tracking matched bytes count and managing stack for alternative paths.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted file containing a regex pattern with REPEAT_ANY_UNGREEDY opcode.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect bounds calculation during backtracking leads to out-of-bounds read.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When handling REPEAT_ANY_UNGREEDY, the loop pushes stack entries for alternative paths after incrementing bytes_matched by 'i', but the subsequent addition of repeat_any_args->min to bytes_matched can exceed max_bytes_matched, causing later operations to read beyond input buffer.
required_preconditions: Input contains regex pattern with REPEAT_ANY_UNGREEDY opcode
Pattern matching reaches alternative paths where i > repeat_any_args->min

fix.strategy: Enforce upper bound on bytes_matched after adding repeat_any_args->min.
added_guards: bytes_matched = yr_min(bytes_matched, max_bytes_matched)
changed_operations: Moved bounds check before next_input calculation in REPEAT_ANY_UNGREEDY loop
fix.post_fix_invariant: bytes_matched never exceeds max_bytes_matched after processing REPEAT_ANY_UNGREEDY opcode.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process a regex match found during scanning, handling match validation and storage
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Writes match data to arena buffers without validating match boundaries

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted file that produces an out-of-bounds match
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check before buffer write
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function writes match_data to an arena buffer using match_length without verifying match_offset + match_length <= data_size
required_preconditions: Match offset and length derived from untrusted input
No validation of match boundaries before write operation

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds assertion before using match data
added_guards: assert(match_offset + match_length <= callback_args->data_size)
fix.post_fix_invariant: Match offset and length are validated to be within data bounds before any buffer operations

functional_semantics.purpose: Allocate memory for a bitmap image with various color modes and optional alpha channel
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Calculates row size based on width and color mode, then allocates memory for pixel data and optional alpha channel

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PDF file with specific width/height values
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow during memory allocation size calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Multiplication of rowSize * height or width * height can overflow before allocation, leading to undersized buffer allocation
required_preconditions: Controlled width/height values
Row size calculation that multiplies width by bytes per pixel
Multiplication result exceeding integer maximum

fix.strategy: Replace unsafe multiplication with overflow-checked allocation function
changed_operations: Replaced gmalloc(rowSize * height) with gmallocn(rowSize, height)
Replaced gmalloc(width * height) with gmallocn(width, height)
fix.post_fix_invariant: Memory allocation uses overflow-safe multiplication

functional_semantics.purpose: Render a glyph from a font into a bitmap for display
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory for bitmap data based on computed dimensions from font metrics

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PDF file with malicious font glyph metrics
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow during memory allocation calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Multiplication of rowSize and bitmap->h in gmalloc(rowSize * bitmap->h) can overflow when product exceeds integer range
required_preconditions: Malicious font metrics causing large bitmap dimensions
RowSize calculation producing non-zero value

fix.strategy: Replace unsafe multiplication with bounds-checked allocation function
changed_operations: Replaced gmalloc(rowSize * bitmap->h) with gmallocn(rowSize, bitmap->h)
fix.post_fix_invariant: Allocation size calculation checks for integer overflow before multiplication

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse network packet headers (L2 and L3) from raw data for transmission processing.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Extracts IP header length field from packet data and uses it to determine how much optional header data to copy.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted IP packet with an invalid IP header length field value.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use of attacker-controlled value without validation for memory access bounds.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The IP header length field (IHL) extracted from the packet was used directly to calculate a copy size without ensuring it meets the minimum valid length for an IP header.
required_preconditions: Local guest OS administrator access
Ability to send network packets to the emulated device

fix.strategy: Add validation check before using the extracted length value.
added_guards: Check that IP header length is not less than the size of struct ip_header
changed_operations: Added bounds validation on l3_hdr->iov_len after assignment from IP_HDR_GET_LEN
fix.post_fix_invariant: IP header length used for buffer operations is guaranteed to be at least the size of the basic IP header structure.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process SVGA command FIFO for virtual graphics device emulation
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses untrusted guest-supplied cursor definition data including dimensions and pixel data, writing to fixed-size arrays

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing SVGA_CMD_DEFINE_CURSOR command with crafted cursor dimensions
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Bounds check uses sizeof(array) instead of element count, allowing overflow
vulnerability.detailed_cause: SVGA_BITMAP_SIZE(x,y) > sizeof cursor.mask comparison miscalculates capacity; sizeof(cursor.mask) returns bytes but comparison needs element count
required_preconditions: Guest has administrative privileges
SVGA_CMD_DEFINE_CURSOR command issued
Malicious cursor width/height/bpp values

fix.strategy: Replace byte-based sizeof with element-count-based sizeof division
added_guards: sizeof(cursor.mask)/sizeof(cursor.mask[0])
sizeof(cursor.image)/sizeof(cursor.image[0])
changed_operations: Bounds check calculation
fix.post_fix_invariant: Cursor data size checks compare against array element capacity, not byte size

functional_semantics.purpose: HTTP stream wrapper for PHP that handles HTTP/HTTPS connections, including proxy support, request/response processing, and redirection.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses HTTP response headers from a network stream, including status lines and header fields, and stores them in a response array.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an HTTP response where the status line is exactly 9 characters long (e.g., 'HTTP/1.0 ').
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Stack-based buffer under-read due to unsafe pointer arithmetic without length validation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When reading the initial HTTP status line, the code calculates a pointer offset (tmp_line + 9) to extract the status code, assuming the line length is greater than 9. If the line length is exactly 9, the pointer points to one byte past the allocated buffer, leading to an under-read when atoi() accesses memory beyond the buffer.
required_preconditions: The HTTP server sends a malformed or minimal status line exactly 9 characters long.
The vulnerable code path is executed (standard HTTP request handling).

fix.strategy: Add explicit length checks before performing pointer arithmetic and buffer accesses.
added_guards: Check that tmp_line_len >= 1 before accessing tmp_line[tmp_line_len - 1].
Check that tmp_line_len > 9 before calculating pointer offset tmp_line + 9.
changed_operations: Changed conditional from 'if (tmp_line_len > 9)' to 'if (tmp_line_len > 9)' (same check, but added length guard for subsequent array accesses).
Added length guard before accessing tmp_line[tmp_line_len - 1] for newline trimming: 'if (tmp_line_len >= 1 && tmp_line[tmp_line_len - 1] == '\n')'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: Pointer arithmetic and array indexing on the tmp_line buffer are only performed after verifying the buffer has sufficient length for the operation.

functional_semantics.purpose: Set a scanout region for display output, associating a graphical resource with a display output channel.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Creates and manages display surfaces from pixman images, with reference counting for shared resources.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Repeatedly issuing VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_SET_SCANOUT commands that cause the creation of new display surfaces.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing reference count decrement on a pixman image after successful surface creation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function calls pixman_image_create_bits() and pixman_image_ref() to create and reference an image, but fails to call pixman_image_unref() on the created rect image when scanout->ds is successfully created, causing a memory leak.
required_preconditions: Guest can issue VIRTIO_GPU_CMD_SET_SCANOUT commands
Commands pass validation checks
qemu_create_displaysurface_pixman() succeeds

fix.strategy: Add missing reference count decrement to balance reference counting.
changed_operations: Added pixman_image_unref(rect) after successful surface creation
fix.post_fix_invariant: Each pixman_image_create_bits() call that succeeds must have a corresponding pixman_image_unref() call when the image is no longer needed.

functional_semantics.purpose: Read and decode a PNG image file into memory using libpng, performing color space conversions and allocating storage for pixel data.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory based on image dimensions and row byte count obtained from libpng after transformations.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PNG file with specific dimensions/format causing an integer overflow in size calculation.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in calculation of total memory allocation size.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The calculation 'rowbytes * mainprog_ptr->height' can overflow when rowbytes is large, bypassing an earlier width*height overflow check.
required_preconditions: Malicious PNG file with manipulated dimensions/format
rowbytes value large enough to cause overflow when multiplied by height

fix.strategy: Add overflow check for the actual allocation size calculation.
added_guards: Check if rowbytes > INT_MAX/height before multiplication
changed_operations: Moved overflow check from width*height to rowbytes*height calculation
fix.post_fix_invariant: Both width*height and rowbytes*height calculations are checked for overflow before allocation.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse H.263 picture header to extract video dimensions and coding parameters
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Decodes width and height values from input stream and uses them to calculate macroblock grid dimensions

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a file with crafted width/height dimensions
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of derived values before arithmetic operations
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Calculating macroblock dimensions using width/height values without checking for integer overflow or zero division
required_preconditions: Width or height values cause mb_width or mb_height to be zero
Subsequent division by zero in ff_h263_decode_mba

fix.strategy: Add early validation of image dimensions before calculating derived values
added_guards: av_image_check_size(s->width, s->height, 0, s) call before mb_width/mb_height calculations
changed_operations: Moved dimension validation earlier in control flow
fix.post_fix_invariant: Width and height are validated before being used in division operations

functional_semantics.purpose: Process received network packets in Stellaris ethernet controller emulation
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Stores received packet data and metadata into a circular buffer with fixed-size slots

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving a network packet larger than the buffer can accommodate
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing size validation before buffer write
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Packet length not checked against available buffer space before copying data and updating state
required_preconditions: Stellaris ethernet controller configured to accept large packets
Network packet reception enabled

fix.strategy: Add early size validation to reject oversized packets
added_guards: Check if packet size exceeds available buffer space before any state modification
changed_operations: Added size validation check
Added error reporting via SE_INT_FOV interrupt flag
fix.post_fix_invariant: Packet size is validated before any buffer write or state update occurs

functional_semantics.purpose: Handle iSCSI asynchronous I/O ioctl requests from guest OS
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes SCSI command descriptor blocks (CDBs) from untrusted guest input and transfers data between guest and iSCSI target

vulnerability.triggering_action: Guest OS issues crafted iSCSI asynchronous I/O ioctl call with SG_IO request
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of user-controlled input size before buffer copy operation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: cmd_len field from guest-controlled ioh structure used in memcpy without bounds checking against destination buffer size
required_preconditions: Local guest OS access
iSCSI block device in use
SG_IO ioctl request type

fix.strategy: Add input validation before dangerous operation
added_guards: Check that cmd_len does not exceed SCSI_CDB_MAX_SIZE
changed_operations: Added early validation and error return path
fix.post_fix_invariant: cmd_len is bounded by SCSI_CDB_MAX_SIZE before memcpy to cdb buffer

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse header metadata from an .aa audio file format, extracting encryption keys and codec information to initialize decryption and audio stream parameters.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses untrusted file input containing string values that are converted to numeric data via sscanf without checking for conversion success, potentially leaving destination variables uninitialized.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a maliciously crafted .aa file where the 'HeaderKey' value string cannot be successfully parsed into four unsigned integers by sscanf.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unchecked return value of a parsing function leads to use of uninitialized stack variables.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The sscanf call to parse four 32-bit integers from the 'HeaderKey' string value did not check its return value. If the string format mismatched (e.g., contained fewer than four numbers or non-numeric characters), sscanf would fail partially or completely, leaving some elements of header_key_part array uninitialized. These uninitialized values were later used in cryptographic key derivation.
required_preconditions: The file passes initial format validation
The 'HeaderKey' metadata entry exists but contains malformed content

fix.strategy: Add explicit validation of parsing success before using parsed values.
added_guards: Check that sscanf returns exactly 4 (the expected number of conversions)
changed_operations: Added return value check for sscanf
Added error return (AVERROR_INVALIDDATA) when parsing fails
fix.post_fix_invariant: The header_key_part array is only used after confirming successful parsing of all four required integers from the input string.

functional_semantics.purpose: Check access control for modifying userAccountControl flags during account creation or modification
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates that the requester has appropriate privileges (extended rights, specific privileges, or administrative group membership) to set or change specific userAccountControl bits

vulnerability.triggering_action: Creating or modifying a machine account (changing between UF_NORMAL_ACCOUNT and UF_WORKSTATION_TRUST_ACCOUNT bits)
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing privilege check for a specific userAccountControl bit transition
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function did not check for domain admin group membership when swapping between UF_NORMAL_ACCOUNT and UF_WORKSTATION_TRUST_ACCOUNT bits during machine account creation/modification
required_preconditions: Remote authenticated user
Domain with both Samba DC and Windows DC
Ability to create/modify machine accounts

fix.strategy: Added explicit privilege checks for specific userAccountControl bit transitions
added_guards: Domain admin group membership check for UF_NORMAL_ACCOUNT ↔ UF_WORKSTATION_TRUST_ACCOUNT transitions
changed_operations: Extended access control mapping to include privilege requirements for specific bit transitions
fix.post_fix_invariant: All userAccountControl bit transitions require appropriate privilege verification (extended rights, specific privileges, or administrative group membership)

functional_semantics.purpose: Decrypt and validate a SPICE ticket password for authentication
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes encrypted password data from a client ticket, compares it against stored credentials, and handles authentication failure

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving a SPICE ticket with a password longer than SPICE_MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Fixed-size buffer overflow
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Stack-allocated buffer 'password' sized to SPICE_MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH could be overflowed by RSA_private_decrypt output when RSA modulus size exceeds buffer size
required_preconditions: Ticketing enabled
Client sends encrypted password
RSA modulus size > SPICE_MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH

fix.strategy: Replace fixed stack buffer with dynamically allocated buffer sized to RSA modulus
added_guards: Warning when RSA modulus size < SPICE_MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH
Error handling for RSA_private_decrypt failure
changed_operations: Buffer allocation moved from stack to heap
Password comparison changed from strncmp with fixed length to strcmp
Centralized error handling with goto
fix.post_fix_invariant: Password buffer always sized to accommodate full RSA decryption output plus null terminator

functional_semantics.purpose: Load virtio-net device state from migration stream
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Deserializes network device configuration from untrusted input during VM migration

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing migration data where curr_queues value exceeds max_queues
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of array index bounds during deserialization
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The curr_queues field read from migration stream was used as loop bound without checking it against max_queues, leading to out-of-bounds write
required_preconditions: Multi-queue feature enabled (max_queues > 1)
Malicious or corrupted migration stream

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds check before using untrusted value as array index
added_guards: Check that curr_queues <= max_queues before loop iteration
changed_operations: Added validation of curr_queues against max_queues
fix.post_fix_invariant: curr_queues never exceeds max_queues when used as array index

functional_semantics.purpose: Convert token enumeration values to human-readable string representations for debugging or display purposes.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Copies token name strings into a caller-provided buffer with size limit 'len'. Must ensure writes stay within buffer bounds.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling jslTokenAsString with insufficient buffer size for the token's string representation.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Buffer overflow due to improper use of strncpy without null-termination guarantee.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: strncpy does not null-terminate the destination buffer when the source string length equals or exceeds the specified limit. The function assumed strncpy would null-terminate, but when len exactly matched source length or was smaller, the buffer remained unterminated, leading to out-of-bounds reads.
required_preconditions: Caller provides buffer smaller than required token string
Token value corresponds to a long string (e.g., 'UNFINISHED TEMPLATE LITERAL')

fix.strategy: Replace strncpy with strcpy after adding explicit length validation.
added_guards: Added assertion requiring len > 28 (size of largest string) at function entry
changed_operations: Replaced all strncpy(str, "...", len) calls with strcpy(str, "...")
fix.post_fix_invariant: Buffer size is verified upfront to accommodate the largest possible string, allowing safe use of strcpy without length parameter.

functional_semantics.purpose: Wait for data to drain from a USB serial port buffer and device during close/disconnect operations
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accesses tty structure obtained from port to manage write wait queue and perform cleanup

vulnerability.triggering_action: Read or write operation on /dev/ttyUSB device after USB serial converter disconnection
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use of a potentially NULL pointer obtained from a tty port without validation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The tty pointer returned by tty_port_tty_get() could be NULL if the tty was detached, leading to NULL pointer dereference when accessing tty->write_wait
required_preconditions: USB serial converter is disconnected
User attempts to read or write to the device

fix.strategy: Add early NULL check for the tty pointer before using it
added_guards: if (!tty) return;
changed_operations: Added NULL check after tty_port_tty_get() call
fix.post_fix_invariant: tty pointer is validated before any dereference operations

functional_semantics.purpose: Disassemble WebAssembly (WASM) opcodes from a binary buffer into a textual representation.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses variable-length LEB128 integers from a user-controlled buffer and constructs a formatted string within a fixed-size buffer.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted WASM file containing a BRTABLE opcode with a large count value.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: A buffer boundary calculation error during string concatenation leads to an out-of-bounds read.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The loop condition `strlen(op->txt) < R_ASM_BUFSIZE` does not account for the length of the upcoming formatted integer string. This allows repeated calls to `strlen` and `snprintf` to read beyond the `op->txt` buffer's end when constructing the BRTABLE output.
required_preconditions: The input buffer must contain a valid WASM BRTABLE opcode.
The 'count' field read by `read_u32_leb128` must be sufficiently large.
The subsequent table entries must cause the concatenated string length to approach or exceed R_ASM_BUFSIZE.

fix.strategy: Enforce a stricter, pre-calculated length check before each string append operation.
added_guards: A check that `strlen(op->txt) + 10 < R_ASM_BUFSIZE` before appending each table entry.
Use of the remaining buffer size (`R_ASM_BUFSIZE - optxtlen`) in the `snprintf` call.
changed_operations: Replaced the loop condition and `snprintf` call for appending table indices. The new logic calculates the current string length once per iteration and uses it to bound the write.
fix.post_fix_invariant: Each `snprintf` call that appends to `op->txt` is given the correct remaining buffer size, preventing out-of-bounds reads during the format string processing.

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode CCITT fax-encoded image data stream, handling both 1-D and 2-D encoding modes to produce pixel data.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted input data (fax stream) containing variable-length codes and references to previous line data.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Reading from an uninitialized array element when processing 2-D encoded fax data.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient initialization of reference line array before use in 2-D decoding.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'refLine' array was only partially initialized in the 2-D decoding path. The code initialized elements up to index 'i' where 'codingLine[i] < columns', then set 'refLine[i++] = columns' and 'refLine[i] = columns'. This left remaining array elements (from i+1 to columns+1) uninitialized, which could be read later during decoding operations.
required_preconditions: Processing 2-D encoded fax data (nextLine2D is true)
The reference line array 'refLine' has more elements than those initialized by the partial initialization loop

fix.strategy: Complete initialization of the entire reference line array before use.
changed_operations: Replaced the two-element assignment 'refLine[i++] = columns; refLine[i] = columns;' with a loop that initializes all remaining array elements from index 'i' to 'columns+1' to 'columns'
fix.post_fix_invariant: All elements of the 'refLine' array from index 0 to 'columns+1' are initialized before being read during 2-D decoding.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse Java bytecode switch (tableswitch) instruction to extract jump table cases
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads variable-length data from input buffer based on calculated offsets and table size

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted Java binary file containing a tableswitch instruction
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient bounds check before reading switch table header fields
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The check 'pos + 8 > len' only validated reading 8 bytes, but the code immediately reads 12 bytes (default_loc, min_val, max_val) from position 'pos'
required_preconditions: Input buffer length ('len') is less than 'pos + 12'
Switch opcode (0xaa) is present
Calculated 'pos' value positions read pointer within buffer

fix.strategy: Strengthen initial bounds check to cover all header reads before accessing data
added_guards: pos + 8 + 8 > len
changed_operations: Changed guard from 'pos + 8 > len' to 'pos + 8 + 8 > len'
fix.post_fix_invariant: Before reading switch header fields (default_loc, min_val, max_val), ensure at least 16 bytes are available from position 'pos'

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize decoder context for VQA video format, parsing header and allocating buffers.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses image dimensions and block size from input, allocates decode buffer based on these values.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted VQA media file where image dimensions are not multiples of block size.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of relationship between image dimensions and block size.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The decode buffer size calculation assumes width/vector_width and height/vector_height produce integer results. When image dimensions are not multiples of block size, integer division truncation leads to undersized buffer allocation, causing heap overflow during decoding.
required_preconditions: Malicious input with width % vector_width != 0 or height % vector_height != 0
Decoder proceeds to decode_chunk operation

fix.strategy: Add explicit validation that image dimensions are multiples of block size before buffer allocation.
added_guards: Check: s->width & (s->vector_width - 1)
Check: s->height & (s->vector_height - 1)
changed_operations: Added early return with error if dimension validation fails
fix.post_fix_invariant: Image dimensions are verified to be integer multiples of block size before any buffer size calculations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize WavPack encoder configuration for audio compression
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes user-provided audio configuration parameters including sample rate, channel count, and format flags to set up encoding streams

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted audio file with a zero sample rate
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of critical input parameter
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function accepted a sample rate of zero without checking, leading to downstream infinite loop during stream processing
required_preconditions: User-provided audio configuration with sample_rate = 0
Hybrid encoding mode enabled (CONFIG_HYBRID_FLAG)
Bitrate calculation using CONFIG_BITRATE_KBPS

fix.strategy: Add early validation check for invalid parameter value
added_guards: Explicit check rejecting zero sample rate at function entry
fix.post_fix_invariant: Sample rate must be non-zero before any further processing occurs

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize and open a codec context for encoding/decoding operations
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Handles resource allocation, validation, and cleanup for codec initialization, including error recovery paths

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling avcodec_open2() with a codec that has a NULL close function pointer, followed by an initialization failure
vulnerability.abstract_cause: NULL pointer dereference during error cleanup
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The error cleanup path unconditionally calls avctx->codec->close(avctx) without checking if the close function pointer exists
required_preconditions: Codec structure has NULL close pointer
Codec initialization fails or early error occurs
Execution reaches the free_and_end error handling path

fix.strategy: Add NULL check before calling function pointer
added_guards: Check avctx->codec->close != NULL before calling
changed_operations: Conditional call to close function based on pointer validity
fix.post_fix_invariant: The close function is only called when the pointer is non-NULL

functional_semantics.purpose: Reset bitstream reading state to a specific bit position
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Calculates remaining bytes available for reading based on buffer size and word offset, then reads data using that calculation

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling faad_resetbits with bits parameter that makes words*4 exceed ld->buffer_size
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer underflow in buffer size calculation leading to buffer overflow
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When ld->buffer_size - words*4 results in negative value, it gets cast to unsigned integer (ld->bytes_left), causing large positive value that bypasses bounds checks
required_preconditions: words*4 > ld->buffer_size
ld->bytes_left is unsigned type

fix.strategy: Add explicit check to prevent negative calculation before assignment
added_guards: if (ld->buffer_size < words * 4) ld->bytes_left = 0
changed_operations: Replaced direct assignment with conditional assignment
fix.post_fix_invariant: ld->bytes_left is never negative after calculation

functional_semantics.purpose: Convert a solid path into a dashed path according to line dash pattern and phase
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes user-controlled dash patterns and path coordinates to generate new path data

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a path with specific dash pattern and phase values
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check during dash pattern phase calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: While loop computing lineDashStartIdx could increment beyond array bounds when lineDashStartPhase exceeds total dash pattern length
required_preconditions: Non-empty dash pattern array
Line dash phase value that causes cumulative dash length comparison to exceed array bounds

fix.strategy: Add bounds check during phase calculation and early exit for invalid state
added_guards: Check lineDashStartIdx < state->lineDashLength in while loop condition
Check if lineDashStartIdx equals lineDashLength after loop and return empty path
changed_operations: Added array bounds validation before array access
fix.post_fix_invariant: lineDashStartIdx is guaranteed to be within array bounds during phase calculation

functional_semantics.purpose: Binary search function to find register information for a given instruction ID in a sorted array
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Performs array bounds checking before binary search to prevent out-of-bounds access

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling the function with an instruction ID outside the range of IDs stored in the array
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check before binary search loop
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The binary search algorithm could access array elements beyond valid bounds when searching for IDs not present in the array
required_preconditions: The target ID is not present in the sorted array
The ID is outside the min/max range of array elements

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds check before entering binary search loop
added_guards: Range check comparing target ID against first and last array elements
changed_operations: Moved mid calculation inside loop
Added early return for out-of-range IDs
fix.post_fix_invariant: Binary search only executes when target ID is within the range of IDs stored in the array

functional_semantics.purpose: Process E-AC-3 audio frames during AVI to MPEG-4 conversion, handling independent and dependent substreams to construct a valid 'dec3' atom metadata.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses and validates E-AC-3 frame headers, tracks substream IDs and types, and concatenates audio blocks. It assumes a specific substream ordering and frame type sequence.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted AVI file containing an E-AC-3 frame where the frame_type is not EAC3_FRAME_TYPE_INDEPENDENT, but the substreamid is non-zero.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation for non-independent frame types with non-zero substream IDs.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The original code only validated that substreamid must be 0 for AC-3 streams (bitstream_id <= 10). For E-AC-3 frames (bitstream_id > 10), it only performed the 'substreamid must be incremental' check inside the 'if (hdr->frame_type == EAC3_FRAME_TYPE_INDEPENDENT)' block. Therefore, if frame_type was not INDEPENDENT (e.g., DEPENDENT, AC3_CONVERT), the code would proceed to the array write 'info->substream[hdr->substreamid]...' without ensuring substreamid was within bounds or valid for that frame type.
required_preconditions: An E-AC-3 frame (bitstream_id > 10) with a frame_type other than INDEPENDENT.
The substreamid field in that frame's header is non-zero.
The info->ec3_done flag is false (still processing stream configuration).

fix.strategy: Add explicit validation for non-independent frame types before the array access.
added_guards: Added an 'else' clause after the independent frame check to handle cases where 'hdr->frame_type != EAC3_FRAME_TYPE_INDEPENDENT'. This guard checks if 'hdr->substreamid != 0' and returns an error (AVERROR_PATCHWELCOME).
changed_operations: Extended the conditional logic for frame_type. Previously, only INDEPENDENT frames had their substreamid validated against info->num_ind_sub. Now, non-INDEPENDENT frames are explicitly checked to ensure substreamid is zero.
fix.post_fix_invariant: For any E-AC-3 frame processed while ec3_done is false, if the frame_type is not INDEPENDENT, its substreamid must be zero. This prevents out-of-bounds write to the info->substream array.

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize a blitter context for OpenGL rendering operations
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Creates OpenGL resources (vertex arrays, framebuffers, buffers) without checking if already initialized

vulnerability.triggering_action: Repeated calls to initialize the blitter context
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing state tracking for resource initialization
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function creates new OpenGL resources each time it's called without setting an initialization flag, causing repeated resource allocation
required_preconditions: Function can be called multiple times
No cleanup of previously allocated resources

fix.strategy: Add state tracking to prevent re-initialization
added_guards: Setting blit_ctx->initialised = true after first initialization
changed_operations: Added state flag assignment
fix.post_fix_invariant: The function creates resources only once per context instance

functional_semantics.purpose: Convert migration stream offset to host memory pointer during RAM loading
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads block identifier and offset from migration stream, returns pointer to RAM block memory region

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing crafted migration savevm data with malicious offset or length values
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check on offset parameter
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Function returned pointer to memory region without validating offset against block length
required_preconditions: Migration stream contains malicious offset value
Function processes RAM_SAVE_FLAG_CONTINUE flag or finds matching block

fix.strategy: Add bounds checking before returning pointer
added_guards: Check block->length > offset before returning pointer
changed_operations: Added offset validation in RAM_SAVE_FLAG_CONTINUE path
Added offset validation in block matching path
fix.post_fix_invariant: Offset must be less than block length when returning pointer

functional_semantics.purpose: Calculate network checksums for TCP/UDP packets within IPv4 frames
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted packet data from guest OS without validating buffer boundaries before accessing header fields

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling net_checksum_calculate with a crafted packet containing insufficient payload length
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds heap read due to missing bounds check
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Function reads IPv4 header fields (total length, protocol) and calculates offsets without verifying the input buffer has sufficient data for those operations
required_preconditions: Guest OS provides crafted packet
Payload length in IPv4 header is smaller than required for checksum calculation

fix.strategy: Add early validation of minimum buffer size before processing header fields
added_guards: Check that length >= 34 bytes (14-byte L2 + 20-byte L3 header) before accessing IPv4 header fields
changed_operations: Added bounds check at function entry
fix.post_fix_invariant: Function returns early if input buffer cannot contain complete L2 and L3 headers

functional_semantics.purpose: Allocate kernel memory with metadata header
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accepts size parameter, adds header size, allocates memory pool

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling function with large size value
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in arithmetic operation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Addition of size parameter and header size without overflow check
required_preconditions: Size parameter large enough to cause overflow when added to header size

fix.strategy: Replace unchecked arithmetic with safe integer addition
added_guards: Explicit overflow check before addition
changed_operations: Replaced 'size + sizeof(header)' with overflow-checked addition
fix.post_fix_invariant: Allocation size calculation is checked for integer overflow

functional_semantics.purpose: Process API requests for chart data with support for Google Visualization API parameters
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses and uses user-supplied query parameters to construct HTTP responses including JSONP callbacks and Content-Disposition headers

vulnerability.triggering_action: User supplies specially crafted parameter values containing newlines or other control characters
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unsanitized user input used directly in HTTP response headers and JavaScript callbacks
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Parameters like responseHandler, outFileName, google_version, google_reqId, google_sig, and google_out were not validated before being embedded in HTTP headers and JavaScript responses
required_preconditions: API endpoint accessible to attackers
User can control query parameters

fix.strategy: Add input validation/sanitization for Google Visualization API parameters
added_guards: Added fix_google_param() calls to sanitize google_out, google_sig, google_reqId, google_version, responseHandler, and outFileName parameters
changed_operations: Added parameter sanitization before using values in HTTP headers and JavaScript responses
fix.post_fix_invariant: All Google API parameters are sanitized before being used in response construction

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse JavaScript expressions including unary operators like 'void'
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The 'void' operator case consumed the next token without checking parser stack limits

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a 'void' token during syntax parsing
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing stack overflow check before parsing unary expression
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The LEX_R_VOID case in jspeFactor() called jspeUnaryExpression() without first calling jspCheckStackPosition()
required_preconditions: User-crafted input file
Parsing reaches 'void' token
Parser stack is near limit

fix.strategy: Add stack limit check before parsing unary expression for 'void' operator
added_guards: jspCheckStackPosition() call before LEX_R_VOID case
changed_operations: Added stack check for 'void' token parsing
fix.post_fix_invariant: All unary operator cases (delete, typeof, void) now check stack limits before parsing their operands

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse PostScript Type1 font data from PDF files to extract font name and character encoding information.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes font encoding arrays where numeric indices from font data are used to access an array of size 256.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PostScript Type1 font containing a negative array index value.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Array index validation missing lower bound check.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code accepted 'code' values from font data using atoi() without verifying they are non-negative before using them as array indices.
required_preconditions: Font data contains '/Encoding 256 array' directive
Font contains 'dup' statements with numeric index values
Numeric index parses to negative integer via atoi()

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds check for both upper and lower array index limits.
added_guards: Check that code >= 0 before array access
changed_operations: Changed condition from 'if (code < 256)' to 'if (likely(code < 256 && code >= 0))'
fix.post_fix_invariant: Array index 'code' is guaranteed to be within [0, 255] before accessing encoding[code].

functional_semantics.purpose: Validate safety of blit operations in Cirrus VGA emulator
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Checks whether blit operations could access unsafe memory regions

vulnerability.triggering_action: Performing blit operations with certain parameters
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incomplete validation of blit operation parameters
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Missing validation for source buffer size in blit operations
required_preconditions: Guest-controlled blit parameters
Source buffer size exceeding safe limits

fix.strategy: Add explicit size validation before performing blit operations
added_guards: Check that blit width does not exceed maximum buffer size
changed_operations: Removed source region safety check
Added width boundary check
fix.post_fix_invariant: Blit width must not exceed defined buffer size limit

functional_semantics.purpose: Scale an image mask using Bresenham's algorithm for both vertical and horizontal scaling
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accesses destination bitmap data pointer without validation

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling scaleMaskYdXu with a destination bitmap containing a NULL data pointer
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing NULL pointer check before dereference
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function dereferences dest->data at line 'destPtr = dest->data;' without verifying it's non-NULL
required_preconditions: dest parameter points to a SplashBitmap object
dest->data field is NULL

fix.strategy: Add explicit NULL check and early return with error
added_guards: Check if dest->data is NULL before using it
changed_operations: Added conditional check: if (destPtr == NULL) { error(...); return; }
fix.post_fix_invariant: dest->data is verified non-NULL before any memory access operations

functional_semantics.purpose: Recursively parse and interpret file format magic numbers to identify file types.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes indirect magic entries that can trigger recursive parsing of file data at computed offsets.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted file containing magic entries that cause deep or infinite recursion.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unbounded recursion due to insufficient recursion depth limit.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The recursion depth limit was a hard-coded constant (20) that could be exceeded by specially crafted magic entries, leading to stack exhaustion or excessive CPU consumption.
required_preconditions: A magic database entry of type FILE_INDIRECT or FILE_USE that points to other magic entries.
A crafted file that matches the pattern triggering recursive parsing.
Recursion depth exceeding the hard-coded limit.

fix.strategy: Increase the recursion depth limit by replacing the hard-coded constant with a defined macro (MAX_RECURSION_LEVEL).
added_guards: Changed recursion level check from 'recursion_level >= 20' to 'recursion_level >= MAX_RECURSION_LEVEL'.
changed_operations: Replaced magic number 20 with symbolic constant MAX_RECURSION_LEVEL.
fix.post_fix_invariant: Recursion depth is bounded by MAX_RECURSION_LEVEL, which is defined elsewhere and presumably set to a safer value.

functional_semantics.purpose: Queue an error SKB (socket buffer) onto a socket's error queue for error reporting
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Adds SKB to socket's error queue with accounting of socket's receive memory allocation

vulnerability.triggering_action: Crafted system calls using SCM_TIMESTAMPING_OPT_STATS feature
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of SKB metadata before queueing
vulnerability.detailed_cause: SKB lacked proper marking as error queue packet before being placed in error queue
required_preconditions: Local user access
Ability to make crafted system calls

fix.strategy: Explicitly mark SKB as belonging to error queue before queueing
changed_operations: Added skb_set_err_queue(skb) call
fix.post_fix_invariant: SKB is explicitly marked for error queue before being queued

functional_semantics.purpose: Process DMARC (Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting & Conformance) for email messages, extracting sender domain from the From header for authentication evaluation.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses and extracts domain information from the From email header to perform DMARC policy checks.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Remote attacker sends an email with a specially crafted From header.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unsafe expansion of unsanitized user-controlled header data.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function expand_string was called on a string built from from_header->text without proper validation or sanitization. This allowed arbitrary content from the attacker-controlled From header to be interpreted as expansion commands.
required_preconditions: EXPERIMENTAL_DMARC feature enabled
Processing of email with a From header

fix.strategy: Replace unsafe dynamic string expansion with a dedicated email address parsing function.
added_guards: Use of parse_find_address_end to safely locate address boundaries
Use of parse_extract_address to extract domain portion
changed_operations: Removed expand_string call on from_header->text
Added proper email address parsing with boundary checking
fix.post_fix_invariant: The From header content is parsed as a structured email address rather than being interpreted as expansion commands.

functional_semantics.purpose: Handle 9P protocol read operations for different file types (directory, regular file, extended attribute)
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes guest-initiated read requests with memory allocation for I/O vectors

vulnerability.triggering_action: Local guest OS administrators performing I/O read operations
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Resource management error under error conditions
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Memory leak when error occurs during file read path before cleanup
required_preconditions: Guest administrator privileges
Error condition during file read operation

fix.strategy: Ensure cleanup execution on all error paths
changed_operations: Added new error handling label for I/O vector cleanup
Redirected error jumps to cleanup label
fix.post_fix_invariant: I/O vectors are destroyed on all exit paths from file read branch

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse CAF (Core Audio Format) file headers to extract audio configuration and metadata.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes chunk-based file format with variable-sized data sections, including audio format description ('desc'), channel layout ('chan'), and audio data ('data') chunks.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a CAF file where the 'data' chunk appears before the required 'desc' (description) chunk.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use of uninitialized stack variable.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function accesses 'caf_audio_format.mBytesPerPacket' when calculating 'total_samples' in the 'data' chunk handler, but 'caf_audio_format' is only initialized if a 'desc' chunk has been previously encountered and processed. If a malicious file places the 'data' chunk first, the structure remains uninitialized.
required_preconditions: Malicious CAF file with 'data' chunk preceding 'desc' chunk
Program attempts to parse the file

fix.strategy: Add state tracking to enforce required chunk ordering.
added_guards: Added 'desc_chunk' flag initialized to 0
Check that 'desc_chunk' is true before processing 'data' chunk
changed_operations: Set 'desc_chunk = 1' after successfully processing 'desc' chunk
Modified 'data' chunk condition to require 'desc_chunk'
fix.post_fix_invariant: The 'caf_audio_format' structure is guaranteed to be initialized before any calculations depending on its fields are performed.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse USB CDC (Communications Device Class) union descriptor to extract control and data interface information for a USB device driver.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function retrieves USB interface pointers using interface numbers from a CDC union descriptor without validating that the retrieved pointers are non-NULL before dereferencing them.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Connecting a malicious USB device that provides a CDC union descriptor with invalid interface numbers (bMasterInterface0 or bSlaveInterface0).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing NULL pointer checks after function calls that can return NULL.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function calls usb_ifnum_to_if() to obtain USB interface pointers but proceeds to dereference those pointers (accessing cur_altsetting member) without checking if the calls returned valid (non-NULL) pointers.
required_preconditions: Physical access to connect a USB device
USB device provides a CDC union descriptor with invalid interface numbers
Kernel attempts to parse the device's CDC data

fix.strategy: Add explicit NULL pointer checks after potentially failing function calls.
added_guards: NULL check for pcu->ctrl_intf after usb_ifnum_to_if() call
NULL check for pcu->data_intf after usb_ifnum_to_if() call
changed_operations: Added conditional return -EINVAL if pcu->ctrl_intf is NULL
Added conditional return -EINVAL if pcu->data_intf is NULL
fix.post_fix_invariant: USB interface pointers obtained from usb_ifnum_to_if() are validated to be non-NULL before being dereferenced.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse configuration metadata from a WavPack file to set up channel layout and reordering information.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted input data from a file to allocate memory and populate a channel reordering array.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Reading a crafted WV file containing malformed channel reordering data.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read due to insufficient validation of array indices.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The channel reordering array stores indices used to map channels, but the code did not verify that these indices are within the valid range of allocated channels.
required_preconditions: A WV file with a channel reordering block is processed
The reordering data contains an index value greater than or equal to the number of channels (nchans)

fix.strategy: Add bounds checking for channel reordering indices.
added_guards: Check if wpc->channel_reordering[i] >= nchans before using the index
changed_operations: When an out-of-bounds index is detected, clamp it to 0 instead of using it directly
fix.post_fix_invariant: All channel reordering indices are guaranteed to be less than nchans, preventing out-of-bounds array accesses.

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode audio data from a compressed WavPack bitstream by reading variable-length codes and applying entropy decoding.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function processes untrusted input data (WV files) and performs arithmetic operations on values derived from that input without validating that intermediate calculations produce sensible ranges.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted WV file that causes the calculated 'low' value to exceed the calculated 'high' value.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read due to an invalid range calculation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The variables 'low' and 'high' are derived from untrusted input data via entropy decoding. If 'low' becomes greater than 'high', the subsequent calculation of 'mid' and the loop condition 'high - low > c->error_limit' can lead to reading beyond intended bounds, as 'high - low' becomes negative and is interpreted as a large unsigned value.
required_preconditions: A malicious WV file is provided as input.
The file triggers a state where the decoded 'low' value exceeds the decoded 'high' value.

fix.strategy: Add a validation step to ensure the range is non-empty before proceeding.
added_guards: if (low > high) high = low;
changed_operations: Enforced the invariant that low <= high before computing mid and entering the range refinement loop.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The value of 'high' is guaranteed to be at least equal to 'low', ensuring 'high - low' is a non-negative value representing a valid range size.

functional_semantics.purpose: Clean up resources during device removal
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Memory region subregions are removed during device exit

vulnerability.triggering_action: Repeatedly unplugging a USB device when xhci uses msix
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Memory leak
vulnerability.detailed_cause: MSI-X memory regions not properly cleaned up when device uses MSI-X
required_preconditions: xhci uses msix
guest OS administrator privileges

fix.strategy: Replace manual MSI-X cleanup with dedicated uninitialization function
changed_operations: Replaced manual memory_region_del_subregion calls for msix_table_mmio and msix_pba_mmio with msix_uninit call
fix.post_fix_invariant: MSI-X cleanup uses dedicated uninitialization function

functional_semantics.purpose: Process a remote request to list all available network interfaces and return the list to the client.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function calculates the total payload length for the reply message based on the number of interfaces and their associated data (names, descriptions, addresses).

vulnerability.triggering_action: A client sends a FINDALLIF request with a non-zero payload length.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Reusing a function parameter variable for an internal calculation, corrupting its original intended meaning.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function parameter 'plen' (payload length of the incoming request) is reused as an accumulator variable to calculate the total length of the outgoing reply payload. The initial value of 'plen' (the length of the client's request data) is added to during the calculation, leading to an incorrect final reply length.
required_preconditions: The client can connect to the rpcapd service.
The client sends a FINDALLIF request with a payload length > 0.

fix.strategy: Introduce a separate, dedicated local variable for the internal calculation, preserving the original parameter's value and meaning.
changed_operations: Added a new local variable 'replylen' of type uint32.
Initialized 'replylen' to 0.
Replaced all accumulator operations on the parameter 'plen' with operations on 'replylen'.
Passed 'replylen' instead of 'plen' to the function that creates the reply header.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The parameter representing the length of the client's request payload is never modified. The length of the server's reply payload is calculated independently from scratch.

functional_semantics.purpose: List extended attributes of a file path
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory for extended attribute data, processes attributes, and must free allocated memory before returning on error paths

vulnerability.triggering_action: Call to flistxattrat_nofollow returns negative value (error)
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Memory leak on error path
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Missing g_free(orig_value) before returning -1 when xattr_len < 0
required_preconditions: Memory allocation succeeds (orig_value = g_malloc(xattr_len))
Second flistxattrat_nofollow call fails (returns negative value)

fix.strategy: Add missing memory deallocation on error path
added_guards: g_free(orig_value) before returning -1 when xattr_len < 0
changed_operations: Added memory deallocation operation
fix.post_fix_invariant: All allocated memory (orig_value) is freed before returning from function, regardless of success or error path

functional_semantics.purpose: Process kernel log buffer entries and forward them to console drivers, stripping log level prefixes.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses variable-length log entries from a circular buffer, extracting priority prefixes that may be malformed.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Writing crafted data to /dev/kmsg that includes a malformed log prefix.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unbounded read from a circular buffer into a function expecting a null-terminated string.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: log_prefix() was called directly with a pointer into the circular log buffer (LOG_BUF(cur_index)). This function reads until a null terminator or newline, but the buffer may wrap before encountering either, causing it to read past the intended end of the prefix and potentially overflow internal buffers.
required_preconditions: Local write access to /dev/kmsg
Ability to trigger console driver invocation via log output

fix.strategy: Copy a bounded prefix from the circular buffer into a local, null-terminated array before parsing.
added_guards: Limit copy length to SYSLOG_PRI_MAX_LENGTH
Explicit null-termination of the local buffer
changed_operations: Replaced direct pointer pass to log_prefix with a copy operation into a stack buffer
fix.post_fix_invariant: log_prefix() receives a null-terminated string of bounded length, regardless of circular buffer wrap.

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode various DPCM (Differential Pulse-Code Modulation) audio formats from input packets into output audio samples.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted input audio streams with stereo channel handling, calculates output buffer sizes based on input size and codec type, and writes decoded samples to an output buffer.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted stereo stream in a media file.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient validation of input buffer size parity for stereo audio decoding.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The decoder assumed stereo audio data would always have an even number of bytes, but a crafted stream with odd buffer size could cause misalignment during channel toggling, leading to buffer over-reads.
required_preconditions: Stereo audio stream (channels > 1)
Input buffer size is odd
Codec type is ROQ_DPCM or XAN_DPCM (based on fix scope)

fix.strategy: Enforce even buffer size for stereo streams by truncating odd-sized buffers.
added_guards: Check if stereo and buffer size is odd, then decrement buffer size by one
changed_operations: Added buffer size adjustment before output size calculation
Removed INTERPLAY_DPCM from output size switch (handled elsewhere)
Standardized ROQ_DPCM and XAN_DPCM to same output size calculation
fix.post_fix_invariant: For stereo streams, buffer size is guaranteed to be even before decoding begins.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse USB CDC union descriptor from interface extra data
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Iterates through variable-length descriptor buffer using length fields from untrusted USB device data

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted USB device descriptor
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read due to insufficient bounds checking
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Loop uses descriptor's bLength field to advance buffer pointer without validating that bLength doesn't exceed remaining buffer
required_preconditions: Local USB device access
Malicious descriptor with invalid bLength

fix.strategy: Add bounds validation before using descriptor fields
added_guards: Check union_desc->bLength <= buflen before using it
Verify descriptor meets minimum size requirement
changed_operations: Changed loop condition from buflen > 0 to buflen >= sizeof(*union_desc)
fix.post_fix_invariant: All descriptor length fields are validated against remaining buffer before use

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode base64-encoded image data from a COVERART tag and add it to a tag list.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory for decoded data based on untrusted input length, performs base64 decoding, and creates an image buffer.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted COVERART tag with base64-encoded data.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in memory allocation calculation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The calculation 'base64_len * 3 / 4' for allocation size can overflow when base64_len is large, leading to undersized buffer allocation.
required_preconditions: Attacker-controlled base64_len parameter
Large base64_len value that causes integer overflow

fix.strategy: Eliminate dynamic memory allocation for decoded data by performing in-place decoding.
changed_operations: Removed g_try_malloc0 call
Changed to decode directly into input buffer (now mutable)
Removed g_free calls
fix.post_fix_invariant: No separate buffer allocation based on untrusted size calculation; decoding occurs in-place on existing data.

functional_semantics.purpose: Transmit network packets by processing buffer descriptors in a linked list
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes buffer descriptors in a loop without limiting iterations

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing buffer descriptors with a length of 0 and crafted flag values
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unbounded loop iteration
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Loop continues indefinitely when buffer descriptors form a circular chain or lack termination condition
required_preconditions: Guest OS administrator access
Ability to craft buffer descriptor values

fix.strategy: Add iteration limit to bound processing
added_guards: Maximum descriptor count check (FEC_MAX_DESC)
changed_operations: Replaced while(1) with while(descnt++ < FEC_MAX_DESC)
fix.post_fix_invariant: Loop executes at most FEC_MAX_DESC iterations

functional_semantics.purpose: Process client request to add glyphs to a glyph set in the X server Render extension
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses variable-length client-supplied data containing glyph IDs, glyph info structures, and bitmap data, performing memory allocation and data copying based on client-controlled sizes

vulnerability.triggering_action: Client sends a maliciously crafted RenderAddGlyphs request
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient validation of pointer arithmetic results when computing offsets into client-supplied data buffer
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code computed pointers to glyph info (gi) and bitmap data (bits) by adding offsets to the request structure pointer without verifying these pointers remain within the bounds of the client's request buffer
required_preconditions: Client has local access to X server
Client can send Render extension requests
Client controls nglyphs field and request data

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds checks on computed pointers before using them
added_guards: Check that gi pointer is within request buffer bounds
Check that bits pointer is within request buffer bounds
changed_operations: Added validation: if (gi < stuff || gi > ((CARD32 *)stuff + client->req_len) || bits < stuff || bits > ((CARD32 *)stuff + client->req_len))
fix.post_fix_invariant: Pointers derived from client-controlled offsets are verified to point within the allocated request buffer before being dereferenced

functional_semantics.purpose: Align video frame dimensions to meet codec-specific alignment requirements for memory access patterns and hardware constraints.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Adjusts width and height parameters by rounding them up to alignment boundaries and potentially adding padding, which can affect buffer allocation sizes.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing video frames with specific pixel formats and codec combinations that lacked proper alignment constraints.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing alignment rules for certain codec and pixel format combinations led to undersized buffer allocations.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The Interplay video codec (AV_CODEC_ID_INTERPLAY_VIDEO) with PAL8, BGR8, RGB8, or RGB555 pixel formats did not have alignment constraints defined, causing width and height to remain unaligned or aligned to insufficient values.
required_preconditions: Using Interplay video codec
Specific pixel formats (PAL8, BGR8, RGB8, RGB555)
Unchecked frame dimensions

fix.strategy: Add missing alignment constraints for previously uncovered codec-pixel format combinations.
added_guards: Added alignment checks for AV_CODEC_ID_INTERPLAY_VIDEO with RGB555 format
Added alignment checks for AV_CODEC_ID_INTERPLAY_VIDEO with PAL8/BGR8/RGB8 formats
changed_operations: Set width and height alignment to 8 for Interplay video codec with affected pixel formats
fix.post_fix_invariant: All known codec and pixel format combinations now have appropriate alignment constraints enforced.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse x86 assembly operand strings into structured operand representations.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes user-controlled input strings representing memory addressing expressions (e.g., '[reg1+scale*reg2+offset]'), registers, and immediates. Maintains arrays (regs, scale) for register components of memory operands.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted operand string containing a memory addressing expression with more than two register components.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds array write.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The `reg_index` variable increments without bound when processing register components (`regs[reg_index]`, `scale[reg_index]`). The arrays `op->regs` and `op->scale` have fixed size (implied to be 2), but the loop lacks a check to prevent writing beyond the last element.
required_preconditions: The operand string represents a memory addressing expression (starts with '[').
The expression contains more than two register components (e.g., more than two registers separated by '+' or '-').

fix.strategy: Add bounds checks before writing to the fixed-size arrays.
added_guards: Conditional check `if (reg_index < 2)` before writing to `op->regs[reg_index]` and `op->scale[reg_index]`.
Conditional check `if (reg_index < 2)` before writing `X86R_UNDEFINED` to `op->regs[reg_index]`.
changed_operations: Array writes (`op->regs[reg_index] = reg;`, `op->scale[reg_index] = temp;`, `op->regs[reg_index] = X86R_UNDEFINED;`) are now guarded by the bounds check.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The `reg_index` variable may still increment beyond the array bounds for tracking purposes, but no array accesses occur when `reg_index >= 2`.

functional_semantics.purpose: Map physical memory regions described by descriptors into scatter-gather I/O vectors for virtio device operations.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes descriptor buffers with specified sizes, mapping physical memory into I/O vectors. Zero-sized buffers cause infinite loop.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Guest OS administrator provides a descriptor buffer with zero length.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation for zero-sized input in a loop termination condition.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The while loop condition 'while (sz)' depends on sz decrementing, but with initial sz=0, len=0, so sz -= 0 leaves sz unchanged at 0, causing infinite loop.
required_preconditions: Guest administrator privileges
Virtio indirect descriptor table usage
Zero-length buffer descriptor

fix.strategy: Add explicit guard clause to reject zero-sized inputs before loop entry.
added_guards: Early validation checking if sz == 0
changed_operations: Added pre-loop check with error report and exit
fix.post_fix_invariant: Function never processes zero-sized buffers; all calls must have sz > 0.

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode ASN.1 data structures from binary format
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: When decoding fails, the function frees allocated memory structures to prevent leaks

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing malformed X509_ATTRIBUTE data in PKCS#7 or CMS applications
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Memory cleanup performed incorrectly during error handling
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The ASN1_TFLG_COMBINE flag was not properly handled during error cleanup, causing premature freeing of memory structures
required_preconditions: ASN1_TFLG_COMBINE flag is set in the aclass parameter
Decoding failure occurs
Error handling path is triggered

fix.strategy: Conditional cleanup based on flag presence
added_guards: Check if ASN1_TFLG_COMBINE flag is set before calling ASN1_item_ex_free
changed_operations: Extract combine flag from aclass parameter early
Use combine flag to skip cleanup when needed
fix.post_fix_invariant: Memory is only freed during error handling when ASN1_TFLG_COMBINE flag is not set

functional_semantics.purpose: Process incoming TCP packets in a VPN connection
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Copies packet data from input buffer to fixed-size local structure without size validation

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving a TCP packet with length exceeding local buffer capacity
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check before buffer copy
vulnerability.detailed_cause: memcpy copies 'len' bytes from input buffer to fixed-size outpkt.data without verifying len <= sizeof(outpkt.data)
required_preconditions: Remote peer is authenticated
TCP packet transmission is used

fix.strategy: Add size validation guard before buffer copy
added_guards: Check if input length exceeds destination buffer size
changed_operations: Early return when length exceeds buffer capacity
fix.post_fix_invariant: memcpy only executes when input length <= destination buffer size

functional_semantics.purpose: Format and throw an error or exception with a custom message
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accepts a format string and variable arguments to construct an error message

vulnerability.triggering_action: Passing format string specifiers in a string used as a class name
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Uncontrolled format string
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The format parameter passed to zend_throw_error was used directly without a format string guard, allowing format specifiers in user-controlled input to be interpreted
required_preconditions: User-controlled string reaches the function as format argument
String contains format specifiers

fix.strategy: Enforce a fixed format string wrapper
changed_operations: Changed zend_throw_error call to use fixed format string '%s' with message as argument
fix.post_fix_invariant: The message parameter is always treated as a plain string argument, not as a format string

functional_semantics.purpose: Decompress data using zlib inflate with support for compressed packets that lack zlib headers
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes compressed input data in a loop, adding dummy bytes when using algorithm 1 (no zlib header) and refilling input buffer as needed

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing malformed compressed packets
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Infinite loop during decompression
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The decompression loop could continue indefinitely when processing certain malformed compressed packets
required_preconditions: Algorithm 1 is used (no zlib header)
Malformed compressed packet input
Specific byte sequence (a3 01 5b ff mentioned in CVE)

fix.strategy: Limit the number of dummy bytes added and add loop exit condition
added_guards: Maximum of 4 dummy 0xFF bytes for algorithm 1
Early loop exit when dummy byte added
changed_operations: Added counter (algo1hack) to track dummy bytes
Added leave flag to break loop
fix.post_fix_invariant: Loop terminates after adding at most 4 dummy bytes for algorithm 1

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse DNxHD video header from input buffer, validate format parameters, and initialize decoder context.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates buffer size constraints, reads and validates various header fields (bit depth, profile, dimensions), calculates data offsets, and checks array bounds for mb_scan_index array.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted DNxHD file with mb_height value that causes out-of-bounds array access.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation check for mb_height relative to frame height in interlaced mode.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The condition '(ctx->mb_height << frame->interlaced_frame) > (ctx->height + 15) >> 4' was only checked in the non-HR (high resolution) code path, not in the HR path. This allowed mb_height to exceed valid bounds when ff_dnxhd_check_header_prefix_hr(header_prefix) returned true.
required_preconditions: Crafted DNxHD file with header_prefix indicating HR format
frame->interlaced_frame = 1
ctx->mb_height value that violates height constraint

fix.strategy: Move the mb_height validation check outside the conditional block to ensure it executes for all code paths.
added_guards: Moved the check '(ctx->mb_height << frame->interlaced_frame) > (ctx->height + 15) >> 4' to execute unconditionally after the data_offset calculation
