fix.strategy: Add guard condition before division operations
added_guards: Check if stride equals 0
fix.post_fix_invariant: Function returns 0 when stride equals 0 before performing division

functional_semantics.purpose: Compare two null-terminated strings for equality
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Compares strings using a custom memory comparison function with a length determined by the first string's length

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling pure_strcmp with strings where the first string is longer than the second
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read due to incorrect length calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function uses strlen(s1) + 1 as the comparison length, which exceeds the bounds of s2 when s1 is longer than s2
required_preconditions: First string length > second string length
Second string memory region ends shortly after its null terminator

fix.strategy: Use the minimum string length plus one for comparison
added_guards: Length calculation now considers both string lengths
changed_operations: Comparison length changed from strlen(s1)+1 to min(strlen(s1), strlen(s2))+1
fix.post_fix_invariant: Comparison never reads beyond the shorter string's allocated memory

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse HVCC (H.265 Video Codec Configuration) atom data from MP4 container format
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Constructs object from external input data without validating minimum required size before processing

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an HVCC atom with size smaller than required for header parsing
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check before buffer access
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The constructor accessed payload array indices up to 22 without verifying payload_size >= 23
required_preconditions: Input size parameter results in payload_size < 23
Payload pointer points to valid memory region

fix.strategy: Add early size validation before any payload processing
added_guards: if (payload_size < 22) return;
changed_operations: Moved m_RawBytes.SetData() after size check
fix.post_fix_invariant: No payload accesses occur unless payload_size >= minimum required for parsing

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse AVC configuration atom payload containing sequence and picture parameter sets
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads variable-length data structures from input buffer without validating bounds

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing malformed AVC configuration atom with crafted parameter length values
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Buffer over-read due to insufficient bounds checking
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code reads parameter length values from input and uses them to copy data without verifying the remaining buffer size accommodates both the length field and the data it describes
required_preconditions: Input contains parameter length values exceeding available buffer space
Program processes untrusted media files

fix.strategy: Add bounds checks before reading length fields and copying parameter data
added_guards: Check cursor+2 <= payload_size before reading length
Check cursor+param_length <= payload_size before copying data
changed_operations: Moved parameter buffer appending inside bounds-checked blocks
fix.post_fix_invariant: All buffer accesses are preceded by verification that sufficient data exists in the payload

functional_semantics.purpose: Reserve space for a tensor list with specified number of elements
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accepts user-controlled integer to determine vector resize size without validation

vulnerability.triggering_action: Providing negative value for num_elements parameter
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of user-controlled size parameter before container resize operation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: User-provided integer passed directly to std::vector::resize() without checking for negative values
required_preconditions: User controls num_elements input
No validation of input sign

fix.strategy: Add explicit validation to reject negative size values
added_guards: Check that num_elements >= 0 before resize operation
fix.post_fix_invariant: num_elements parameter must be non-negative before vector resize

functional_semantics.purpose: Construct a matrix from diagonal values with configurable output dimensions and padding.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accepts user-controlled tensor parameters (num_rows, num_cols, padding_value) without validating they are non-empty scalars before accessing their contents.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Passing empty tensors for num_rows, num_cols, or padding_value parameters.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of tensor emptiness before accessing tensor data.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code directly accessed flat() data from input tensors without checking if those tensors were non-empty scalars, leading to out-of-bounds reads when empty tensors were provided.
required_preconditions: Operating in MatrixDiagV2 mode (more than kNumV1Inputs)
At least one of the parameter tensors (num_rows, num_cols, padding_value) is empty

fix.strategy: Add explicit scalar shape validation for each parameter tensor before accessing their data.
added_guards: TensorShapeUtils::IsScalar(num_rows_tensor.shape())
TensorShapeUtils::IsScalar(num_cols_tensor.shape())
TensorShapeUtils::IsScalar(padding_value_tensor.shape())
changed_operations: Added validation before reading num_rows from input(2)
Added validation before reading num_cols from input(3)
Added validation before reading padding_value from input(4)
fix.post_fix_invariant: All parameter tensors (num_rows, num_cols, padding_value) are verified to be scalars before their contents are accessed.

functional_semantics.purpose: Allocate and initialize a dithering object with a color palette
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates input parameters for palette color count and handles memory allocation

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PNG file with invalid color count parameter
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation for minimum color count input
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function allowed ncolors=0, which could lead to insufficient palette allocation or other downstream issues
required_preconditions: ncolors parameter equals 0
Function called with crafted input

fix.strategy: Add input validation for minimum color count
added_guards: Check if ncolors < 1 and return error
changed_operations: Changed lower bound check from ncolors < 2 to ncolors < 1
Added error status assignment for ncolors > SIXEL_PALETTE_MAX
fix.post_fix_invariant: ncolors must be ≥ 1 when ncolors ≥ 0

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse HEVC Picture Parameter Set (PPS) data from a bitstream and store it in a state structure.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads an unsigned exponential Golomb-coded integer (pps_id) and uses it as an array index without checking for negative values after initial bounds check.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malformed HEVC bitstream containing a PPS with a negative pps_id value.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation for negative array index after reading a signed integer from untrusted input.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function gf_bs_read_ue_log() returns a signed 32-bit integer, but the code only checked for values >= 64, allowing negative values to pass the bounds check and be used as an array index.
required_preconditions: The attacker controls the input bitstream.
The array hevc->pps has fixed size (64 elements).
Negative index calculation leads to out-of-bounds memory access.

fix.strategy: Add explicit lower bound check for negative values in addition to existing upper bound check.
added_guards: Check for pps_id < 0 before array access
changed_operations: Changed bounds check from 'pps->sps_id >= 16' to '(pps->sps_id<0) || (pps->sps_id >= 16)'
fix.post_fix_invariant: All array indices derived from untrusted exponential Golomb-coded integers are validated to be non-negative and within array bounds.

functional_semantics.purpose: Quote special characters in IMAP strings by escaping them with backslashes and wrapping the result in double quotes.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function writes to a fixed-size buffer 'dest' with maximum capacity 'dlen'. It must ensure all writes stay within bounds.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling the function with input 'src' containing enough characters that require escaping, such that the quoted output would exceed the buffer size.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect calculation of the space reserved for framing characters.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The initial reservation 'dlen -= 2;' accounts for the opening and closing double quotes. However, if the final character written before the closing quote requires escaping (adding a backslash), the function may write the backslash and the character, then the closing quote, exceeding the buffer by one byte.
required_preconditions: The input string contains a special character (backtick, double quote, or backslash) as the last character to be processed before the loop breaks or ends.
The remaining buffer space 'dlen' is exactly 1 when that final character is encountered.

fix.strategy: Increase the initial space reservation to account for the worst-case scenario where an extra backslash might need to be written immediately before the closing quote.
changed_operations: Changed the initial reservation from 'dlen -= 2;' to 'dlen -= 3;'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: After reserving space, the loop guarantees that if there is any buffer space remaining (dlen > 0), there is always enough room to write either a single character or an escape sequence plus the character, and then the final closing quote.

functional_semantics.purpose: Read MPC (Magick Persistent Cache) image format, which stores image metadata and pixel data in a persistent cache file.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses image headers containing various properties (dimensions, colorspace, profiles, etc.) and attaches persistent pixel cache. Handles memory allocation for image structures including colormaps for pseudo-class images.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a specially crafted MPC image file with PseudoClass storage class.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Memory leak due to missing deallocation of colormap memory when image creation fails after resource allocation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When image->storage_class == PseudoClass, the function allocates memory for image->colormap using AcquireQuantumMemory. If subsequent resource acquisition (AcquireMagickResource for width/height) fails, the function throws an exception and returns without freeing the already-allocated colormap memory.
required_preconditions: Input is an MPC format image
Image has PseudoClass storage class
Width or height exceeds resource limits

fix.strategy: Move resource limit checks before critical memory allocations to ensure early failure without leaking resources.
added_guards: Added AcquireMagickResource checks for WidthResource and HeightResource before allocating colormap memory
changed_operations: Moved resource limit validation from after colormap allocation to before it
fix.post_fix_invariant: Colormap memory is only allocated after verifying that image dimensions don't exceed resource limits, preventing memory leaks when resource acquisition fails.

functional_semantics.purpose: MD5 hash transformation function used for generating sequence numbers and fragment identification values in IPv4/IPv6 implementations
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Generates predictable values that can be exploited for session hijacking or denial of service

vulnerability.triggering_action: Remote attacker sends crafted packets using predicted sequence/fragment ID values
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use of cryptographically weak algorithm for security-sensitive random value generation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: MD4-derived algorithm produces predictable output patterns
required_preconditions: System uses vulnerable kernel version
Network traffic is observable by attacker
Attacker can send packets to target

fix.strategy: Replace weak algorithm with cryptographically secure alternative
changed_operations: Algorithm replacement (not shown in this specific code change)
fix.post_fix_invariant: Sequence numbers and fragment IDs are generated using cryptographically secure methods

functional_semantics.purpose: Determine whether JavaScript execution should be allowed for a web frame based on content settings and other factors
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Controls whether inline JavaScript can run on web pages, affecting privacy and security when script blocking is enabled

vulnerability.triggering_action: Website attempts to execute inline JavaScript when script blocking is enabled
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect or insufficient content setting rule evaluation for script permissions
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function used a local content_setting_rules_ structure to check script permissions instead of querying the content settings manager
required_preconditions: Script blocking is enabled via content settings
User visits a specially crafted website

fix.strategy: Replaced direct content setting rules evaluation with a call to the content settings manager's GetSetting method
changed_operations: Replaced GetContentSettingFromRules call with content_settings_manager_->GetSetting call
fix.post_fix_invariant: Script permission decisions now consistently use the centralized content settings manager instead of potentially stale local rules

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse and packetize Xiph configuration data from RTP fmtp parameter
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Extracts a length value from input to allocate memory for base64 configuration data

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted fmtp parameter with a large length value
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Stack buffer size determined by attacker-controlled input
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Variable-length array allocation on stack using size derived from untrusted input
required_preconditions: Input contains fmtp parameter with configuration= field
Length calculation yields large value
Stack space insufficient for allocated array

fix.strategy: Replace stack allocation with heap allocation
added_guards: Memory allocation failure check
changed_operations: char b64[len + 1] → char *b64 = malloc(len + 1)
fix.post_fix_invariant: Buffer size still determined by input but allocation occurs on heap with bounds checking

functional_semantics.purpose: Allocate memory for a sequence header and append an End of Sequence (EOS) marker for muxers.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory based on a length value read from input data without checking for integer overflow in the size calculation.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted video file with a malicious length value in the sequence header.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in a size calculation leading to undersized buffer allocation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The length value 'len' is read from untrusted input (p_block->p_buffer + 5). This value is used to calculate an allocation size as 'len + sizeof(eos)' without checking if the addition overflows. If 'len' is close to UINT32_MAX, the sum can wrap around to a small value, causing malloc to allocate a buffer too small for the subsequent memcpy operations.
required_preconditions: A sequence header is being processed (p_block->p_buffer[4] == 0).
The output extra data buffer has not been allocated yet (!p_enc->fmt_out.p_extra).
The 'len' value read from the input is crafted to be large enough to cause an overflow when added to sizeof(eos).

fix.strategy: Add an overflow check before performing the size calculation for memory allocation.
added_guards: if( len > UINT32_MAX - sizeof( eos ) ) return NULL;
fix.post_fix_invariant: The sum 'len + sizeof(eos)' is guaranteed not to overflow a 32-bit unsigned integer before being passed to malloc.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse ADTS (Audio Data Transport Stream) frames from input data, extract audio payload, and forward it as packets.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses a header containing a frame_size field and a hdr_size field, then computes payload size as frame_size minus hdr_size. This computed size is used to allocate a buffer and copy payload data.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted ADTS frame where the parsed frame_size value is smaller than the parsed hdr_size value.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Arithmetic underflow/wrap-around leading to a negative size interpreted as a large unsigned value.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The calculation `size = ctx->hdr.frame_size - ctx->hdr.hdr_size` results in a negative value when frame_size < hdr_size. This negative value is stored in an unsigned integer variable (`size`), causing it to wrap to a very large positive number. This large size is then used for memory allocation and as the length argument to memcpy, causing heap overflow.
required_preconditions: The attacker can supply or influence the input ADTS data.
The parser reaches the code path where the size calculation and subsequent memcpy occur.
The parsed frame_size and hdr_size values are not validated to ensure frame_size >= hdr_size.

fix.strategy: Add an explicit validation check before using the computed size.
added_guards: A check that `ctx->hdr.frame_size` is greater than or equal to `ctx->hdr.hdr_size`.
changed_operations: Added a conditional block that logs a warning and jumps to an error handling label (`drop_byte`) if `frame_size < hdr_size`.
fix.post_fix_invariant: Before computing `size = frame_size - hdr_size`, the condition `frame_size >= hdr_size` is guaranteed to hold, preventing the underflow.

functional_semantics.purpose: Line wrapping algorithm for text layout that attempts to equalize line lengths by moving words between lines
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes glyph arrays with pointer arithmetic and boundary checks while tracking line counts

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing text with specific line wrapping patterns that cause the algorithm to miscalculate line boundaries
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Inconsistent state between line count tracking and actual line break markers during line length optimization
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When moving a line break marker during optimization, the code failed to properly update the line count when the new break position already had a linebreak flag set or was at the beginning of the text
required_preconditions: wrap_style setting is not 1
text requires line wrapping optimization
optimization attempts to move a line break to a position that already has linebreak flag or is the first glyph

fix.strategy: Maintain consistency between line count variable and actual line break markers during optimization
added_guards: Check if target position already has linebreak flag before moving break
Check if target position is at text beginning before moving break
changed_operations: Decrement line count when moving break to position with existing linebreak
Skip setting linebreak flag when target is first glyph
fix.post_fix_invariant: Line count always matches actual number of line breaks in glyph array

functional_semantics.purpose: Concatenates tensors along a specified dimension
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Performs tensor concatenation without validating input tensor rank and dimension bounds

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling ParallelConcat operation with specific input tensors
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of input tensor properties
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The operation did not validate that the input tensor has rank ≥1 and that its 0th dimension size exceeds the concatenation location index

Input tensor's 0th dimension size ≤ concatenation location index

added_guards: Check that input tensor rank ≥1
Check that 0th dimension size > concatenation location index

functional_semantics.purpose: Translate encoded coordinate values using fixed-point arithmetic
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Performs bit shifting operations based on nb_bits parameter

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling function with nb_bits = 0
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow/wraparound
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Right shift by (nb_bits-1) where nb_bits=0 causes undefined behavior due to shift by -1

Function called with nb_bits=0

functional_semantics.purpose: Set diagonal values of a matrix or batch of matrices, with support for specifying diagonal offsets.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates input tensor shapes and accesses elements by index without checking if the tensor is empty.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Passing an empty tensor as the diagonal index parameter.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Null pointer dereference due to unchecked empty tensor access.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code validated that the diagonal index tensor was a scalar or vector but did not check if it had zero elements. Accessing the first element via flat<int32>()(0) on an empty tensor causes undefined behavior.
required_preconditions: Diagonal index tensor is empty (NumElements() == 0)
Diagonal index tensor passes shape validation (scalar or vector)

fix.post_fix_invariant: Diagonal index tensor must be non-empty when accessed by index.

functional_semantics.purpose: Convert axis indices (including negative values) to valid positive indices within tensor dimension bounds, while deduplicating results.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates that converted indices fall within the valid range [0, num_dims-1] after adjusting negative indices.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Passing an axis index that, after negative adjustment, remains outside valid tensor dimension bounds.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing runtime validation of array index bounds in production builds.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Bounds check was only performed via DCHECK macro (debug assertion), which compiles out in release builds, allowing out-of-bounds indices to propagate.
required_preconditions: Debug assertions disabled (release build)
Caller provides axis index that resolves to value <0 or >=num_dims

fix.strategy: Add explicit runtime bounds check that executes in all build configurations.
added_guards: Bounds check: if (current < 0 || current >= num_dims) return false
changed_operations: Function now returns false on invalid index instead of proceeding
fix.post_fix_invariant: Function guarantees returned indices are within [0, num_dims-1] or returns failure.

functional_semantics.purpose: Check if the APIC (Advanced Programmable Interrupt Controller) has pending events for a virtual CPU
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Directly accesses the APIC structure pointer without validating its existence

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode PPM/PGM/PBM image data into an OpenCV matrix

functional_semantics.purpose: Create a temporary mount point directory for a device.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Creates a directory at a predictable path derived from system temporary or runtime locations.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Creating a log file at a fixed path in /tmp as root.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insecure use of predictable temporary file path.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Using a fixed path in a world-writable directory (/tmp) without proper safety checks, allowing symlink attacks.

Attacker can create symlinks in /tmp

Changed default fallback from "/tmp" to "/run/user/0"

functional_semantics.purpose: System boot repair tool that mounts partitions, creates temporary working directories, and executes repair scripts.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Creates and writes to a log file at a fixed path while running with elevated privileges.

vulnerability.abstract_cause: Privileged process follows symbolic links when writing to a fixed temporary file path.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The application used a hardcoded path (/tmp/.deepin-clone.log) in a world-writable directory (/tmp) without checking if the path was a symbolic link, allowing symlink attacks.
required_preconditions: Application runs with elevated privileges
World-writable temporary directory exists
Attacker can predict or influence the fixed file path

fix.strategy: Move temporary files from world-writable directory to protected application-specific directory.
changed_operations: Changed temporary directory from /tmp/.deepin-clone to /var/cache/deepin-clone
fix.post_fix_invariant: Temporary files are created in a directory not writable by unprivileged users.

functional_semantics.purpose: The function retrieves partition size information by executing external commands and parsing their output.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function writes a log file at a fixed path when executing a partclone command for unmounted partitions.

vulnerability.triggering_action: An unprivileged user creates a symbolic link at the fixed log file path before the function executes.

vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function uses a hardcoded log file path (/tmp/.deepin-clone.log) without checking if it's a symbolic link, allowing symlink attacks.

The fixed log file path exists or is a symbolic link created by an unprivileged user.
The program operates in GUI mode (as indicated by CVE description).

changed_operations: Changed log file path from /tmp/.deepin-clone.log to /var/log/partclone.log

The code path processes DT_HASH or DT_GNU_HASH validation.
The attacker controls the ELF file's dynamic section structure.

fix.strategy: Add explicit null-check before pointer dereference.
added_guards: Added conditional check `!x_sym ? 0 :` before computing `v_sym` in both DT_HASH and DT_GNU_HASH validation blocks.
changed_operations: Changed `unsigned const v_sym = get_te32(&dynp0[-1+ x_sym].d_val);` to `unsigned const v_sym = !x_sym ? 0 : get_te32(&dynp0[-1+ x_sym].d_val);`
Added `|| !v_sym` to the DT_HASH validation condition.
Added `|| !v_sym` to the DT_GNU_HASH validation condition.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The `v_sym` value is guaranteed to be zero when DT_SYMTAB is absent, preventing invalid pointer arithmetic. Subsequent validation logic then correctly handles the zero case.

Added `|| !v_sym` to the condition that triggers the 'bad DT_HASH' error.
Added `|| !v_sym` to the condition that triggers the 'bad DT_GNU_HASH' error.
changed_operations: Changed `unsigned const v_sym = get_te32(&dynp0[-1+ x_sym].d_val);` to `unsigned const v_sym = !x_sym ? 0 : get_te32(&dynp0[-1+ x_sym].d_val);`

vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of parsed size value before using it for memory allocation and file reading
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The size value 'l' extracted from bytes 4-7 of the WebP header was used without validation to allocate memory and determine read size, allowing integer overflow/wrap-around
required_preconditions: Malicious WebP file with manipulated size field
Size field value that causes integer issues when adding 8
Size field value that passes basic RIFF/WEBP signature checks

fix.strategy: Add bounds checking on parsed size value before use
added_guards: Check that l > 12 (minimum valid size after adding 8)
Check that l - 12 does not exceed SSIZE_MAX (when defined)
changed_operations: Added validation of 'l' before malloc and fread operations
fix.post_fix_invariant: Parsed size value is validated to be greater than minimum valid size and within reasonable bounds before being used for memory allocation

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse MP4 box string data from input stream
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory based on box size field and copies data from stream

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing MP4 file with large box size value
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer size mismatch in memory allocation calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: 64-bit box size cast to 32-bit integer in malloc argument calculation
required_preconditions: Box size value > 32-bit maximum
No validation of box size before allocation

fix.strategy: Add bounds validation before memory allocation
added_guards: Check box size >= 8
Check box size <= SIZE_MAX
fix.post_fix_invariant: Box size validated against minimum required size and maximum allocatable size

functional_semantics.purpose: Save tensor data to storage with optional slicing
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates input arguments before processing

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling the operation with invalid inputs
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Error status not causing immediate termination
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Validation function sets error status but kernel execution continues
required_preconditions: Input validation fails
No check of status after validation

fix.strategy: Explicit early return on validation failure
added_guards: Check context status after validation
changed_operations: Added conditional return
fix.post_fix_invariant: Validation failure immediately terminates kernel execution

functional_semantics.purpose: Restore tensor data from checkpoint files, supporting both V1 and V2 checkpoint formats with backward compatibility.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates input arguments before proceeding with restore operations.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling the operation with invalid inputs that cause validation to fail.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Error status set by validation function not checked before continuing execution.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Validation function uses OP_REQUIRES macro which sets error status but only returns from the validation function, not from the main Compute method. Execution continues with potentially invalid state.
required_preconditions: Input validation fails
No check of context status after validation call

fix.strategy: Explicitly check operation context status after validation and return early if validation failed.
added_guards: Explicit check of context->status().ok() after ValidateInputs call
changed_operations: Added early return when validation fails
fix.post_fix_invariant: Validation failure immediately terminates kernel execution.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process GIF LZW compressed raster data by decoding LZW codes and building a dictionary.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses externally controlled LZW code size value and uses it to calculate array indices and bit masks without validation.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a GIF image with an LZW minimum code size value exceeding the maximum supported size.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of an input value used for arithmetic that determines array bounds.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'lzw_cs' value read from the GIF file is used to calculate 'clear' (1 << lzw_cs) and later to index the 'g->codes' array. A large 'lzw_cs' causes 'clear' to exceed the array bounds, leading to a stack buffer overflow when initializing array elements.
required_preconditions: The parser receives GIF data from an untrusted source.
The GIF contains a malicious or malformed LZW minimum code size field.

fix.strategy: Add an upper bound check on the input value before using it in calculations.
added_guards: Check that 'lzw_cs' is not greater than 'gif_lzw_max_code_size'.
changed_operations: Added an early validation step that rejects the input and returns an error if the bound is exceeded.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The 'lzw_cs' value is guaranteed to be within a defined, safe maximum before any dependent calculations or array accesses occur.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process Program Association Table (PAT) data in MPEG-2 Transport Stream demuxer to create program entries and associated Program Map Table (PMT) filters.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates and registers PMT section filters for each program PID found in PAT data, storing them in a global array indexed by PID.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted MP4 file containing PAT data with duplicate or conflicting PID values.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use-after-free due to overwriting existing array entry without proper cleanup.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code unconditionally assigned 'ts->ess[pmt->pid] = (GF_M2TS_ES *)pmt' without checking if the PID slot was already occupied, potentially overwriting a previous pointer and causing the previous object to be leaked.
required_preconditions: PAT contains multiple programs with same PID value
Previous PMT filter exists for that PID
System later attempts to use the overwritten pointer

fix.strategy: Add guard condition before allocation and registration to prevent overwriting existing entries.
added_guards: Check if pid is zero (reserved)
Check if ts->ess[pid] already exists
changed_operations: Changed unconditional allocation to conditional allocation only when pid != 0 AND ts->ess[pid] is NULL
fix.post_fix_invariant: Each PID slot in ts->ess array contains at most one valid pointer, preventing overwrites.

functional_semantics.purpose: Shape inference validation for quantization operations
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates tensor shape constraints and parameter bounds before processing

vulnerability.triggering_action: Shape inference function execution with invalid axis parameter
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of parameter bounds
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'axis' parameter could be set to values that cause out-of-bounds array access during shape inference
required_preconditions: Axis parameter set to value less than -1
Shape inference function called with invalid axis

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds check for parameter values
added_guards: Axis parameter lower bound check
changed_operations: Added validation that axis >= -1
fix.post_fix_invariant: Axis parameter validated to be at least -1 before shape inference proceeds

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse Apple QuickTime file structure recursively
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads size values from file input and uses them to calculate memory offsets and control recursion depth

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a specially crafted Apple QuickTime file containing malicious size values
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in size calculation leading to infinite recursion
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The size value read from file is used in arithmetic operations without overflow checks, allowing wrap-around to smaller values that bypass loop termination conditions
required_preconditions: Malicious file with crafted size field
32-bit integer arithmetic
Recursive parsing of file structure

fix.strategy: Add overflow checks before using size values in arithmetic operations
added_guards: Check for negative size values
Check for overflow in save + size calculation
fix.post_fix_invariant: All size-based calculations are validated for overflow before use

functional_semantics.purpose: Write an image in PICT format.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates three memory buffers for internal processing. If any allocation fails, the function throws an exception but previously did not free already-allocated buffers.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A memory allocation failure for one of the three buffers (buffer, packed_scanline, or scanline) after at least one other buffer has been successfully allocated.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing cleanup of acquired resources on an error path.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function used a single conditional check to see if all three memory allocations succeeded. If any allocation failed, it would throw an exception immediately without freeing the memory pointers that had already been successfully allocated, causing a memory leak.
required_preconditions: The function attempts to allocate multiple memory blocks.
At least one, but not all, of the allocations fails.

fix.strategy: Explicitly free each successfully allocated buffer before throwing the exception on allocation failure.
added_guards: Individual NULL checks for each buffer pointer before calling RelinquishMagickMemory.
changed_operations: Replaced a single ThrowWriterException call with a block that conditionally frees each allocated buffer before throwing.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If the combined allocation check fails, all previously allocated buffers are freed before the function exits via exception.

functional_semantics.purpose: Handle file uploads from HTTP requests by writing request body content to a file in a specified directory
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Constructs file path by concatenating user-provided filename to target directory and opens file for writing

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing HTTP upload request with malicious filename parameter
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Path traversal through user-controlled filename without sanitization
vulnerability.detailed_cause: User-provided filename concatenated directly to directory path without removing directory traversal sequences
required_preconditions: Upload functionality enabled
Attacker can control filename parameter

fix.strategy: Sanitize constructed file path before use
added_guards: Path sanitization function call
changed_operations: Added remove_double_dots() on path before fopen()
fix.post_fix_invariant: File path is sanitized to prevent directory traversal before file operations

functional_semantics.purpose: Reads screenshot images from display devices on Windows using GDI32 API.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates multiple resources (device contexts, bitmaps, image objects) in a loop enumerating display devices. If an error occurs after some resources have been allocated but before they are added to the managed image list, those resources may not be properly cleaned up.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling SetImageExtent fails (returns MagickFalse) after a display device context (hDC) and image object (screen) have been created but before the image is fully initialized and added to the list.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Resource leak due to missing cleanup on an early error path.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When SetImageExtent fails, the function returns DestroyImageList(image). At that point, the 'screen' image object has been allocated via AcquireImage and its dimensions set, but it has not been appended to the 'image' list if 'image' was NULL. DestroyImageList only destroys images in the linked list starting from 'image'. Since 'screen' is not in the list, it is not destroyed. Additionally, the device context (hDC) created for the current display device is not deleted.
required_preconditions: The code is compiled for Windows (MAGICKCORE_WINGDI32_DELEGATE defined).
EnumDisplayDevices finds at least one active display device.
CreateDC succeeds for that device.
AcquireImage succeeds.
SetImageExtent fails for the allocated image object.

fix.strategy: Reorder operations to ensure the image object is added to the managed list before performing operations that can fail, guaranteeing cleanup on error.
changed_operations: Moved the 'AppendImageToList' (or assignment to 'image') to occur before the call to 'SetImageExtent'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If SetImageExtent fails, DestroyImageList(image) is called, which will destroy the 'screen' image object because it is now part of the 'image' list. The device context (hDC) leak remains but is now associated with an image that will be cleaned up.

functional_semantics.purpose: Writes an image in CALS format by creating a header and converting the image to GROUP4 format.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates intermediate resources (ImageInfo, Image) during conversion and must clean them up on all execution paths, including error paths.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an image to write it in CALS format.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Resource leak due to missing cleanup on error paths.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function `CloneImageInfo` allocates an `ImageInfo` structure (`write_info`). On two early error return paths (when `group4_image` or `group4` are NULL), this allocated `write_info` was not destroyed before returning, causing a memory leak.
required_preconditions: The function `CloneImage` returns NULL, or
The function `ImageToBlob` returns NULL.

fix.strategy: Ensure all allocated resources are cleaned up on all function exit paths.
changed_operations: Added `write_info=DestroyImageInfo(write_info);` before `(void) CloseBlob(image);` on the two early error return paths.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The `write_info` `ImageInfo` structure is destroyed on all function exit paths, whether successful or due to early errors.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse HTTP query parameters and populate a Lua table with key-value pairs after validation and decoding.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes user-supplied query strings, decodes URL-encoded values, validates parameters to exclude certain patterns (csrf), and checks if values represent file paths.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an HTTP query parameter where the value after '=' is empty (e.g., 'param=').
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation for empty parameter values before pointer arithmetic.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code performed pointer arithmetic on '_equal' (pointer to '=') without checking if the substring after '=' has content. This led to dereferencing a pointer that could be at the string's null terminator.
required_preconditions: Query string contains a parameter with an empty value (e.g., 'key=').
The parameter is not filtered out by other conditions (e.g., not 'csrf').

fix.strategy: Add a length check before processing the parameter value.
added_guards: Check that strlen(_equal) > 1 after locating '='.
changed_operations: Modified conditional to require the substring after '=' to have length > 1.
fix.post_fix_invariant: A parameter is only processed if it contains a '=' character and the substring after '=' has at least one character before the null terminator.

functional_semantics.purpose: Handles IMAP connection state transitions during initial connection setup, including authentication and encryption negotiation.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes server responses during connection establishment, including PREAUTH (pre-authenticated) responses, and decides whether to proceed with STARTTLS encryption.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Server sends a PREAUTH response during initial connection greeting.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Client proceeds with authenticated session without encryption when configured to require STARTTLS.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When the client is configured to require STARTTLS (model->m_startTls is true) and receives a PREAUTH response, the original code allowed the connection to proceed without encryption. This could lead to cleartext transmission of sensitive data (like draft/sent messages) if an attacker intercepts the PREAUTH response.
required_preconditions: Client configured to require STARTTLS
Attacker can send forged PREAUTH response (man-in-the-middle)
Client would later send sensitive data without encryption

fix.strategy: Enforce encryption requirement by rejecting PREAUTH when STARTTLS is configured.
added_guards: Check if STARTTLS is required (model->m_startTls) before processing PREAUTH
changed_operations: Added logout with error message when PREAUTH received but STARTTLS required
fix.post_fix_invariant: If client requires STARTTLS and server responds with PREAUTH, connection is terminated rather than proceeding without encryption.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse DWARF debugging information compilation unit entries from a binary buffer.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Extracts a string pointer from parsed attribute values and stores it in a database if the attribute name matches DW_AT_comp_dir.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling sdb_set with a string pointer that may be invalid or null.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of a pointer before dereferencing it.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function passes a pointer extracted from parsed data directly to sdb_set without checking if it is a valid, non-null pointer to a string.
required_preconditions: The parsed ELF file contains crafted DWARF debugging information.
The attribute value for DW_AT_comp_dir is parsed, resulting in an invalid or null string pointer.

fix.strategy: Add a guard to validate the string pointer before using it.
added_guards: A check that the pointer value exceeds 1024 before passing it to sdb_set.
changed_operations: The call to sdb_set is now conditional.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The string pointer passed to sdb_set is guaranteed to be non-null (or above a low address threshold).

functional_semantics.purpose: Process a FILECONTENTS_SIZE or FILECONTENTS_RANGE request for clipboard file data, either from an IStream or from local file descriptors.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function accesses array elements using an index (listIndex) from an untrusted network message without validating that the index is within bounds.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A remote client sends a FILECONTENTS_SIZE or FILECONTENTS_RANGE PDU with a listIndex value that exceeds the valid range of the clipboard's file descriptor or file_names arrays.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check on an array index derived from untrusted input.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function used fileContentsRequest->listIndex to directly index into clipboard->fileDescriptor[] and clipboard->file_names[] arrays in the non-stream (else) branch, without first checking if listIndex < clipboard->nFiles.
required_preconditions: The function is handling a FILECONTENTS_SIZE or FILECONTENTS_RANGE request
The bIsStreamFile flag is FALSE (i.e., the data is not being retrieved from an IStream)
The attacker-controlled listIndex is equal to or greater than clipboard->nFiles

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds checks before using the untrusted listIndex to access array elements.
added_guards: if (clipboard->nFiles <= fileContentsRequest->listIndex) goto error;
changed_operations: Added the guard before both the FILECONTENTS_SIZE and FILECONTENTS_RANGE handling blocks in the non-stream (else) branch.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The listIndex is guaranteed to be less than clipboard->nFiles before being used to index into clipboard->fileDescriptor or clipboard->file_names arrays.

functional_semantics.purpose: Compute gradient with respect to filters in a 2D convolution operation
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates output tensor based on user-provided filter dimensions, then performs buffer operations using computed sizes

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing convolution gradient computation with mismatched filter dimensions
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Inconsistent buffer size calculation leading to buffer overflow
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Code computes filter_total_size from convolution dimensions but uses allocated tensor's element count for buffer operations without validation
required_preconditions: User-provided filter_sizes tensor
Computed filter_total_size differs from allocated tensor's element count

fix.strategy: Add validation check before buffer operations
added_guards: Verify filter_total_size * dims.out_depth equals filter_backprop->NumElements()
fix.post_fix_invariant: Buffer size calculations match allocated tensor size before buffer operations

functional_semantics.purpose: Invalidate I/O bitmap permissions for a task by setting the I/O bitmap base to an invalid offset
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Controls user-space I/O port access permissions by marking the I/O bitmap as invalid

vulnerability.triggering_action: I/O bitmap invalidation
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Loss of synchronization between I/O permission bitmaps in different contexts
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Direct modification of a task's TSS I/O bitmap base without proper CPU awareness
required_preconditions: Multiple tasks with I/O permissions
I/O bitmap invalidation operations

fix.strategy: Use per-CPU write operation instead of direct structure modification
changed_operations: Replaced direct structure field assignment with this_cpu_write()
fix.post_fix_invariant: I/O bitmap invalidation targets the current CPU's TSS

functional_semantics.purpose: Handles HTTP requests for Lua scripts, parsing query parameters, cookies, and session data to prepare the Lua environment before script execution.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes HTTP GET parameters, validates CSRF tokens for certain requests, and sets up user session context from cookies.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Accessing administrative endpoints (paths containing '/admin/') without providing a valid CSRF token in the request parameters.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing mandatory CSRF token validation for administrative operations.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code validated CSRF tokens only when a 'csrf' parameter was present in the query string. Administrative endpoints could be accessed if no 'csrf' parameter was submitted, bypassing validation entirely.
required_preconditions: Request targets a URI containing '/admin/'
No 'csrf' parameter in the query string

fix.strategy: Enforce CSRF token validation for all administrative endpoints by requiring the presence of a valid 'csrf' parameter.
added_guards: Check that a CSRF token was found (csrf_found is true) for requests to '/admin/' paths
changed_operations: Added a boolean flag (csrf_found) to track if a CSRF parameter was processed
Added validation after parameter parsing to reject admin requests lacking CSRF tokens
fix.post_fix_invariant: Any request to a URI containing '/admin/' must include a valid 'csrf' parameter in the query string.

functional_semantics.purpose: Populate a lookup table from an input vector, with special handling for dithering mode
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Copies values from input vector to fixed-size output table, potentially accessing out-of-bounds indices

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling setTable with an input vector size >= 65536
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check on input size
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Loop iterations assume input vector has fewer than 65536 elements, but no validation enforces this limit
required_preconditions: Input vector size >= 65536
Dithering mode is enabled

fix.strategy: Add explicit size validation before table processing
added_guards: Check that input vector size is less than 65536
changed_operations: Added early validation with ThrowRDE
fix.post_fix_invariant: Input vector size is guaranteed to be less than TABLE_SIZE before any table accesses

functional_semantics.purpose: Perform X-Trans demosaicing interpolation on raw image data
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes image pixel arrays using precomputed offset tables, accesses memory using calculated indices, and validates input patterns

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an image with dimensions smaller than the algorithm's tile size or with malformed color pattern data
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds memory access due to unvalidated offset calculations
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'allhex' offset table contained uninitialized or invalid values that were used to index into image arrays, leading to invalid memory reads
required_preconditions: Image width or height less than TS constant
Malformed X-Trans color filter array pattern
Uninitialized allhex table values

fix.strategy: Add validation checks before using calculated offsets and initialize tables with safe defaults
added_guards: Check image dimensions against minimum tile size
Initialize allhex table with known safe values
Validate allhex table values before use
Add loop counter to prevent infinite loops
changed_operations: Added early rejection for small images
Added table initialization
Added table value validation
Added retry counter in processing loop
fix.post_fix_invariant: All offset values used for array indexing are validated to be within expected bounds before use

functional_semantics.purpose: Process raw SCSI command requests from userspace for SCSI RAID controllers
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Copies command data from userspace, processes it, and returns a reply structure to userspace

vulnerability.triggering_action: User invokes the aac_send_raw_srb ioctl with a native device request
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Uninitialized kernel stack memory disclosure to userspace
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The reply structure allocated on stack was not fully initialized before being copied to userspace
required_preconditions: CAP_SYS_ADMIN capability
Native device type
Valid command parameters

fix.strategy: Explicitly initialize the entire reply structure before populating specific fields
changed_operations: Added memset(&reply, 0, sizeof(reply)) before setting reply fields
fix.post_fix_invariant: All fields of the reply structure are explicitly initialized before being copied to userspace

functional_semantics.purpose: Send email notifications about job events to job owners or specified mail users.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Constructs and executes a command to send email using an external mail program (sendmail). The email recipient addresses are derived from user-controlled input (job attributes).

vulnerability.triggering_action: A remote attacker provides shell metacharacters in the email address value (via the -M switch to qsub).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unsanitized user input is incorporated into a shell command string that is executed via popen().
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function builds a command line for sendmail by concatenating a constant command string, a 'from' address, and a 'to' address string (mailto) using sprintf. The mailto string is constructed from user-provided data (JOB_ATR_mailuser or JOB_ATR_euser). This concatenated string is passed to popen(), which invokes a shell. If the user data contains shell metacharacters (e.g., semicolons, backticks), they are interpreted by the shell, leading to arbitrary command execution.
required_preconditions: The system is configured to send email notifications.
An attacker can submit a job and influence the email address field (e.g., via the -M switch).

fix.strategy: Replace the use of popen() (which invokes a shell) with direct execution via execv(), avoiding shell interpretation entirely. User-provided arguments are passed as separate elements in an argument vector.
added_guards: The fix does not add explicit input validation or sanitization guards. It changes the method of invocation to bypass the shell.
changed_operations: Replaced sprintf/cmdbuf construction and popen() call with construction of an argument array (sendmail_args).
Replaced popen() with a combination of pipe(), fork(), dup2(), and execv().
The email recipient string is tokenized (split on commas) and each token is passed as a separate argument in the array to execv.
fix.post_fix_invariant: User-provided email address strings are passed as literal arguments to the sendmail executable via execv, preventing shell metacharacter interpretation.

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize hardware components and allocate resources for an audio co-processor in a GPU driver.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates multiple kernel memory structures (acp_genpd, acp_cell, acp_res, i2s_pdata) and registers them with system frameworks (mfd_add_hotplug_devices, pm_genpd_add_device).

vulnerability.triggering_action: Failure of mfd_add_hotplug_devices() or pm_genpd_add_device() calls after successful memory allocations.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing cleanup of allocated resources on error paths.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function allocated multiple kernel memory structures but returned immediately on certain error conditions without freeing previously allocated resources.
required_preconditions: Caller has privileges for module loading
Memory allocation succeeds but subsequent registration fails

fix.strategy: Consolidate error handling using a goto label that frees all previously allocated resources before returning.
added_guards: failure label with cleanup of i2s_pdata, acp_res, acp_cell, and acp_genpd
changed_operations: Changed early returns to goto failure
Added initialization of i2s_pdata to NULL
Added error code assignment before goto
fix.post_fix_invariant: All allocated resources are freed before returning on any error path after the first allocation.

functional_semantics.purpose: Render print page data for Lexmark 5700M printer by processing scan lines and generating printer commands
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Dynamically buffers printer command data with potential reallocation during processing

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing crafted EPS file data that causes buffer overflow during printer command generation
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Buffer overflow in dynamic buffer reallocation logic
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The buffer_store macro reallocates buffer but fails to preserve write pointer position after reallocation, causing subsequent writes to use stale pointer
required_preconditions: Crafted input data requiring buffer expansion
Buffer expansion triggered during processing

fix.strategy: Preserve write pointer offset across buffer reallocation
changed_operations: Store pointer offset before reallocation
Restore pointer position after memory copy
Update pointer calculation to use offset
fix.post_fix_invariant: Write pointer remains valid after buffer reallocation

functional_semantics.purpose: Convert a string representation of special keys or characters to their internal form, handling escape sequences and multi-byte characters.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes input string pointers with bounds checking for special key sequences and multi-byte characters.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Reading a NUL byte from the input string.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read due to incorrect pointer advancement.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When the input character is NUL ('\0'), the pointer was always advanced by one byte, potentially reading beyond valid string boundaries.
required_preconditions: Input string contains NUL byte at position being processed
Function is called with pointer to NUL byte

fix.strategy: Conditional pointer advancement based on whether current character is NUL.
added_guards: Check for NUL character before advancing pointer
changed_operations: Changed unconditional pointer increment to conditional: *sp = str + (*str == NUL ? 0 : 1)
fix.post_fix_invariant: Pointer does not advance when encountering NUL character, preventing out-of-bounds read.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse ELF symbol tables to look up symbol names from an executable file.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads symbol names from a string table using an offset without validating that the offset is within the table's bounds.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Comparing a symbol name from the string table against a target name.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read due to missing bounds check on an index/offset.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code uses the symbol's name offset (s->st_name) to compute a pointer into the string table (strtab) and then performs string comparison operations (strcmp) without verifying that the offset is less than the string table's size (symstrsize).
required_preconditions: A malicious or malformed ELF file where a symbol entry's st_name field points outside the allocated string table region.

fix.strategy: Add bounds check before using the offset and use bounded string comparison.
added_guards: Calculate remaining size in string table: size = symstrsize - s->st_name
Use strncmp with the calculated size instead of strcmp
changed_operations: Replaced strcmp with strncmp, using the calculated remaining string table size as the length limit.
fix.post_fix_invariant: String comparisons using the symbol name pointer are limited to the remaining bytes in the string table, preventing reads beyond its allocated memory.

functional_semantics.purpose: Handles memory write operations in a virtual address space, supporting both direct RAM access and MMIO regions.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Maps guest RAM addresses to host pointers for direct memory copying operations.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling qemu_map_ram_ptr with an address offset that may exceed the RAM block boundaries.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds validation when converting guest RAM addresses to host pointers.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The qemu_map_ram_ptr function was called with addr1 without verifying it stays within the RAM block's allocated region, potentially returning a pointer outside valid memory.
required_preconditions: Guest has privileged access
Write operation targets RAM region
Address offset exceeds RAM block size

functional_semantics.purpose: Read and parse authentication keys from a configuration file, validating each key entry and loading valid keys into the system.

When pointed at a log file (which contains many error lines), it repeatedly reads its own error messages as new input lines, generating new errors, leading to an unbounded cycle.
required_preconditions: Attacker must be authenticated (have ability to configure key file path).
Target file must exist and be readable.
File must contain content that triggers parsing errors.

fix.strategy: Limit the number of errors processed during a single file parse to break the cycle.
added_guards: Added a counter (nerr) to track consecutive errors.
Added a check to break the reading loop if nerr exceeds nerr_maxlimit.
Added a conditional at the end to log a summary if total errors exceed nerr_loglimit.
changed_operations: Replaced direct msyslog calls with log_maybe(&nerr, ...) which increments the error counter.
Added final check after file close to handle cases where error limit was exceeded or many errors occurred.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The function will process at most nerr_maxlimit consecutive error-generating lines before aborting, preventing infinite self-feeding loops.

functional_semantics.purpose: Tokenize a line of assembly source code into lexical tokens for preprocessing and parsing.

vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect pointer advancement after skipping a quoted string within a %[ construct leads to reading beyond the allocated buffer.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When handling quoted strings inside %[ constructs, the code calls nasm_skip_string() to advance past the string. The original code added 1 to the returned pointer (p = nasm_skip_string(p - 1) + 1), causing p to point one character past the end of the string. If the string was at the end of the input buffer, this could result in reading beyond the buffer boundary.
required_preconditions: Input contains a %[ construct
Construct contains a quoted string (single quote, double quote, or backtick)
String parsing reaches end of input buffer

fix.strategy: Ensure pointer advancement stays within bounds by using the return value of nasm_skip_string() directly and only incrementing if not at end of string.
changed_operations: Changed pointer advancement from 'p = nasm_skip_string(p - 1) + 1' to 'p = nasm_skip_string(p - 1); if (*p) p++;'

vulnerability.detailed_cause: The minimum length check for a kerning sub-table allowed a value that was large enough to pass the check (length > 6) but too small to safely read the 8 bytes of header data (coverage, num_pairs fields) that follow. This mismatch between the check and the actual data requirement could lead to an out-of-bounds read.

A sub-table within the kern table reports a length greater than 6 but less than or equal to 14 (6 + 8).
The sub-table passes the initial coverage check, causing execution to proceed to the vulnerable header read.

fix.strategy: Strengthen the early validation check to ensure the reported sub-table length is sufficient for all subsequent mandatory header reads before those reads are attempted.
added_guards: Increased the minimum required sub-table length from 6 to 14 (6 + 8).
changed_operations: Changed the condition 'if ( length <= 6 )' to 'if ( length <= 6 + 8 )'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If a sub-table's length field passes the initial check, it is guaranteed to be large enough to accommodate the subsequent reads of the coverage and num_pairs fields (8 bytes) that occur before the next bounds check.

functional_semantics.purpose: Extract Rock Ridge alternate name (NM) entries from ISO9660 filesystem directory records and concatenate them into a filename buffer.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes NM entries by copying their name field into a destination buffer without checking for embedded null terminators within the source data.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted isofs filesystem containing an NM entry with '\0' characters embedded in the name field.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Information leak due to uninitialized kernel memory exposure.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function used strncat to copy the NM entry's name field. strncat stops copying at the first encountered null byte. If the source field contains an embedded null, bytes after that null in the kernel buffer (which could be uninitialized memory from previous kernel operations) are not overwritten in the destination buffer. Subsequent concatenations append after the current string length, leaving the uninitialized bytes in the middle of the constructed filename, which is then returned to user space.
required_preconditions: Local user access
Ability to mount a crafted ISO9660 filesystem with Rock Ridge extensions
The filesystem contains an NM entry with an embedded null character in its name field

fix.strategy: Replace concatenation with explicit length-bounded memory copy and manual null-termination, while detecting and handling embedded nulls.

changed_operations: Replaced strncat with memcpy for copying.
Added logic to adjust the copy length (len) if an embedded null is found, copying only up to that null.
Explicitly null-terminates the destination buffer after each copy operation.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The constructed filename in retname contains no uninitialized memory bytes from the kernel stack or heap between concatenated NM entry parts; embedded nulls in the source data truncate the copy for that specific entry but do not create gaps filled with uninitialized memory.

functional_semantics.purpose: Determine if an existing connection can be reused for a new request based on protocol, host, port, authentication state, and other connection properties.

vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient credential matching when reusing connections that are in a non-initial NTLM authentication state.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The connection reuse logic only enforced credential matching for HTTP+NTLM requests (wantNTLMhttp) but not for connections already in an NTLM authentication state (check->ntlm.state != NTLMSTATE_NONE). vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a dictionary word longer than MAXWLEN-1 characters.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check on depth variable before array write.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The loop condition allowed depth to increment without checking against MAXWLEN. When a word exceeded MAXWLEN-1 characters, writing word[depth] = c would overflow the word buffer, and subsequent writes to arridx[depth] and curi[depth] would overflow those buffers.
required_preconditions: Dictionary file contains word longer than MAXWLEN-1 characters
Function is called to dump words from that dictionary

fix.strategy: Add early termination check before incrementing depth.
added_guards: Check depth >= MAXWLEN - 1 before treating character as normal (non-zero) byte

The input length ('len') must be large enough that '4 * len' exceeds PY_SSIZE_T_MAX.

changed_operations: The multiplication '4*len' is now guarded by a preceding overflow check.

changed_operations: Added validation before any pointer arithmetic using Phdr offsets

functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses image dimensions and pixel data from untrusted input files without sufficient validation of data availability during pixel reading loops.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PNM image with insufficient pixel data relative to declared dimensions.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing early EOF checks during pixel-by-pixel reading loops leads to out-of-bounds memory access.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The parser reads image width/height values, allocates buffers accordingly, then enters pixel reading loops without verifying sufficient data remains in the file. When the file ends prematurely, subsequent read operations access uninitialized memory.
required_preconditions: Malformed PNM image with valid headers but insufficient pixel data
Image processed through formats '1', '2', or '3' (ASCII PNM variants)

fix.strategy: Add per-pixel EOF checks within pixel reading loops to abort processing when data is exhausted.
added_guards: EOFBlob(image) check after each PNMInteger() call in format '1', '2', and '3' processing loops
Additional EOFBlob check at end of each row iteration
changed_operations: Inserted EOF check before SetPixelGray() in format '1' and '2' loops
Inserted EOF check before SetPixelRed() in format '3' loop
Added row-level EOF checks after pixel loops
fix.post_fix_invariant: Pixel reading loops terminate immediately when file data is exhausted, preventing out-of-bounds memory access.

functional_semantics.purpose: Test function for bson_append_code_with_scope and bson_iter_codewscope functionality, including handling of malformed BSON data with zero-length code strings.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function tests parsing of BSON data containing CODEWSCOPE elements, including edge cases with malformed data that could trigger buffer over-reads during validation.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malformed BSON document containing a CODEWSCOPE element with an invalid zero-length code string.

vulnerability.detailed_cause: The bson_iter_codewscope function miscalculated the length argument passed to bson_utf8_validate, leading to a heap-based buffer over-read.
required_preconditions: Malformed BSON input with CODEWSCOPE type
Invalid string length field in code_w_s structure
Code validation path executed

fix.strategy: Refactored test code to use properly scoped variables and avoid reusing variable names, but the actual vulnerability fix occurred elsewhere (not shown in this test change).
changed_operations: Separated malformed test data declaration from usage
Renamed variables to avoid shadowing
fix.post_fix_invariant: Malformed BSON documents with zero-length code strings in CODEWSCOPE elements are properly rejected without buffer over-reads.

functional_semantics.purpose: Collect syscall information from a target task for reporting via /proc/pid/syscall interface.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Copies syscall arguments from kernel registers to a user-visible info structure.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Reading /proc/pid/syscall for a process.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Uninitialized kernel stack memory disclosure.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The syscall_get_arguments function writes directly into the info->data.args array, which may leave elements uninitialized when fewer than six arguments exist, leaking previous stack contents.
required_preconditions: Target process is in a syscall with fewer than six arguments
Attacker has read access to /proc/pid/syscall

fix.strategy: Initialize a local array before use and copy only initialized elements.
added_guards: Explicit initialization of local args array
changed_operations: Changed from direct writing to info->data.args to intermediate local buffer
fix.post_fix_invariant: All six elements of info->data.args are explicitly defined, preventing leakage of uninitialized stack memory.

functional_semantics.purpose: Perform file synchronization (mirroring) between source and target directories, including creating directories, transferring files, removing old files, and adjusting permissions.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function executes file operations (mkdir, rm, rmdir, chmod) on the local system based on remote file names and directory structures. It can recursively delete local files and directories.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A remote attacker provides malicious file/directory names during reverse mirroring.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: The program uses unsanitized remote file names directly in local file system operations.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When constructing arguments for local file operations (rm, rmdir, chmod), the code used the raw file->name without sanitizing or properly qualifying it relative to a safe base directory. This allowed a remote server to supply names like ".." or absolute paths, leading to operations outside the intended target directory.
required_preconditions: User performs reverse mirroring from an attacker-controlled FTP server.
The attacker can supply malicious file/directory names.
The DELETE flag is enabled (or other relevant operation flags).

fix.strategy: Sanitize file names by explicitly qualifying them relative to the current directory ("./") before passing them to file operation commands.
changed_operations: In TARGET_REMOVE_OLD_FIRST/TARGET_REMOVE_OLD case: Changed args->Append(file->name) to args->Append(dir_file(".", file->name)).
In TARGET_CHMOD case: Changed a->Append(file->name) to a->Append(dir_file(".", file->name)).
In SOURCE_REMOVING_SAME case: Changed args->Append(file->name) to args->Append(dir_file(".", file->name)).
fix.post_fix_invariant: File names passed to local file operation commands are explicitly anchored to the current working directory, preventing path traversal outside the intended target directory.

functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates kernel memory for user input, validates debugfs entry name, parses numeric parameters, performs power management operations, executes flood test

vulnerability.triggering_action: Writing to debugfs entry with unsupported name

changed_operations: Replaced direct return with assignment and goto to cleanup label
