functional_semantics.purpose: Parse ASN.1 UTCTIME strings from X.509 certificates into time_t values.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted certificate timestamp data without proper validation of ASN.1 structure integrity.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted X.509 certificate with malformed timestamp fields.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Memory corruption due to improper parsing of ASN.1 time strings.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function directly accessed timestr->data and timestr->length fields without validating the ASN.1 string type or checking for embedded null bytes, allowing malformed inputs to cause buffer overreads or other memory corruption.
required_preconditions: Untrusted certificate data reaches the parsing function
Certificate contains crafted notBefore or notAfter timestamps

fix.strategy: Add validation checks before parsing and use safe accessor functions.
added_guards: Check ASN1_STRING_type(timestr) == V_ASN1_UTCTIME
Verify ASN1_STRING_length(timestr) equals strlen(ASN1_STRING_data(timestr))
Use ASN1_STRING_length() instead of direct field access
changed_operations: Replaced direct timestr->data access with ASN1_STRING_data(timestr)
Replaced direct timestr->length access with ASN1_STRING_length(timestr)
fix.post_fix_invariant: The function validates ASN.1 type and string integrity before parsing timestamp components.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse X.509 certificate subject or issuer name from ASN.1-encoded data
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes a SET of RelativeDistinguishedName elements, each containing attribute type-value pairs

vulnerability.triggering_action: Parsing a malicious certificate with multiple attribute type-value pairs in a single SET
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Lack of input validation on structural constraints
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function allowed multiple attribute type-value pairs within a single SET by using a loop, violating X.509 specification that requires exactly one pair per SET
required_preconditions: Parsing a certificate with non-compliant structure
Multiple attributes packed in single SET

fix.strategy: Enforce structural constraint by removing loop and requiring exactly one attribute per SET
added_guards: Check that parser reaches SET end after processing single attribute
changed_operations: Replaced loop with single attribute processing
Added early return if extra data remains in SET
fix.post_fix_invariant: Each SET contains exactly one attribute type-value pair

functional_semantics.purpose: Handle VT (virtual terminal) ioctl commands for console mode and keyboard operations.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function processes privileged and unprivileged ioctl commands that read or modify console state, including the console mode (vc_mode).

vulnerability.triggering_action: Concurrent execution of KDGETMODE (read) and KDSETMODE (write) ioctl operations on the same virtual terminal.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Lack of synchronization (locking) around a shared data structure field accessed by both read and write operations.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The field vc->vc_mode was read in the KDGETMODE case without any lock, while the KDSETMODE case (via vt_kdsetmode) could modify it concurrently. This created a race condition.
required_preconditions: Multiple threads/processes must have access to the same virtual terminal file descriptor.
One thread must execute the KDGETMODE ioctl.
Another thread must concurrently execute the KDSETMODE ioctl.

fix.strategy: Enclose the mode-setting operation within the existing console lock to synchronize access with readers.
added_guards: console_lock()
console_unlock()
changed_operations: The KDSETMODE case now calls console_lock() before vt_kdsetmode() and console_unlock() after.
fix.post_fix_invariant: Access to vc->vc_mode during KDSETMODE operations is now serialized with respect to other console operations protected by the same lock.

functional_semantics.purpose: Reconstruct chunk offset tables from file data when the original offset table is missing or corrupted, by reading chunk headers sequentially.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads chunk headers from a stream, validates part numbers and coordinates, computes chunk sizes, and populates offset tables. Contains bounds checking for array accesses.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted EXR file with a part number equal to the size of the parts vector.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Off-by-one error in array bounds check.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The condition 'partNumber > static_cast<int>(parts.size())' allowed 'partNumber' to be equal to 'parts.size()', leading to an out-of-bounds array access when using 'parts[partNumber]'.
required_preconditions: A multipart EXR file is being processed.
The file contains a chunk where the read part number equals the total number of parts.

fix.strategy: Correct the bounds check to use greater-than-or-equal instead of strictly greater-than.
changed_operations: Changed bounds check from 'partNumber > static_cast<int>(parts.size())' to 'partNumber >= static_cast<int>(parts.size())'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The 'partNumber' index is guaranteed to be less than the size of the 'parts' vector for all array accesses.

functional_semantics.purpose: Update buffer parameters for raw MIDI input stream
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reallocates buffer when requested size differs from current size

vulnerability.triggering_action: Concurrent access to raw MIDI input parameters
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Double free due to unprotected concurrent buffer reallocation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: krealloc called without lock protection, allowing concurrent threads to free same buffer
required_preconditions: Multiple threads accessing same raw MIDI substream
Buffer size change requested

fix.strategy: Replace realloc with allocate-copy-free pattern protected by lock
added_guards: spin_lock_irq(&runtime->lock)
changed_operations: krealloc → kmalloc + kfree
fix.post_fix_invariant: Buffer pointer and size updates are atomic under lock

functional_semantics.purpose: Callback function for reading data from a network transfer into a buffer
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Copies received data into a fixed-size buffer without checking if it fits

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving more data than the buffer can hold
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check before buffer write
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function copies 'realsize' bytes into 's->orig_buf' at offset 's->buf_off' without verifying the write stays within buffer bounds
required_preconditions: Network transfer provides more data than buffer capacity
Buffer offset plus received size exceeds buffer length

fix.strategy: Add bounds check and limit copy size to remaining buffer capacity
added_guards: Check if buffer offset exceeds buffer length before copying
Limit copy size to remaining buffer space using MIN()
changed_operations: Added early return when buffer full
Reduced realsize to fit available buffer space
fix.post_fix_invariant: Buffer write never exceeds allocated buffer length

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse incoming AMQP frames from a network connection, handling protocol headers and frame bodies.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Calculates buffer size for incoming frames based on a frame size field from the network, then allocates memory and copies data into that buffer.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malicious frame header from a server where the frame size field is crafted to cause an integer overflow.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in buffer size calculation leading to undersized allocation and subsequent heap buffer overflow.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The `frame_size` value read from the network (a 32-bit unsigned integer) was used directly in the calculation `frame_size + HEADER_SIZE + FOOTER_SIZE` to compute `target_size`. If `frame_size` was large enough (close to UINT32_MAX), the addition could overflow the 32-bit integer, resulting in a small `target_size`. This undersized buffer was then allocated, but later operations (like `memcpy` and frame body processing) used the original, large `frame_size` logic, writing beyond the allocated buffer bounds.
required_preconditions: The system is connected to a malicious or compromised AMQP server.
The server sends a frame with a `frame_size` field value large enough to cause an overflow when added to HEADER_SIZE and FOOTER_SIZE.

fix.strategy: Validate the untrusted frame size value before using it in arithmetic operations to prevent integer overflow.
added_guards: A check that the parsed `frame_size` is less than INT32_MAX before calculating `target_size`.
changed_operations: The raw `frame_size` is now stored in a local variable (`uint32_t frame_size`) and validated.
The calculation `state->target_size = frame_size + HEADER_SIZE + FOOTER_SIZE` is performed only after the validation passes.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The `frame_size` used to compute `target_size` is guaranteed to be less than INT32_MAX, ensuring the addition does not overflow a signed 32-bit integer and that the allocated buffer is sufficiently large for subsequent operations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Handles incoming connection requests (connect messages) during the authentication phase of the Ceph messaging protocol version 1 (msgr1). It validates protocol version, checks required features, verifies the client's authorizer, and manages connection state transitions including handling existing connections, session resets, and races.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Enforces authentication by verifying the client's authorizer via a challenge-response mechanism for CEPHX_V2. It checks that the connecting peer supports required feature bits (e.g., MSG_AUTH for signatures) before proceeding with the connection establishment.

vulnerability.triggering_action: An attacker with network access can replay a previously captured authentication sequence (authorizer) to establish a connection without possessing the valid, current credentials.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: The authentication protocol lacked replay protection, allowing previously valid authentication material to be reused.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The protocol did not mandate the use of CEPHX_V2, which provides a challenge-response mechanism. The configuration settings (`cephx_service_require_version` and `cephx_cluster_require_version`) were not consulted to enforce the CEPHX_V2 feature requirement during the connection handshake, leaving connections potentially using the older, replay-vulnerable CEPHX_V1.
required_preconditions: The attacker has access to the cluster network to capture authentication packets.
The targeted connection uses the msgr2 protocol (as msgr1 was not affected).
The Ceph cluster is configured to use the cephx authentication protocol.

fix.strategy: Enforce the use of the replay-resistant CEPHX_V2 protocol by checking configuration-driven version requirements and mandating the corresponding feature bit during the connection handshake.
added_guards: Added checks for configuration parameters `cephx_require_version` and `cephx_cluster_require_version` (for cluster entities like OSD, MDS, MGR) and `cephx_service_require_version` (for other entities). If the required version is >=2, the code now adds `CEPH_FEATUREMASK_CEPHX_V2` to the `connection->policy.features_required` mask.
changed_operations: The feature requirement logic for CEPHX_V2, which previously only checked `cephx_service_require_version`, was expanded. It now also checks the new `cephx_require_version` and `cephx_cluster_require_version` configuration parameters and uses the correct feature mask `CEPH_FEATUREMASK_CEPHX_V2`.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If the configuration mandates cephx version 2 or higher, any successful connection establishment must have advertised and been verified to support the `CEPH_FEATUREMASK_CEPHX_V2` feature bit, ensuring the use of the challenge-response mechanism.

Path length > PATH_MAX
GIT utility execution

fix.strategy: Remove local path construction, require caller to provide pre-concatenated path
changed_operations: Eliminated sprintf call
Removed local concatpath buffer
Changed function signature to accept single path parameter
fix.post_fix_invariant: Caller must ensure concatenated path fits within system limits before invocation

functional_semantics.purpose: Add or remove a file path from the diff queue for version control operations.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Constructs a full file path by concatenating a base path and a relative path, then processes it.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling the function with a base and path combination whose concatenated length exceeds PATH_MAX.

required_preconditions: Local user control over 'base' or 'path' parameters
The sum of 'base' and 'path' string lengths exceeds PATH_MAX
The function is called via git utilities like git-diff or git-grep

fix.strategy: Shift responsibility for safe path construction to the caller.

Removed sprintf concatenation
Changed function signature: parameter 'concatpath' replaces separate 'base' and 'path' parameters
fix.post_fix_invariant: The caller must ensure the provided 'concatpath' is valid and does not exceed system path length limits.

functional_semantics.purpose: Set palette data for PNG image
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates palette length against maximum allowed based on image bit depth

vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer comparison vulnerability

changed_operations: Comparison operator operand type conversion

Message compression enabled
Attacker can craft wire protocol messages

functional_semantics.purpose: Save and clear the processor's vector/floating-point/SPE registers for a task during context switch or other operations that require giving up these resources.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function accesses and modifies hardware registers (vector, floating-point, SPE) belonging to a task. It checks which registers are currently in use by examining the task's MSR (Machine State Register) bits before performing operations.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A local user process triggers a Facility Unavailable exception while using hardware transactional memory (tbegin) and accesses vector registers.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing check for transactional memory state before reading user-controlled register state.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function `check_if_tm_restore_required(tsk)` was called after reading `tsk->thread.regs->msr`. This allowed a race condition where a process in a hardware transactional memory state could have its vector registers read and potentially corrupted with values from another process.
required_preconditions: PowerPC platform with hardware transactional memory support
Local user access
Multiple processes using vector registers
Transactional memory operation in progress

fix.strategy: Reorder operations to perform transactional memory state check before reading user-controlled register state.
changed_operations: Moved `check_if_tm_restore_required(tsk)` call earlier, before reading `tsk->thread.regs->msr`
fix.post_fix_invariant: Transactional memory state is checked and potentially handled before examining or manipulating the task's hardware register state.

functional_semantics.purpose: Configure a USB gadget device by processing user-provided configuration data.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates a buffer for configuration data, validates the structure, and registers the gadget driver. On failure, must clean up allocated resources.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Call to usb_gadget_probe_driver fails after buffer allocation.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Failure to re-acquire a lock before accessing shared data structures during error cleanup.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When usb_gadget_probe_driver returns an error, the code frees dev->buf and sets it to NULL, but does not clear other pointers (dev->config, dev->hs_config, dev->dev) that reference the same buffer. These dangling pointers could be accessed later.
required_preconditions: The function reaches the driver probe call
usb_gadget_probe_driver returns a non-zero error value
The device structure persists after the failed configuration attempt

fix.strategy: Ensure all pointers derived from the allocated buffer are nullified before freeing the buffer, and maintain lock protection during the cleanup.
added_guards: Acquiring spin_lock_irq before jumping to the fail: label in the error path
changed_operations: Replaced direct kfree(dev->buf) and dev->buf=NULL in the probe error path with a lock acquisition and jump to the consolidated fail: cleanup routine
Added explicit NULL assignments to dev->config, dev->hs_config, and dev->dev in the fail: routine before unlocking and freeing the buffer
fix.post_fix_invariant: If dev->buf is freed, all pointers (dev->config, dev->hs_config, dev->dev) referencing into that buffer are also set to NULL, and the lock is held during pointer nullification.

functional_semantics.purpose: Allocate and initialize a new image structure with specified width and height dimensions.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates that memory allocation size calculations do not overflow before performing allocations.

Width value large enough to cause overflow when multiplied by sizeof(unsigned char)

fix.strategy: Add missing integer overflow check before the vulnerable allocation calculation.
added_guards: overflow2(sizeof(unsigned char *), sx)
changed_operations: Added overflow check for width dimension before gdCalloc loop
fix.post_fix_invariant: Both width and height dimensions are checked for integer overflow before any size-dependent memory allocations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Perform a collection rename operation as part of applyOps command processing, handling UUID-based collection identification and drop target specifications.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Specially crafted applyOps invocation with a malformed target namespace.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of user-controlled namespace input.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The target namespace parameter extracted from the command BSON was not validated for proper format before being used in subsequent operations.

Ability to issue applyOps commands

fix.strategy: Add input validation for target namespace parameter.
added_guards: Validation of target namespace format using userAllowedWriteNS() function
changed_operations: Added check that target namespace follows 'database.collection' format
fix.post_fix_invariant: Target namespace must pass userAllowedWriteNS validation before being used in rename operations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse Photoshop image resource blocks from a data buffer, extracting specific metadata like resolution and merged image flags.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Iterates through a buffer using pointer arithmetic, reading structured data fields (ID, name length, count) and conditionally processing variable-length data blocks based on ID values.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malformed or crafted PSD image file containing a specific image resource block.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient validation of a calculated pointer offset before using it to bound a subsequent memory read operation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The check `if ((p+count) > (blocks+length))` prevented reading beyond the end of the buffer, but did not prevent `p+count` from wrapping around to a value less than `blocks` (i.e., an integer underflow), which could lead to a buffer over-read in later loop logic.
required_preconditions: The input `length` parameter is at least 16.
The function is processing a resource block where the calculated `p+count` results in an integer underflow (wrapping below the start address `blocks`).
The underflow passes the existing upper-bound check, allowing the loop to continue with an invalid pointer `p`.

fix.strategy: Add a lower-bound check to complement the existing upper-bound check, ensuring pointer arithmetic does not underflow.
added_guards: A check for pointer underflow: `(p+count) < blocks`.
changed_operations: Changed the conditional from `if ((p+count) > (blocks+length))` to `if (((p+count) < blocks) || ((p+count) > (blocks+length)))`.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The calculated pointer `p+count` is guaranteed to lie within the inclusive address range [`blocks`, `blocks+length`] before the switch statement uses `count` to advance `p` or read data.
