functional_semantics.purpose: Process incoming IKE packets, validate header structure and version numbers, then route to appropriate protocol handler.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses network packet headers, validates version numbers and packet structure, handles malformed packets by sending notifications or dropping them.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving an IKE packet with a small length value and either no version or an invalid major version number.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient validation of packet header structure before accessing version fields.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code attempted to read and check the major/minor version numbers from a packet buffer even when in_struct() indicated the header was malformed. This could lead to reading out-of-bounds or uninitialized memory.
required_preconditions: Packet length is smaller than IKE header size
Header parsing fails (in_struct returns false)

fix.strategy: Eliminate version checking when header parsing fails entirely, treating all malformed headers uniformly.
added_guards: Removed conditional version check after in_struct() failure
changed_operations: Replaced detailed version analysis on malformed headers with immediate drop and notification
fix.post_fix_invariant: If in_struct() fails, no version field access occurs and packet is immediately dropped.

functional_semantics.purpose: A setuid-root program that manages network interfaces for unprivileged users in LXC containers, handling creation and deletion of virtual network devices.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accepts user-supplied path arguments and opens them to access network namespaces. Performs privilege checks before allowing operations on network namespaces.

vulnerability.triggering_action: User invokes the program with the 'delete' command and provides a path argument.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unconditional opening of user-supplied paths without proper validation or safe opening semantics.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When processing the 'delete' command, the program opened the user-provided path argument with O_RDONLY, triggering actual filesystem operations. This allowed users to probe for existence of inaccessible files and trigger side effects by opening special kernel files.
required_preconditions: Program is setuid-root
User can invoke program with 'delete' command
User controls the path argument

fix.strategy: Use safe opening semantics that avoid triggering filesystem operations, then validate the opened resource before performing actual operations.
added_guards: Open with O_PATH flag to avoid actual open() operations
Verify the opened file descriptor refers to a network namespace using fhas_fs_type()
changed_operations: Changed open() call from O_RDONLY to O_PATH|O_CLOEXEC
Added filesystem type verification before using the descriptor
Re-opened the O_PATH descriptor with O_RDONLY only after validation
fix.post_fix_invariant: User-supplied paths are opened with O_PATH first to avoid side effects, then validated to ensure they refer to network namespaces before any privileged operations occur.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process metadata from a tar archive entry in PHP's phar extension
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory based on an untrusted size field (uncompressed_filesize) from a tar file to read metadata

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted tar file containing a metadata entry with a malicious uncompressed_filesize value
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in memory allocation size calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Using emalloc with direct addition of 1 to entry->uncompressed_filesize could overflow when the size is near SIZE_MAX, causing undersized buffer allocation
required_preconditions: Untrusted tar file input
uncompressed_filesize value close to maximum size_t value

fix.strategy: Replace unsafe direct allocation with safe allocation function that checks for integer overflow
changed_operations: Replaced emalloc(entry->uncompressed_filesize + 1) with safe_emalloc(1, entry->uncompressed_filesize, 1)
fix.post_fix_invariant: Memory allocation size calculation is protected against integer overflow

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse and load a text-based image format (TXT) containing pixel data with coordinates and color values.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads numeric values from untrusted input file and converts them to pixel components using arithmetic operations and type casting.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted TXT image file containing negative or extremely large floating-point color values.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow/wrap-around during conversion from floating-point to unsigned integer type.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function converts double values to QuantumAny (unsigned integer type) via ScaleAnyToQuantum without validating that the input values are non-negative. Negative inputs can wrap to large unsigned values, causing undefined behavior.
required_preconditions: Untrusted input file
File contains negative color values
Program uses affected ImageMagick version

fix.strategy: Clamp input values to prevent negative numbers from being converted to unsigned types.
added_guards: MagickMax(red+0.5,0.0)
MagickMax(green+0.5,0.0)
MagickMax(blue+0.5,0.0)
MagickMax(black+0.5,0.0)
MagickMax(alpha+0.5,0.0)
changed_operations: Replaced direct (red+0.5) with MagickMax(red+0.5,0.0) before casting to QuantumAny
fix.post_fix_invariant: All color component values passed to ScaleAnyToQuantum are guaranteed to be non-negative.

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode IRC color codes in a string, optionally preserving color formatting information.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted input containing IRC color codes and builds an output string dynamically.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing crafted IRC color codes that cause excessive output growth.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Heap buffer overflow due to insufficient output buffer allocation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The initial buffer allocation based on (2 * input length + 1) could be insufficient when color decoding expands the output beyond that bound. The code used strcat to append strings without checking remaining buffer space.
required_preconditions: keep_colors parameter is true
Input contains sequences that expand significantly when decoded

fix.strategy: Dynamic buffer resizing when output approaches capacity.
added_guards: Minimum initial buffer size check
Output position tracking
Buffer reallocation when needed
changed_operations: Replaced strcat with buffer-aware memcpy
Added reallocation logic when output exceeds current capacity
fix.post_fix_invariant: Output buffer is always large enough for current decoded content.

functional_semantics.purpose: Provide a buffer for XML parsing, resizing it if insufficient space exists for requested length
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accepts a length parameter and attempts to allocate buffer space accordingly, with potential integer overflow during size calculations

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling XML_GetBuffer with a large len value
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in buffer size calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The calculation 'len + (int)(bufferEnd - bufferPtr)' could overflow when len is large, leading to negative neededSize that passes subsequent checks
required_preconditions: Large len parameter provided
Current buffer space insufficient for requested len

fix.strategy: Add explicit integer overflow checks before using calculated sizes
added_guards: Check for negative len parameter
Check for negative neededSize after calculation
Check for bufferSize overflow during doubling loop
changed_operations: Added early return for negative len
Added overflow check after neededSize calculation
Modified bufferSize doubling loop to check for overflow
fix.post_fix_invariant: All size calculations are checked for overflow before allocation attempts

functional_semantics.purpose: Build a PHAR archive from an iterator, adding files from the filesystem or streams to the archive.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function copies file contents into the archive but originally did not preserve the source file's permissions (mode bits).

vulnerability.triggering_action: Creating a PHAR archive using PharData::buildFromIterator() with files that have restrictive permissions.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Loss of security metadata during archival.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When adding a file from the filesystem to the archive, the function copied only the file content, discarding the source file's permission bits. The archive entry was created with default permissions (0666) regardless of the original file's mode.
required_preconditions: The function is called to build a PHAR archive from an iterator.
The iterator yields files from the filesystem (not streams).
The source files have permissions more restrictive than 0666.

fix.strategy: Preserve the source file's permission bits by reading them from the filesystem and storing them in the archive entry's metadata.
added_guards: Added a call to php_stream_stat() on the opened source file stream to retrieve its mode (st_mode).
On success, the mode bits (masked by PHAR_ENT_PERM_MASK) are assigned to the internal file's flags.
On failure (e.g., stat fails), a fallback logic adjusts the default flags by the current umask (non-Windows only).
changed_operations: After copying the file content, the code now reads the source file's stat information.
The retrieved mode bits are stored in data->internal_file->flags.
fix.post_fix_invariant: When a file is added from the filesystem to a PHAR archive via this function, the archive entry's permission flags reflect the original file's permissions (masked appropriately), not a default value.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process client request to set keyboard mapping (XkbSetMap)
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates and applies keyboard mapping data from client to multiple devices

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing XkbSetMap request with insufficient length validation
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds memory access
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Missing validation of request length before processing keyboard mapping data
required_preconditions: Client has Xkb initialized
Client has device access permissions
Malformed XkbSetMap request

fix.strategy: Add explicit length check before processing request data
added_guards: _XkbSetMapCheckLength(stuff) call
changed_operations: Added length validation step before pointer arithmetic
fix.post_fix_invariant: Request length validated before accessing variable-length data

functional_semantics.purpose: Set the hostname for SSL/TLS context, typically for Server Name Indication (SNI) extension.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates heap memory based on hostname length and copies hostname string into allocated buffer.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Remote SSL server sends a long hostname in Server Name Indication (SNI) extension.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing length validation before memory allocation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function allocated heap buffer sized exactly to hostname length + 1, but downstream code (not shown in record) uses this buffer with insufficient capacity.
required_preconditions: Client connects to malicious SSL server
Server sends SNI extension with long hostname

fix.strategy: Add length check before allocation to enforce maximum allowed hostname length.
added_guards: Check if hostname_len exceeds SSL_MAX_HOST_NAME_LEN
fix.post_fix_invariant: Hostname length is bounded by SSL_MAX_HOST_NAME_LEN before any allocation or copy operation.

functional_semantics.purpose: Convert classic BPF (cBPF) bytecode to extended BPF (eBPF) instructions.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The conversion process expands certain cBPF instructions into multiple eBPF instructions, which can change the relative offsets of jump targets. The function calculates jump offsets based on the expanded instruction sequence positions.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A cBPF program containing a long jump instruction (BPF_JMP | BPF_JA) that jumps over a sequence of instructions which, when expanded into eBPF, require substantial expansion (e.g., one cBPF instruction expands to multiple eBPF instructions).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in jump offset calculation due to insufficient validation of the calculated offset.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The macro BPF_EMIT_JMP calculated the jump offset as `addrs[target] - addrs[i] - 1` and then adjusted it for the position within the current temporary instruction block (`insn - tmp_insns`). The resulting offset was directly assigned to the 16-bit signed `insn->off` field without checking if it fit within the valid range for a signed 16-bit immediate offset (S16_MIN to S16_MAX). An overflowed offset could lead to out-of-bounds jumps or misinterpretation of the program.
required_preconditions: A cBPF program is being converted to eBPF.
The program contains a long jump instruction.
The jump skips over a region of code where, during conversion, one or more cBPF instructions expand into several eBPF instructions.
The expansion causes the calculated PC-relative offset between the jump instruction and its target to exceed the range of a signed 16-bit integer.

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds checking for the calculated jump offset before assigning it to the instruction field.
added_guards: In the BPF_EMIT_JMP macro, after calculating the provisional offset (`off`), check if it is less than S16_MIN or greater than S16_MAX. If so, goto an error label (`err`).
changed_operations: The BPF_EMIT_JMP macro was modified to: 1) Declare constants `off_min` and `off_max` as S16_MIN and S16_MAX. 2) Store the calculated offset in a signed 32-bit variable (`s32 off`). 3) Perform the bounds check. 4) Only assign `insn->off = off` if the check passes.
fix.post_fix_invariant: All jump offsets (`insn->off`) generated during cBPF to eBPF conversion are guaranteed to be within the valid signed 16-bit range required by the eBPF instruction format.

functional_semantics.purpose: Adds a value to an EXIF image information structure, handling different data formats (strings, bytes, numeric types).
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes externally supplied length and value buffer parameters without validating that the declared length matches the actual available buffer size.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a file with EXIF data where the declared length field for a value exceeds the actual available data buffer size.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read due to missing bounds check between a declared length parameter and the actual buffer size.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function used the 'length' parameter to control memory reads from the 'value' buffer but did not have the buffer's actual size. This allowed reading past the allocated buffer when 'length' was larger than the buffer.
required_preconditions: Attacker-controlled or malformed EXIF data
A 'length' field value larger than the actual data buffer
Processing of a data format that triggers the vulnerable read path

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds checking by providing the actual buffer size and validating the declared length against it.
added_guards: Added 'value_len' parameter to pass the actual buffer size
Check 'length > value_len' for string/byte/undefined formats and set value to NULL if violated
For numeric array formats, compute remaining bytes per iteration and break if insufficient
changed_operations: Added parameter to function signature
Added length validation before buffer operations
Added loop iteration guard based on remaining buffer size
fix.post_fix_invariant: The function will not read beyond 'value_len' bytes from the 'value' buffer, regardless of the declared 'length' parameter.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process USB/IP command submission packets to allocate and submit USB request blocks (URBs) for USB over IP communication.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates kernel memory for URB transfer buffers based on a length value extracted from an untrusted network packet.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving a specially crafted USB over IP packet containing a CMD_SUBMIT command.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unbounded memory allocation controlled by an untrusted input.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'transfer_buffer_length' field from the network packet was used directly for a kernel memory allocation ('kzalloc') without validation against a reasonable upper bound.
required_preconditions: The system has the USB/IP functionality enabled.
An attacker can send USB/IP packets to the target.

fix.strategy: Add a bounds check on the untrusted length field before allocation.
added_guards: A check ensuring 'transfer_buffer_length' is less than or equal to INT_MAX.
changed_operations: The condition for allocating the transfer buffer was changed from 'transfer_buffer_length > 0' to 'transfer_buffer_length > 0 && transfer_buffer_length <= INT_MAX'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The 'transfer_buffer_length' used for kernel memory allocation is constrained to a maximum value of INT_MAX.

functional_semantics.purpose: Generate a password element (point on elliptic curve) for EAP-pwd authentication using hunting-and-pecking method
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Iteratively searches for valid curve point by incrementing counter; failure leaks information about password

vulnerability.triggering_action: EAP-pwd handshake execution
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Information leakage through search failure side channel
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Limited iteration count (10) causes statistically predictable failures, revealing whether candidate points satisfy curve equation
required_preconditions: EAP-pwd protocol enabled
Elliptic curve group selected
Valid authentication attempt

fix.strategy: Increase search space to reduce failure probability
changed_operations: Increased maximum iteration count from 10 to 100
fix.post_fix_invariant: Probability of search failure reduced from ~1/2048 to negligible level

functional_semantics.purpose: Write image data to a persistent cache file (MPC format), including metadata, profiles, and pixel data.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory for a colormap when the image storage class is PseudoClass. If an unsupported depth is encountered, the function throws an exception but previously leaked the allocated colormap memory.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an image with PseudoClass storage class and an unsupported depth value (not 8, 16, or 32).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Memory leak due to missing resource cleanup on an error path.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: In the default case of a switch statement handling unsupported depth values, the function threw an exception without first freeing the previously allocated colormap buffer.
required_preconditions: Image storage class is PseudoClass.
Image depth is not 8, 16, or 32 bits per channel.

fix.strategy: Ensure resource cleanup before error propagation.
changed_operations: In the default case of the depth switch, the colormap is freed before throwing the exception.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The colormap buffer is freed in all code paths before the function returns or throws an exception.

functional_semantics.purpose: Clone file data ranges between inodes in the Btrfs filesystem, handling different extent types (regular, preallocated, inline).
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: When cloning compressed inline extents, the function reads the entire extent item into a buffer before processing. For compressed inline extents, the buffer contains compressed data, but the function may copy only a portion of the buffer (adjusted by skip/trim) without decompressing it first, potentially exposing pre-truncation data.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A local user performs a clone action on a file containing a compressed inline extent.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Information exposure due to improper handling of compressed data during partial cloning.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function clones compressed inline extents by reading the compressed data buffer and then adjusting the copy range (skip/trim) without decompressing. This can result in copying a fragment of the compressed byte stream that, when later decompressed, reveals data from the original uncompressed content that should have been truncated or excluded.
required_preconditions: The source file contains a compressed inline extent.
The clone operation targets a subrange of the extent (partial clone).
The user has read access to the source file.

fix.strategy: Extract the inline extent cloning logic for compressed data into a separate helper function that properly handles decompression and range extraction.
changed_operations: Replaced inline handling of BTRFS_FILE_EXTENT_INLINE type with a call to clone_copy_inline_extent().
fix.post_fix_invariant: When cloning a subrange of a compressed inline extent, the data is properly decompressed before range extraction, ensuring only the intended uncompressed data is copied.

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode a character code point into a numerical digit value for Punycode processing.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Performs arithmetic subtraction on input character code points and returns a numerical value. The return value is used in further calculations.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a specially crafted character code point that causes integer overflow during subtraction.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in arithmetic operation due to insufficient type constraints.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function accepts a wide integer type (punycode_uint) as input and performs subtraction operations without checking if the result would overflow when stored in the return type.
required_preconditions: Input character code point value is large enough to cause overflow when subtracting 48, 65, or 97.
The overflowed result is used in subsequent calculations that depend on valid numerical ranges.

fix.strategy: Narrow the input parameter type and explicitly cast the result to ensure proper unsigned return type.
changed_operations: Changed input parameter type from punycode_uint to int
Added explicit unsigned cast to the entire conditional expression result
fix.post_fix_invariant: The return value is explicitly cast to unsigned, preventing integer overflow in the return value while maintaining the same arithmetic logic.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse DMG disk image format metadata to locate and track data chunks for decompression.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates buffers based on maximum compressed chunk length and maximum sectors per chunk values read from the image file.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malicious DMG image file containing crafted chunk metadata.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Lack of validation for chunk length and sector count values read from the file before using them to allocate memory.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The values s->lengths[i] and s->sectorcounts[i] are read from the file and used to calculate allocation sizes without checking if they are within reasonable/safe bounds.
required_preconditions: Local user can supply a DMG image file
The file is processed by QEMU's DMG block driver

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds checks for chunk length and sector count values against defined maximum constants before using them.
added_guards: Check s->sectorcounts[i] > DMG_SECTORCOUNTS_MAX
Check s->lengths[i] > DMG_LENGTHS_MAX
changed_operations: Added validation after reading s->sectorcounts[i]
Added validation after reading s->lengths[i]
fix.post_fix_invariant: Chunk length and sector count values are bounded by DMG_LENGTHS_MAX and DMG_SECTORCOUNTS_MAX respectively before being used for memory allocation calculations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Extract a file entry from a PHAR archive to a destination directory on the filesystem.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function constructs a full destination path by concatenating a user-controlled destination directory ('dest') with a filename derived from an archive entry. It then creates directories and writes file contents to this constructed path.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Extracting a PHAR archive entry where the function fails to properly free a dynamically allocated buffer ('new_state.cwd') in one specific error path.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use-After-Free (CWE-416). A memory buffer is incorrectly freed using 'free()' instead of the matching allocator's 'efree()', leading to mismatched memory management.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: In the error handling block for a failed 'php_stream_mkdir' operation, the code calls 'free(new_state.cwd)' instead of 'efree(new_state.cwd)'. Since 'new_state.cwd' was allocated with 'emalloc', this creates a heap corruption vulnerability.
required_preconditions: The 'phar_extract_file' function is invoked.
The target directory for the extracted file does not exist.
Creating this directory via 'php_stream_mkdir' fails.
The function enters the error handling path for the failed directory creation.

fix.strategy: Correct the memory deallocation function to match the allocation function.
changed_operations: Replaced 'free(new_state.cwd)' with 'efree(new_state.cwd)' in two locations within the 'php_stream_mkdir' failure blocks.
fix.post_fix_invariant: Memory allocated with 'emalloc' is always freed with 'efree', maintaining consistency in the PHP runtime's memory management scheme.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse and validate a JSON Web Token (JWT) by checking its structure, decoding components, and verifying the HMAC signature.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Compares a computed HMAC signature against a provided signature to authenticate the token.

vulnerability.triggering_action: An attacker submits a JWT with a crafted signature for validation.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: The comparison of secret values leaks information through timing differences.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The standard string equality operator (`==`) performs a short-circuiting, non-constant-time comparison, allowing an attacker to infer the correct HMAC value by measuring the time taken for the validation to fail.
required_preconditions: The system uses JWT for authentication.
An attacker can repeatedly submit tokens for validation and measure response times.

fix.strategy: Replace the vulnerable string comparison with a constant-time comparison function.
changed_operations: Replaced `hmac.get() == signature.get()` with `constantTimeEquals(hmac.get(), signature.get())`.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The signature validation step's execution time does not depend on the content of the signatures being compared.

functional_semantics.purpose: Implements the saxon:line-number() XPath extension function to retrieve line numbers from XML nodes.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes node-set arguments to find a specific node, then extracts its line number. Handles namespace nodes specially by dereferencing to their owner element.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling saxon:line-number() with a node-set containing namespace nodes.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of node type before dereferencing.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function passed namespace nodes directly to xmlGetLineNo() without checking if they were valid for line number retrieval. Namespace nodes require special handling to find their owner element.
required_preconditions: Function receives a node-set argument
Node-set contains at least one namespace node
Namespace node is selected as the 'cur' node after node comparison logic

fix.strategy: Add explicit handling for namespace nodes by extracting their owner element before line number retrieval.
added_guards: Check if cur->type == XML_NAMESPACE_DECL
Validate that dereferenced owner element is not NULL and is an XML_ELEMENT_NODE
changed_operations: Moved xmlXPathFreeObject() call to end of function to ensure proper cleanup in all paths
Added intermediate lineNo variable with default value -1
Added NULL check for cur before calling xmlGetLineNo()
fix.post_fix_invariant: Namespace nodes are dereferenced to their owner elements before line number retrieval, and all code paths properly free the xmlXPathObject.

functional_semantics.purpose: Format and write access log entries according to a configurable format string containing placeholders for request metadata.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function constructs a log line by parsing a format string, expanding placeholders with data from the current request, and writing the result to a log file descriptor. It uses a fixed-size stack buffer (FPM_LOG_BUFFER) for the constructed log line.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a log format string where the expansion of a placeholder (e.g., %r for request URI) results in a string that, when added to the output buffer, would exceed the buffer's capacity.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect interpretation of the snprintf return value leads to an out-of-bounds buffer write.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function uses snprintf to write placeholder expansions into the buffer, passing the remaining buffer space (FPM_LOG_BUFFER - len) as the size limit. snprintf returns the number of characters that would have been written if the buffer were large enough, not the number actually written. The code adds this return value (len2) directly to the buffer pointer (b) and length counter (len) without checking if the write was truncated. This can cause len to exceed FPM_LOG_BUFFER, leading to subsequent writes (like the newline) occurring outside the buffer bounds.
required_preconditions: A custom log format is configured that includes placeholders for user-controlled data (e.g., request URI).
The expanded data for a placeholder is long enough that its snprintf output would exceed the remaining buffer space.

fix.strategy: Add a guard after each snprintf call to ensure the total length does not exceed the buffer capacity, truncating the log line if necessary.
added_guards: A check (if (len >= FPM_LOG_BUFFER)) after updating len and b, which breaks the loop and truncates the log line if the buffer is full.
changed_operations: The snprintf calls themselves are unchanged; the fix adds a length check after the pointer/length update following each snprintf.
fix.post_fix_invariant: After processing each log format token, the total accumulated length (len) is guaranteed not to exceed FPM_LOG_BUFFER. If adding the latest expansion would exceed the limit, the loop terminates and the log line is truncated.

functional_semantics.purpose: Sanitize filenames extracted from archives by removing directory traversal sequences
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes filenames from archive entries to prevent path traversal attacks during extraction

vulnerability.triggering_action: Extracting a TAR archive containing a filename with a single '../' traversal sequence
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incomplete sanitization of path traversal sequences
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function only tracked the position after '../' sequences but didn't reject them, allowing a single '../' to bypass protection
required_preconditions: Archive contains a filename with '../'
Extraction overwrites existing files

fix.strategy: Reject rather than track traversal sequences
added_guards: Return NULL when '../' sequence is detected
changed_operations: Changed prefix_len assignment to early return with NULL
fix.post_fix_invariant: Any filename containing '../' is rejected entirely

functional_semantics.purpose: Configure libarchive extraction flags for archive operations
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Controls security restrictions during archive extraction

vulnerability.triggering_action: Extracting a crafted TAR archive containing symlinks
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient symlink security restrictions during archive extraction
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Missing ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS flag allowed symlinks to target locations outside extraction directory
required_preconditions: Archive contains symlinks
User extracts archive
Archive is processed by affected version

fix.strategy: Add explicit symlink security flag to extraction configuration
added_guards: ARCHIVE_EXTRACT_SECURE_SYMLINKS
changed_operations: Replaced configurable flags with fixed secure defaults
fix.post_fix_invariant: Extraction always applies symlink security restrictions

functional_semantics.purpose: Set value at specified index in doubly linked list
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Frees memory for invalid index before throwing exception

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling offsetSet with out-of-range index
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Premature resource cleanup during error handling
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Double free occurs when zval_ptr_dtor(value) is called before throwing exception for invalid index, and caller may also free the same value
required_preconditions: Invalid index provided
Value requires reference counting

fix.strategy: Remove premature cleanup during error path
changed_operations: Removed zval_ptr_dtor(value) call before throwing out-of-range exception
fix.post_fix_invariant: Value reference count unchanged when exception thrown for invalid index

functional_semantics.purpose: Read SCSI command data into a command FIFO buffer from either DMA or non-DMA sources
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function transfers data into a fixed-size command FIFO without checking if there is sufficient capacity before pushing data

vulnerability.triggering_action: A privileged guest user triggers SCSI command transfer that exceeds the command FIFO capacity
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check when writing to fixed-size buffer
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function pushes data into cmdfifo without verifying the available space, potentially causing buffer overflow
required_preconditions: DMA or non-DMA SCSI command transfer is initiated
Transfer size exceeds available space in cmdfifo

fix.strategy: Add capacity check before pushing data to prevent overflow
added_guards: Check available space in cmdfifo before push operation
Limit transfer size to available capacity
changed_operations: Added MIN(fifo8_num_free(&s->cmdfifo), dmalen) before DMA push
Added MIN(fifo8_num_free(&s->cmdfifo), n) before non-DMA push
fix.post_fix_invariant: Data pushed to cmdfifo never exceeds its available capacity

functional_semantics.purpose: LZW decompression algorithm for GIF images
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes compressed data stream, builds decompression table, outputs decompressed bytes

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted compressed stream containing code words absent from decompression table
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check on stack pointer during decompression
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When encountering invalid code words (code >= max_code), the algorithm pushes values onto stack without checking stack capacity
required_preconditions: Input contains malicious LZW codes
Decompression table incomplete for encountered codes

fix.strategy: Add bounds checking before all stack push operations
added_guards: sp < &(stack[STACK_SIZE]) before *sp++ operations
changed_operations: Added stack overflow check for code == max_code case
Added stack overflow check in while (code >= clear_code) loop
Added stack overflow check before final *sp++ assignment
fix.post_fix_invariant: Stack pointer never exceeds allocated stack array bounds

functional_semantics.purpose: Process incoming DNS messages and generate appropriate responses
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: DNS server processes incoming packets and may generate reply packets

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving a DNS packet with the QR (query/response) field set to indicate it's a response
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of packet header field
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The server did not check whether incoming DNS packets were marked as responses before processing them and potentially generating replies
required_preconditions: Server receives a forged DNS response packet
Server processes the packet

fix.strategy: Add validation to reject packets that are already marked as responses
added_guards: Check DNS_FLAG_REPLY bit in incoming packet's operation field
changed_operations: Added early return with error when packet has reply flag set
fix.post_fix_invariant: Server will not process or respond to packets that are already marked as DNS responses

functional_semantics.purpose: Process privileged commands from a communication channel in a privilege separation architecture
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads commands from a file descriptor, validates them, and performs privileged operations on network interfaces

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving a partial/truncated command message from the communication channel
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incomplete message handling allows continued execution with corrupted state
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When readn() returns fewer bytes than sizeof(cmd), the code continues the loop without proper termination, potentially processing uninitialized or partially initialized command data
required_preconditions: Privilege separation mechanism is active
Communication channel can deliver partial messages
Daemon is running with elevated privileges

fix.strategy: Terminate the privilege-separated process when receiving incomplete messages
added_guards: Check for short reads and exit the function
changed_operations: Replaced 'continue' with 'return' when ret != sizeof(cmd)
fix.post_fix_invariant: The function either processes a complete command or terminates when communication is corrupted

functional_semantics.purpose: Encode image pixel data into a specific binary format for Cisco IP Phone images, packing 4 pixels into a byte with 2 bits per pixel.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes image pixel data sequentially, reading pixel values using pointer arithmetic with offsets based on pixel index and channel count.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an image where the number of columns is not a multiple of 4, during the final incomplete block of pixels.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read due to incorrect pointer offset calculation when handling trailing pixels.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The original code used a fixed index 'i' (equal to image->columns % 4) to compute pointer offsets via MagickMin(i,3), MagickMin(i,2), etc. This caused the same offset to be reused for multiple pixel components, leading to reads beyond the allocated pixel buffer when i was less than the component index being accessed.
required_preconditions: Image with width not divisible by 4
Image data buffer with insufficient trailing padding

fix.strategy: Replaced the monolithic offset calculation with a loop that processes each remaining pixel individually, accumulating bits into the byte correctly.
changed_operations: Replaced single-byte calculation using MagickMin with iterative per-pixel processing
Introduced loop variable 'x' to track current column position
fix.post_fix_invariant: Each pixel component is accessed exactly once, and pointer offsets are computed based on the actual pixel position relative to the start of the row.

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize a UNIX domain socket (server or client) using a provided path string.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function accepts a path argument, validates its length, copies it into a socket address structure, and uses it for socket operations (bind or connect).

vulnerability.triggering_action: Passing a path string containing an embedded null character ('\0') to UNIXServer.open or UNIXSocket.open.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: The path argument was not validated for the presence of null characters before being used in socket system calls.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function used `FilePathValue` to convert the path argument, which does not check for or reject null bytes within the string. The subsequent `memcpy` copied the full length of the Ruby string, including any embedded nulls, into the `sockaddr.sun_path` buffer. This could result in the socket being bound or connected to a different filesystem path than intended by the caller.
required_preconditions: An attacker can control or influence the path string passed to the vulnerable socket open methods.
The string contains an embedded null character followed by additional characters.

fix.strategy: Replace the generic path value conversion with a dedicated function that validates the string for null bytes.
added_guards: Validation that the path string does not contain null characters.
changed_operations: Replaced `FilePathValue(path);` with `path = unixsock_path_value(path);`.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The path string used for the socket address is guaranteed to contain no null characters before the terminating null added by the socket API.

functional_semantics.purpose: Add encrypted pre-authentication data (enc-padata) to KDC responses for specific use cases like referrals and FAST negotiation.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function processes encrypted pre-authentication data in Kerberos KDC responses, which can be triggered by client requests.

vulnerability.triggering_action: An attacker makes an S4U2Self request after obtaining a krbtgt ticket using an older encryption type (single-DES, triple-DES, or RC4).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: A reachable assertion that can be triggered by an attacker under specific conditions.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The assertion 'assert(reply_encpart->enc_padata == NULL)' could be reached and fail when processing certain requests, causing the KDC to crash.
required_preconditions: Attacker possesses a krbtgt ticket using older encryption type
Attacker makes an S4U2Self request

fix.strategy: Remove the assertion that could be triggered by an attacker.
changed_operations: Removed assertion check on reply_encpart->enc_padata
fix.post_fix_invariant: The function no longer contains a reachable assertion that can crash the KDC when processing malicious requests.

functional_semantics.purpose: Open and execute commands from a script file, with optional immediate execution mode
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Executes commands from an external file, potentially allowing arbitrary command execution

vulnerability.triggering_action: Using the :source! command with a malicious modeline
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing sandbox restriction check before sourcing external files
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The openscript() function could be invoked to source files without verifying if execution occurs within a sandboxed environment
required_preconditions: Ability to provide malicious input through modelines
Direct execution mode enabled

fix.strategy: Add sandbox restriction check before allowing file sourcing
added_guards: check_secure() call to prevent sourcing in sandbox
fix.post_fix_invariant: Files cannot be sourced when executing within a sandbox

functional_semantics.purpose: Write BMP image format files, handling various BMP versions (2, 3, 4), color depths (1, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32 bits per pixel), compression options, and color mapping for paletted images.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory for pixel data and colormap buffers. If memory allocation fails, the function throws an exception but must ensure previously allocated resources are properly released before exiting.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a BMP image with a PseudoClass storage class (paletted image) when memory allocation for the colormap buffer fails.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Memory leak due to missing cleanup of a previously allocated resource on an error path.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: In the 'before' code, when `AcquireQuantumMemory` fails for `bmp_colormap`, the function throws `ResourceLimitError` via `ThrowWriterException`. However, it does not first release the `pixel_info` memory (allocated earlier via `AcquireVirtualMemory`), causing a memory leak. The allocated `pixel_info` remains unreleased.
required_preconditions: The image storage class is PseudoClass (paletted).
The function reaches the colormap dumping section.
Memory allocation for `bmp_colormap` fails (`AcquireQuantumMemory` returns NULL).

fix.strategy: Ensure proper resource cleanup on the error path by releasing the previously allocated `pixel_info` before throwing the exception.
added_guards: Added a check to release `pixel_info` if `bmp_colormap` allocation fails.
changed_operations: In the error handling block after `bmp_colormap` allocation fails, added `pixel_info=RelinquishVirtualMemory(pixel_info);` before throwing the exception.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If `bmp_colormap` allocation fails, the function releases the `pixel_info` memory before propagating the error, preventing a memory leak.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse X Window System window dumping (XWD) image files and convert them to ImageMagick's internal format.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads and validates a file header structure, allocates memory based on header fields, reads pixel data, and processes colormap information.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted XWD image file with a header.xoffset value that exceeds the file size.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of a header field against input file boundaries.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The header.xoffset field was not checked to ensure it is within the bounds of the input file before being used.
required_preconditions: Malformed XWD file with header.xoffset >= file size
Program attempts to parse the file

fix.strategy: Add a bounds check before processing header data.
added_guards: Check that header.xoffset is less than the total blob size
changed_operations: Added validation: if ((MagickSizeType) header.xoffset >= GetBlobSize(image)) ThrowReaderException(...)
fix.post_fix_invariant: header.xoffset is guaranteed to be within file bounds before further processing.

functional_semantics.purpose: Read and decode PCD (Photo CD) image files, handling various resolutions and overview thumbnails.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates multiple memory buffers for image processing (luma, chroma1, chroma2). If any allocation fails, the function should clean up previously allocated buffers before throwing an exception.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PCD file that causes memory allocation for one of the three buffers (luma, chroma1, chroma2) to fail after others have already succeeded.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Memory leak due to missing cleanup on partial allocation failure.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When allocating three separate buffers (chroma1, chroma2, luma), the code checked if any allocation failed via a combined condition `if ((chroma1 == NULL) || (chroma2 == NULL) || (luma == NULL))`. If, for example, chroma1 and chroma2 succeeded but luma failed, the function would throw an exception without freeing chroma1 and chroma2, leaking that memory.
required_preconditions: The function is reading a PCD image (or a crafted file that passes initial header checks).
The system is under memory pressure, causing at least one of the three buffer allocations to fail, while at least one other allocation had previously succeeded.

fix.strategy: Add cleanup for each individually allocated buffer before throwing the exception on allocation failure.
added_guards: Before throwing the `ResourceLimitError` exception, the fix adds three conditional checks to release each buffer if it was non-NULL.
changed_operations: Replaced a direct `ThrowReaderException` call with a block that checks each buffer pointer and calls `RelinquishMagickMemory` for any that are not NULL, then throws the exception.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If any of the three critical buffer allocations fails, all previously successfully allocated buffers among them are freed before propagating the error, preventing memory leaks.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse MNG (Multiple-image Network Graphics) files, reading chunks and constructing image sequences with support for loops, framing, and object definitions.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted MNG chunk data, including LOOP chunks that specify iteration counts, and may enter infinite loops if iteration counts are not properly validated.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted MNG file containing a LOOP chunk with a zero or negative iteration count.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Infinite loop due to incorrect loop iteration count validation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The condition 'if (loop_iters == 0)' only checked for zero iterations, allowing negative iteration counts to bypass the skipping mechanism and cause an infinite loop when decrementing the loop count never reaches zero.
required_preconditions: A LOOP chunk is present in the MNG file
The iteration count field is set to a negative value or zero

fix.strategy: Expand validation to treat both zero and negative iteration counts as invalid, triggering loop skipping for non-positive values.
added_guards: Changed condition from 'if (loop_iters == 0)' to 'if (loop_iters <= 0)'
changed_operations: Modified loop iteration validation logic
fix.post_fix_invariant: Loop iterations with non-positive counts are skipped, preventing infinite loops.

functional_semantics.purpose: Allocate or resize a buffer for XML parsing, ensuring sufficient space for incoming data
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Calculates buffer size requirements and performs memory allocation/reallocation

vulnerability.triggering_action: Providing a large amount of compressed XML data to the parser
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in buffer size calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Signed integer overflow when calculating needed buffer size (len + bufferEnd - bufferPtr) and when doubling buffer size during reallocation
required_preconditions: Parser receives large compressed XML data
Buffer needs expansion

fix.strategy: Prevent signed integer overflow by using unsigned arithmetic for critical calculations
changed_operations: Changed 'len + (int)(bufferEnd - bufferPtr)' to '(int)((unsigned)len + (unsigned)(bufferEnd - bufferPtr))'
Changed 'bufferSize * 2' to '(int)(2U * (unsigned)bufferSize)'
fix.post_fix_invariant: Buffer size calculations use unsigned arithmetic to avoid signed overflow, then cast back to signed int for compatibility

functional_semantics.purpose: Send USB/IP response packets containing USB request block (URB) data back to a client.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes incoming USB/IP packets, constructs response packets using data from kernel URB structures, and transmits them over a network socket.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a specially crafted USB over IP packet that triggers the construction of a response for a URB where `urb->actual_length` is greater than zero but `urb->transfer_buffer` is a null pointer.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: A NULL pointer dereference occurs when code attempts to use a pointer that has not been validated.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function accessed `urb->transfer_buffer` (via pointer arithmetic `urb->transfer_buffer + urb->iso_frame_desc[i].offset`) to populate I/O vectors for network transmission without first checking if the pointer was valid, despite `urb->actual_length` indicating there was data to send.
required_preconditions: The system is using the USB/IP subsystem.
A malicious or malformed USB/IP packet is received.
The packet causes the kernel to process a URB response where `urb->actual_length > 0` and `urb->transfer_buffer == NULL`.

fix.strategy: Add an early validation check to abort processing if a contradictory state is detected.
added_guards: A check for `(urb->actual_length > 0 && !urb->transfer_buffer)` was added at the beginning of the loop iteration.
changed_operations: The function now returns an error immediately if the guard condition is met, before any further processing or memory allocation occurs.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If `urb->actual_length` is greater than zero, then `urb->transfer_buffer` must be a valid, non-null pointer before it is used for constructing the network packet.

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize and open an HFS btree structure from filesystem metadata
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses filesystem metadata structures (extent records, btree headers) from disk, validates them, and creates in-memory btree representation

vulnerability.triggering_action: Mounting an HFS filesystem containing a malformed MDB extent record
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of relationship between two metadata fields before using one as an array index
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function hfs_inode_read_fork() populated alloc_blocks and first_blocks fields from filesystem metadata, but subsequent code only checked if first_blocks was zero, not whether alloc_blocks exceeded first_blocks
required_preconditions: Local user can mount an HFS filesystem
Filesystem contains crafted metadata where alloc_blocks > first_blocks
first_blocks is non-zero (passes existing check)

fix.strategy: Add validation check for relationship between two dependent metadata fields
added_guards: Check that alloc_blocks does not exceed first_blocks for HFS_EXT_CNID case
changed_operations: Moved unlock_new_inode() call earlier in error path for HFS_EXT_CNID case
Added validation before setting a_ops pointer
fix.post_fix_invariant: For HFS_EXT_CNID btrees, alloc_blocks must be ≤ first_blocks; for HFS_CAT_CNID btrees, first_blocks must be non-zero

functional_semantics.purpose: Release a spinlock associated with a bus ID private structure
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Unconditionally dereferencing a potentially null pointer to access a spinlock

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling put_busid_priv with a null pointer argument
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing null check before pointer dereference
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function assumed its pointer argument was always valid, but concurrent probe/disconnect/rebind operations could result in a null pointer being passed
required_preconditions: Concurrent USB over IP operations creating race conditions
Function called with freed or null bid pointer

fix.strategy: Add null pointer guard before dereferencing
added_guards: if (bid)
changed_operations: Conditional spin_unlock call
fix.post_fix_invariant: spin_unlock is only called when bid is non-null

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse HDF5 data layout messages to allocate and read data chunks from a file.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates heap memory based on file-controlled size values and reads data into that buffer.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a data layout message with layout_class=1 where data->data already points to allocated memory.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing deallocation of previously allocated heap buffer before reallocation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When layout_class=1, if data->data was already allocated (e.g., from previous message), the code would allocate new memory with calloc without freeing the old buffer, causing a memory leak. However, the CWE-787 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow) suggests the leak might have been exploitable via subsequent operations that assumed wrong buffer size.
required_preconditions: Processing a file with layout_class=1 data layout message
data->data already points to allocated memory from previous operation

fix.strategy: Explicitly free existing buffer before allocating new one for the same field.
added_guards: if (data->data) { free(data->data); data->data = NULL; }
changed_operations: Added buffer cleanup before allocation in layout_class=1 case
fix.post_fix_invariant: When processing layout_class=1, data->data is either NULL or freshly allocated for the current chunk, with no stale previous allocation.

functional_semantics.purpose: Clip matrix element values to stay within specified min and max bounds
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Iterates through matrix elements and modifies them in place without checking if matrix dimensions are valid

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted JPEG 2000 image
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Invalid memory read due to missing validation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Function attempts to access matrix data without verifying that the matrix has non-zero dimensions
required_preconditions: Matrix has zero rows or zero columns
Matrix pointer is non-null but dimensions are zero

fix.strategy: Add guard condition before processing
added_guards: Check that matrix row count > 0
Check that matrix column count > 0
fix.post_fix_invariant: Matrix processing only occurs when both dimensions are positive

functional_semantics.purpose: Destroy inline data in an ext4 inode by clearing the inline data area and updating inode metadata.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Clears inline data from both the on-disk inode structure and the in-memory inode cache.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Mounting and operating on a crafted ext4 filesystem image.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incomplete data clearing during inline data destruction.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function only cleared inline data in the on-disk inode buffer but not in the in-memory inode cache (ei->i_data).
required_preconditions: Local user access
Ability to mount a crafted ext4 filesystem image

fix.strategy: Clear inline data from both on-disk and in-memory locations.
changed_operations: Added memset to clear ei->i_data for EXT4_MIN_INLINE_DATA_SIZE
fix.post_fix_invariant: Inline data is cleared from both on-disk and in-memory representations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse email messages and their parts, including handling security-related parts like OpenPGP signatures.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes email message parts in a queue, which includes security parts like signatures. The order in which parts are added to the final part list matters for security validation.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an email containing a specially crafted attachment with a valid OpenPGP signature.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect ordering of security-related parts relative to other message parts during parsing.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Security parts (like OpenPGP signatures) were being added to the output queue in an order that allowed them to be misinterpreted as applying to different message content.
required_preconditions: Email contains a valid OpenPGP signature as an attachment
Signature is crafted to appear as applying to arbitrary message content

fix.strategy: Ensure security parts are positioned before header parts in the processing queue
changed_operations: Added call to reorder security parts before headers
fix.post_fix_invariant: Security parts (like signatures) are always processed before header parts in the mail part queue

functional_semantics.purpose: Perform binary search on index samples to estimate selectivity of a query predicate.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Uses user-controlled input (pRec->nField) to calculate array indices without proper bounds checking.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling whereKeyStats with pRec->nField larger than pIdx->nSample.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in array index calculation due to unchecked multiplication.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The calculation iSample = pIdx->nSample * nField can overflow when nField (user-controlled) is very large, leading to out-of-bounds array access.
required_preconditions: User can control pRec->nField value
pRec->nField > pIdx->nSample
Multiplication pIdx->nSample * nField exceeds integer range

fix.strategy: Limit user-controlled input before using it in index calculations.
added_guards: MIN(pRec->nField, pIdx->nSample) to bound nField
changed_operations: Replaced direct assignment nField = pRec->nField with bounded assignment
fix.post_fix_invariant: nField never exceeds pIdx->nSample, preventing overflow in iSample calculation.

functional_semantics.purpose: Extract a string value from a DICOM object element and copy it to a buffer
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Copies string data from a DICOM element to a caller-provided buffer using strlcpy

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a database query result where getString() returns an error but leaves aString uninitialized or invalid
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use of unvalidated pointer after potentially failed operation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The aString pointer is passed to strlcpy without checking if the preceding getString() call succeeded
required_preconditions: elem->getString() returns non-EC_Normal error
aString contains invalid/uninitialized data
bufsize is insufficient for the invalid data

fix.strategy: Add validation check before using operation result
added_guards: Check ec == EC_Normal after elem->getString() call
fix.post_fix_invariant: strlcpy is only called when getString() succeeds

functional_semantics.purpose: Draw dashed polygons by processing vertex data and dash pattern specifications
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes external input (dash patterns and vertex data) to allocate memory and perform geometric calculations

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted file containing polygon drawing instructions
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Type mismatch between signed and unsigned integer variables in loop condition
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Comparison between signed loop counter (i) and unsigned size variable (number_vertices) without proper casting, potentially allowing out-of-bounds access
required_preconditions: External input controls polygon vertex data
Loop counter variable is signed type
Bound variable is unsigned type
No explicit bounds checking in loop condition

fix.strategy: Explicit type casting in loop condition to ensure proper comparison
added_guards: Explicit cast of unsigned number_vertices to signed type in loop condition
changed_operations: Changed 'i < number_vertices' to 'i < (ssize_t) number_vertices'
fix.post_fix_invariant: Loop counter comparison uses consistent signed types to prevent underflow/wrap-around issues

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode a JBIG2 symbol dictionary from compressed data, handling both Huffman and arithmetic coding, and supporting various symbol types including generic, refinement, and aggregate symbols.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses potentially untrusted input data to construct symbol dictionaries, with multiple code paths that can fail due to invalid input.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling jbig2_decode_text_region() without checking its return value when processing aggregate symbols in a Huffman-coded symbol dictionary.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing error handling after a function call that can return an error code.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function jbig2_decode_text_region() returns an error code, but the original code didn't check it before proceeding to use the result. This could lead to using uninitialized or partially initialized data.
required_preconditions: Processing a Huffman-coded symbol dictionary (SDHUFF=true)
Processing aggregate symbols (SDREFAGG=true)
Having REFAGGNINST > 1
jbig2_decode_text_region() returning an error

fix.strategy: Add error checking after the jbig2_decode_text_region() call and propagate errors appropriately.
added_guards: Added check for negative return value from jbig2_decode_text_region()
Added goto cleanup4 on error to ensure proper cleanup
changed_operations: Changed from calling jbig2_decode_text_region() without checking return value to storing and checking the return value
Added error propagation path
fix.post_fix_invariant: All error codes from jbig2_decode_text_region() are checked and properly handled before proceeding with further operations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse a CRW image directory structure from binary data
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates offsets and sizes before reading data to prevent out-of-bounds access

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted CRW image file
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in bounds check leading to out-of-bounds read
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The expression 'o+2 > size' could overflow when 'o' is near maximum uint32_t value, bypassing validation. The expression '(o + (count * 10)) > size' could overflow when 'count * 10' exceeds uint32_t range.
required_preconditions: Malformed CRW image with manipulated directory offset or entry count

fix.strategy: Reorganize arithmetic to prevent overflow before comparison
changed_operations: Changed 'o+2 > size' to 'o > size-2'
Changed '(o + (count * 10)) > size' to 'static_cast<uint32_t>(count) * 10 > size-o'
fix.post_fix_invariant: All arithmetic operations are performed in a way that prevents integer overflow before bounds checking

functional_semantics.purpose: Export pixel index values from an image's colormap to a byte buffer with various bit depths.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Casts the return value of GetPixelIndex() to unsigned char without checking if the value fits within the range of unsigned char (0-255).

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PDF file that causes GetPixelIndex() to return a value outside the range of unsigned char.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow/truncation during type conversion.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Direct cast of GetPixelIndex() return value to unsigned char can result in truncation of values >255, leading to undefined behavior when the truncated value is used in subsequent bitwise operations.
required_preconditions: Image storage class is PseudoClass
GetPixelIndex() returns a value >255

fix.strategy: Add intermediate cast to signed type before narrowing cast.
changed_operations: Changed '(unsigned char) GetPixelIndex(image,p)' to '(unsigned char) ((ssize_t) GetPixelIndex(image,p))'
fix.post_fix_invariant: GetPixelIndex() return value is first cast to ssize_t (signed), then to unsigned char, ensuring defined truncation behavior.

functional_semantics.purpose: The DrawImage function parses and executes drawing primitives from a string-based command language (MVG - Magick Vector Graphics). It interprets tokens representing graphical operations like shapes, transformations, colors, and text rendering.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function processes externally supplied input (the 'primitive' string) which can come from file contents or direct user input. It uses a token parsing function (GetNextToken) to extract keywords and parameters from this input string.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted file containing malicious drawing primitive commands.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Buffer overflow due to incorrect buffer size calculation when parsing tokens.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function calls GetNextToken with an incorrectly calculated buffer size parameter. Before the fix, it passed 'extent' (which equals strlen(token) + MagickPathExtent) as the buffer size for keyword extraction. However, the keyword buffer is only MagickPathExtent bytes, so if strlen(token) is large, the calculated size exceeds the actual buffer size, leading to overflow when copying parsed keywords.
required_preconditions: External input containing drawing primitives is processed
The input contains tokens that cause GetNextToken to write beyond the keyword buffer bounds
No validation of the calculated buffer size against actual buffer size

fix.strategy: Use a fixed buffer size constant instead of a calculated value for the keyword buffer parameter.
changed_operations: Changed GetNextToken call for keyword parsing from GetNextToken(q,&q,extent,keyword) to GetNextToken(q,&q,MagickPathExtent,keyword)
This ensures the size parameter matches the actual size of the keyword buffer
fix.post_fix_invariant: The size parameter passed to GetNextToken for keyword extraction always matches the actual size of the destination keyword buffer (MagickPathExtent).

functional_semantics.purpose: Build glyph class definitions for OpenType font layout processing
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates an array to store glyph classes and iterates through input arrays to set classes

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted font file with malicious charmap data
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Array size mismatch between allocation and usage
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function allocated an array sized for 'num_total_glyphs' but only initialized 'count' elements, while later operations could access glyph indices up to 'num_total_glyphs-1'
required_preconditions: Font file contains glyph indices outside the allocated range
Application processes the malicious font

fix.strategy: Match allocation size to actual usage requirements

Updated the post-operation register updates (dst_x, dst_y) to use the calculated unsigned coordinates.

functional_semantics.purpose: Prepare MSR (Model-Specific Register) access bitmap for nested virtualization by merging L1 guest's MSR bitmap into L0 hypervisor's bitmap, controlling which MSR accesses are intercepted.

functional_semantics.purpose: Callback function that processes the result of an authorization check for PackageKit actions.

required_preconditions: The user lacks authorization for the 'package-install' action.
The transaction possesses the 'ALLOW_REINSTALL' flag.
The package being installed is signed.

changed_operations: Removed the conditional block that checked for 'package-install' action and 'ALLOW_REINSTALL' flag upon authorization failure.
