vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a YANG file containing a leaf of type 'identityref' with a sufficiently long module name or identity value.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Stack buffer overflow due to missing length check before copying data into fixed-size buffer.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: In the LY_TYPE_IDENT case, sprintf() and strcpy() were called without verifying that the combined length of module_name and value strings (or value alone) would not exceed the 512-byte buf capacity.
required_preconditions: Untrusted YANG file input
Leaf type identityref with long module name or identity value
Application uses libyang to parse the file

fix.strategy: Add explicit length checks before string copying operations.
added_guards: Length check before sprintf() in LY_TYPE_IDENT case when adding module prefix
Length check before strcpy() in LY_TYPE_IDENT case when no prefix needed
changed_operations: Added LY_CHECK_ERR_RETURN with strlen validation before sprintf
Added LY_CHECK_ERR_RETURN with strlen validation before strcpy
fix.post_fix_invariant: All string copying operations in the LY_TYPE_IDENT case are preceded by validation that the resulting string will not exceed buffer capacity.

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode LZW-compressed data stream, building a code table dynamically and converting codewords to output indexes.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted input data containing LZW codes, maintains internal state including code table and previous code, and handles special control codes (clear and end-of-information).

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted GIF image with LZW compression containing specific code sequences.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Infinite loop in write_indexes function due to cyclic code table references.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When c->self_code equals 10, self->code_table[10].extends assigns value 11 to c. Next iteration assigns self->code_table[11].extends to c, giving value 10, creating infinite loop.
required_preconditions: Processing LZW-compressed data
Code table contains cyclic extends references between entries 10 and 11
write_indexes function traverses extends chain

fix.strategy: Move invalid code check earlier and simplify code addition logic.
added_guards: if (self->code >= self->code_table_size) check before write_indexes call
changed_operations: Removed else-if branch checking self->code == self->code_table_size
Changed add_code logic to use else branch for both self->code >= self->code_table_size cases
fix.post_fix_invariant: Invalid codes (self->code >= self->code_table_size) are detected and handled before write_indexes is called, preventing traversal of invalid code table entries.

functional_semantics.purpose: Unregister a CAPI controller from the system by removing it from the controller array and cleaning up associated resources.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accesses an array using an index derived from user-controlled or externally supplied controller number (cnr) without validation.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling detach_capi_ctr with a controller struct where the cnr field has an out-of-bounds value.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check on an array index before use.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The cnr field of the ctr parameter was used directly to calculate an index into the capi_controller array without verifying it falls within the valid range of the array.
required_preconditions: The cnr field of the provided controller struct is less than 1 or greater than CAPI_MAXCONTR.

fix.strategy: Add a guard condition to validate the array index before any array access.
added_guards: Check that ctr->cnr is at least 1 and that ctr->cnr - 1 is less than CAPI_MAXCONTR.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The calculated array index (ctr->cnr - 1) is guaranteed to be within the bounds [0, CAPI_MAXCONTR - 1] before being used to access the capi_controller array.

functional_semantics.purpose: Read and decode MATLAB (.mat) image files, handling various data types, compression, and matrix structures.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses a complex binary file format with multiple nested objects, reading header fields and data blocks, and may create temporary decompressed images.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted MATLAB image file with malformed or inconsistent size fields.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use-after-free due to improper lifetime management of a temporary image object during error handling.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When an error occurs during scanline reading (e.g., a short read), the code jumps to a cleanup label ('ExitLoop') where the temporary 'image2' may be destroyed, but later code paths might still reference it.
required_preconditions: A crafted .mat file triggers an error during pixel data reading.
The error occurs after a temporary decompressed image ('image2') has been created and is distinct from the main 'image'.

fix.strategy: Immediate termination on critical read failure to prevent subsequent use of invalid objects.
added_guards: Added a 'ThrowReaderException' call when 'ReadBlob' fails to read the expected number of bytes for a scanline, before jumping to the cleanup label.
changed_operations: Changed the condition for entering the main object parser loop from 'while(!EOFBlob(image))' to 'while(filepos < GetBlobSize(image) && !EOFBlob(image))'.
Added a bounds check on 'filepos' against 'GetBlobSize(image)' and zero at the start of each loop iteration.
Changed an overflow check from '>' to '>=' when comparing 'ObjectSize+filepos' against the total blob size.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If a critical read operation fails during pixel data processing, the function will throw an exception and terminate, preventing further execution that might rely on partially read or invalidated objects.

functional_semantics.purpose: Open and monitor an input device for button events
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Manages file descriptors and event sources for input device monitoring

vulnerability.triggering_action: Repeated execution of the function without proper cleanup of previous event source
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Resource leak during re-initialization
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When button_open is called multiple times on the same Button object, the existing sd_event_source stored in b->io_event_source is not released before creating a new one
required_preconditions: Function is called multiple times on same Button object
Previous call successfully created an event source

fix.strategy: Explicitly release previous event source reference before creating new one
changed_operations: Added sd_event_source_unref call on b->io_event_source before sd_event_add_io
fix.post_fix_invariant: Event source reference is properly managed across multiple calls

functional_semantics.purpose: Add a new HIDP (Human Interface Device Profile) connection for Bluetooth, handling session creation and registration with L2CAP layer.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function accesses a socket's L2CAP channel structure to obtain connection information before performing session setup and registration.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling hidp_connection_add with a control socket that lacks a valid L2CAP channel structure.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Access of a potentially uninitialized or invalid pointer.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The pointer 'chan' was derived from 'ctrl_sock->sk' before the socket verification function (hidp_verify_sockets) completed. If hidp_verify_sockets failed, the function could return early, but 'chan' had already been accessed during its initialization via l2cap_pi().
required_preconditions: The hidp_verify_sockets function returns a failure (non-zero value).
The control socket's internal sk structure is in an invalid state or the l2cap_pi() macro produces an invalid result.

fix.strategy: Reorder operations to ensure socket verification succeeds before dereferencing the socket to obtain the L2CAP channel.
changed_operations: Moved the assignment 'chan = l2cap_pi(ctrl_sock->sk)->chan;' to after the call to hidp_verify_sockets and its success check.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The socket's L2CAP channel pointer is only accessed after the sockets have been verified as valid.

functional_semantics.purpose: Shrink the Lua stack when usage is low to reduce memory consumption.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Calculates a target stack size based on current usage and conditionally reallocates the stack.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Stack shrinking during garbage collection.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect calculation of target stack size during shrink operation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The formula for 'goodsize' used a percentage-based growth (inuse + (inuse / 8) + 2*EXTRA_STACK) that could result in a stack size too small for safe garbage collection.
required_preconditions: Garbage collection is running
Stack usage is low enough to trigger shrinking

fix.strategy: Replace dynamic calculation with fixed minimum size.
changed_operations: Changed goodsize calculation from inuse + (inuse/8) + 2*EXTRA_STACK to inuse + BASIC_STACK_SIZE
fix.post_fix_invariant: Shrunk stack always maintains at least BASIC_STACK_SIZE additional space beyond current usage.

functional_semantics.purpose: Convert TrueType font data to Type 42 sfnts array format for embedding in PostScript output.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes font table data from potentially untrusted PDF documents, constructing new table structures and writing them via output functions.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling dumpString() with a length parameter that exceeds the actual size of the source buffer.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Buffer over-read due to incorrect bounds check logic.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When writing synthetic vhea or vmtx tables, the code compared length >= buffer_size, allowing equality case to pass. This permitted reading one byte beyond buffer end when length equaled buffer size.
required_preconditions: Processing a TrueType font requiring synthetic vertical metrics tables
The calculated length for vheaTab or vmtxTab equals the buffer size

fix.strategy: Change comparison from >= to > to prevent reading beyond buffer when length equals buffer size.
changed_operations: Changed length >= sizeof(vheaTab) to length > sizeof(vheaTab)
Changed length >= vmtxTabLength to length > vmtxTabLength
fix.post_fix_invariant: dumpString() is never called with length exceeding the source buffer size.

functional_semantics.purpose: Cleanup function for X Window System resources, releasing memory and destroying window objects.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Frees X11 resources (windows, images, cursors, pixmaps, fonts, etc.) to prevent resource leaks.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling DestroyXResources() without properly cleaning up all allocated XImage objects.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing cleanup of a specific XImage field (matte_image) in resource destruction routine.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The XImage pointer 'matte_image' in XWindowInfo structure was not being destroyed with XDestroyImage() before being nulled, causing memory leak.
required_preconditions: X11 display system is used
matte_image field contains allocated XImage object
DestroyXResources() is called

fix.strategy: Add missing cleanup for previously overlooked resource field.
added_guards: if (magick_windows[i]->matte_image != (XImage *) NULL)
changed_operations: Added XDestroyImage(magick_windows[i]->matte_image) call
fix.post_fix_invariant: All XImage objects in XWindowInfo structure (both ximage and matte_image) are properly destroyed before being nulled.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse and validate CLOOP disk image format header and offset table
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads and validates image metadata from untrusted file, allocates memory based on calculated sizes

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malicious CLOOP image with crafted offset values
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of offset table ordering and compressed block size
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code accepted non-monotonically increasing offsets and excessively large compressed block sizes without validation, allowing memory allocation overflow
required_preconditions: Malicious CLOOP image with decreasing offset values
Malicious CLOOP image with offset differences exceeding reasonable bounds

fix.strategy: Add validation checks for offset ordering and compressed block size bounds
added_guards: Check that offsets[i] >= offsets[i-1] for monotonic increase
Check that compressed block size <= 2 * MAX_BLOCK_SIZE
changed_operations: Added validation before size calculation in offset processing loop
fix.post_fix_invariant: Offset table must be monotonically increasing and compressed block sizes must be bounded

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode a PKCS#15 private key data file (PrKDF) entry from ASN.1 encoded data.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses ASN.1 structures to extract private key information, including paths, algorithm parameters, and access control rules. Allocates memory for extracted data (e.g., subject value, GOST parameters).

vulnerability.triggering_action: ASN.1 decoding fails (sc_asn1_decode_choice returns r < 0).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect cleanup of partially allocated resources on error path.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The error handling code attempted to free a field (`asn1_com_prkey_attr[0].parm`) based on a flawed condition check, rather than freeing the actual allocated buffer (`info.subject.value`). This could lead to a double-free or memory leak depending on the state.
required_preconditions: The function reaches the error path where r < 0.
Memory for `info.subject.value` was allocated earlier in the function (via sc_format_asn1_entry).

fix.strategy: Directly free the correctly identified allocated resource on the error path.
changed_operations: Replaced the conditional free of `asn1_com_prkey_attr[0].parm` with an unconditional `free(info.subject.value);`.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If ASN.1 decoding fails (r < 0), any memory allocated for `info.subject.value` is freed before the function returns.

functional_semantics.purpose: Construct a single byte array from multiple reply fragments for CTCP protocol communication
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory based on calculated total size of input replies

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted CTCP request with manipulated reply fragments
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect memory allocation and population logic
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The pre-allocated QByteArray was incorrectly populated due to reference aliasing and replacement logic
required_preconditions: Remote attacker can send CTCP requests
System processes CTCP requests

fix.strategy: Replaced manual memory population with safe container operations
changed_operations: Replaced manual replace() operations with append()
Changed from pre-sized constructor to reserve() + append() pattern
fix.post_fix_invariant: Memory operations use safe container APIs instead of manual indexing

functional_semantics.purpose: Export pixel index values from a colormapped image to a byte buffer with various bit depths
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Converts pixel index values to unsigned char for output packing, potentially truncating values

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PDF file that causes GetPixelIndex() to return values outside the range representable by unsigned char
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow/truncation when converting pixel index values to unsigned char
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Direct casting of GetPixelIndex() return value to unsigned char without range checking
required_preconditions: Image must be PseudoClass storage class
GetPixelIndex() must return value > 255

fix.strategy: Add intermediate cast to ssize_t before casting to unsigned char
changed_operations: Changed pixel=(unsigned char) *indexes++; to pixel=(unsigned char) ((ssize_t) *indexes++);
fix.post_fix_invariant: Pixel index values are first cast to signed type ssize_t before narrowing to unsigned char

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse FITS file header to extract metadata and validate format compliance
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted file headers containing string fields like XTENSION

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malformed FITS file with an invalid XTENSION header
vulnerability.abstract_cause: NULL pointer dereference due to missing validation of function return value
vulnerability.detailed_cause: fits_decode_card() returns NULL for invalid XTENSION header, but code proceeds to dereference fdat->fstring without checking
required_preconditions: XTENSION header exists in file
Header is malformed/invalid
fits_decode_card() returns NULL

fix.strategy: Add explicit NULL check before dereferencing pointer
added_guards: Check if fdat != NULL before strcpy
changed_operations: Added conditional block to handle NULL return from fits_decode_card()
fix.post_fix_invariant: XTENSION field is only accessed after confirming successful decoding

functional_semantics.purpose: Resolve and validate file system paths, handling both absolute and relative paths, with platform-specific logic for Windows UNC paths and drive letters.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates input path length against a maximum buffer size (MAXPATHLEN) to prevent buffer overflows, constructs full paths by combining current directory with relative paths, and performs path canonicalization.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted ZIP archive extraction operation with a path that triggers an integer overflow during path length calculation.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in path length calculation leading to stack-based buffer overflow.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The initial validation check allowed a path_length of zero to pass, which could interact with subsequent arithmetic operations (like path_length + state_cwd_length + 1) in a way that causes integer overflow, bypassing the MAXPATHLEN-1 check and resulting in buffer overflow.
required_preconditions: Path length must be zero
Relative path processing must be invoked
Current directory state must have non-zero length

fix.strategy: Strengthen initial input validation to reject zero-length paths.
added_guards: Reject path_length <= 0 instead of just path_length == 0
changed_operations: Changed condition from 'path_length == 0 || path_length >= MAXPATHLEN-1' to 'path_length <= 0 || path_length >= MAXPATHLEN-1'
fix.post_fix_invariant: Path length must be strictly positive and less than MAXPATHLEN-1 before any path construction arithmetic.

functional_semantics.purpose: Handle client file transfer requests by routing messages between client and agent, managing transfer IDs and active connections.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Uses a hash table to associate file transfer IDs with active connections, allowing data routing based on ID without verifying ownership.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Client sends file transfer data or status messages with an ID that belongs to another user's active transfer.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing authorization check when processing file transfer data/status messages.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function looked up connection from active_xfers hash table using client-provided ID but did not verify the requesting client owns that transfer ID.
required_preconditions: Multiple users have active file transfers
Attacker can send messages to the file transfer interface
Attacker knows or can guess another user's transfer ID

fix.strategy: Prevent ID reuse by checking for existing ID during transfer start.
added_guards: Check if transfer ID already exists in active_xfers table before accepting new transfer start
changed_operations: Added validation in VD_AGENT_FILE_XFER_START case to reject duplicate IDs
fix.post_fix_invariant: Each transfer ID in active_xfers table is unique and owned by the session that started it.

functional_semantics.purpose: Load a font face from an archive, caching results to avoid redundant loading.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads font data from an archive entry and processes it for font rendering.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted font file.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Heap-based buffer over-read.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function ft_font_face_hash (not shown in the provided code fragments) reads beyond allocated bounds when computing a hash for a font face structure.
required_preconditions: A crafted font file is provided as input.

fix.strategy: Removed an error-handling code block that set an error but did not return NULL, allowing execution to continue with potentially invalid data.
changed_operations: Simplified the early return logic after gxps_archive_read_entry fails.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If gxps_archive_read_entry fails, the function returns NULL immediately without proceeding.

functional_semantics.purpose: Authenticate users against system password databases (passwd/shadow files).
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Checks account status (locked, expired), password expiration, and valid shell before returning encrypted password for verification.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Remote authentication request with expired password.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incomplete password expiration check.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code checked only the account expiration field (sp_expire) but not the password aging fields (sp_lstchg + sp_max) from the shadow password structure.
required_preconditions: Unix authentication mode enabled
Shadow passwords in use
Password expiration policy configured via aging fields

fix.strategy: Added missing password aging check using sp_lstchg and sp_max fields.
added_guards: sp_lstchg > 0
sp_max >= 0
current_date > (sp_lstchg + sp_max)
changed_operations: Extended conditional to include password aging logic before existing account expiration check
fix.post_fix_invariant: Both password aging (sp_lstchg+sp_max) and account expiration (sp_expire) are checked when shadow passwords are available.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process the result of a DNSKEY fetch for managed DNSSEC trust anchors, updating the local key database and trust status based on validation and key state changes.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates fetched DNSKEY records using current trusted keys, manages the lifecycle of trust anchors (addition, revocation, removal), and updates internal state accordingly. Failure to handle certain key conditions can cause assertion failures.

vulnerability.triggering_action: During a DNSSEC key rollover, a trust anchor's keys are replaced with keys that use an unsupported cryptographic algorithm.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing error handling for a specific failure condition (unsupported algorithm) leads to an unexpected program state and subsequent assertion failure.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function `compute_tag` can fail (return a non-success result) when processing a DNSKEY with an unsupported algorithm. The original code assumed this operation always succeeded (`RUNTIME_CHECK`). When it failed during key rollover processing, the program state became inconsistent, leading to an assertion failure later.
required_preconditions: Managed-keys feature is enabled.
A configured trust anchor undergoes a key rollover.
The new key introduced during the rollover uses a cryptographic algorithm not supported by the BIND instance.

fix.strategy: Add explicit error handling for the `compute_tag` failure case, skipping the problematic key and logging an error, instead of allowing the failure to propagate and cause an assertion.
added_guards: A check on the return value of `compute_tag`.
A conditional branch that logs an error and uses `continue` to skip further processing of the key if `compute_tag` fails.
changed_operations: Replaced unconditional `RUNTIME_CHECK(result == ISC_R_SUCCESS);` after `compute_tag` calls with a conditional check and error handling flow.
fix.post_fix_invariant: Keys with unsupported algorithms are logged and skipped during managed-keys processing, preventing state corruption and assertion failures.

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize double-precision floating-point audio data handling by setting up function pointers for reading/writing based on endianness and CPU capabilities.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Computes blockwidth as sizeof(double) * channels, then later divides datalength by blockwidth to calculate frame count.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted audio file with zero channels.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Divide-by-zero error during frame count calculation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When channels = 0, blockwidth = sizeof(double) * 0 = 0, leading to division by zero in psf->sf.frames = psf->datalength / psf->blockwidth.
required_preconditions: Audio file parsed with channels field set to zero
File passes initial validation that only checks channels < 1

fix.strategy: Add upper bound validation to reject invalid channel counts.
added_guards: Check that channels <= SF_MAX_CHANNELS
changed_operations: Changed condition from 'if (psf->sf.channels < 1)' to 'if (psf->sf.channels < 1 || psf->sf.channels > SF_MAX_CHANNELS)'
fix.post_fix_invariant: Channels field is guaranteed to be between 1 and SF_MAX_CHANNELS inclusive before blockwidth calculation.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse and validate XWD image file header
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads and validates header fields from untrusted file data, calculates offsets for image data access

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malicious XWD file with crafted header values
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient validation of header field values leading to buffer over-read
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Header fields like color_map_entries, pixmap_width, pixmap_height, and bytes_per_line were not bounded, allowing arithmetic overflows in size calculations
required_preconditions: Malicious XWD file input
Program attempts to parse the file

fix.strategy: Add comprehensive bounds checking to all header fields used in memory calculations
added_guards: header_size <= 65535
color_map_entries <= 256
pixmap_width between 1 and 65535
pixmap_height between 1 and 65535
bytes_per_line bounded by width-based minimum and maximum
total allocation size capped
bits_per_pixel restricted to 24 or 32
changed_operations: Replaced pointer arithmetic with UNPACK_FIELD macros
Changed n_colors to color_map_entries in size calculations
Added explicit cast to gsize for bytes_per_line multiplication
fix.post_fix_invariant: All header fields used in memory calculations are bounded within safe ranges before use

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse a filename string containing optional colon-separated mode/options for deepzoom image export.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Copies user-provided filename into fixed-size buffers, splits on colon, and processes optional mode string.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling the function with a filename string that does not contain a colon.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use of uninitialized stack memory.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'mode' character array is not initialized if the colon is not found in the filename. This uninitialized buffer is later copied and processed.
required_preconditions: Filename argument contains no colon character.

fix.strategy: Ensure local buffer is initialized in all control flow paths.
added_guards: Explicit initialization of 'mode' buffer when colon is not found.
changed_operations: Added else branch with strcpy(mode, "") after colon check.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The 'mode' buffer is explicitly initialized before being used, regardless of input.

functional_semantics.purpose: Load a saved virtio device state from a migration/save image.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Deserializes multiple fields from untrusted input including device configuration, features, and queue data.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted savevm image.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds write due to insufficient validation of array index.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'num' value read from the file controls loop iterations accessing 'vdev->vq[i]' without checking against array bounds.
required_preconditions: Untrusted input source (savevm image)
Array size smaller than maximum possible 'num' value

fix.strategy: Add bounds check before array access.
added_guards: Check that 'num' does not exceed VIRTIO_PCI_QUEUE_MAX before loop.
changed_operations: Added validation step between reading 'num' and using it as loop bound
fix.post_fix_invariant: Loop index 'i' will not exceed array bounds of 'vdev->vq'.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse XML text content containing entity references and character references, building a list of nodes representing the parsed content.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Recursively expands entity references by calling xmlStringGetNodeList on entity content. When an entity's children are NULL, it recursively processes the entity's content to populate the entity's child nodes.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted XML document containing a specially formed entity reference.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unbounded recursion due to a missing cycle detection or state guard during entity expansion.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When expanding an entity reference, the function sets ent->children = xmlStringGetNodeList(...). If the entity's content itself triggers expansion of the same entity (directly or indirectly), the recursive call chain can continue without bound.
required_preconditions: Library used in recovery mode
Crafted XML document containing cyclic or self-referential entity expansion

fix.strategy: Break recursion by marking the entity as being processed before the recursive call.
added_guards: Setting ent->children to a sentinel value ((xmlNodePtr) -1) before the recursive call to xmlStringGetNodeList
changed_operations: Added assignment 'ent->children = (xmlNodePtr) -1;' prior to the recursive call
fix.post_fix_invariant: An entity's children field is set to a non-NULL sentinel value while its content is being recursively expanded, preventing re-entry into expansion for the same entity within the same call chain.

functional_semantics.purpose: USB device probe function for PN533 NFC controller driver
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates and initializes USB URBs (USB Request Blocks) for communication, registers the device, and handles error paths

vulnerability.triggering_action: Error occurs after device registration but before successful finalization
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use-after-free during error cleanup
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When pn533_finalize_setup() fails after pn533_register_device() succeeds, the error goto jumps to 'error' label which frees URBs while the registered device may still hold references to them
required_preconditions: USB device probe fails after device registration
Registered device maintains references to allocated URBs

fix.strategy: Add dedicated cleanup path for post-registration errors and ensure URBs are killed before freeing
added_guards: Added 'err_deregister' label for post-registration cleanup
Added usb_kill_urb() calls before usb_free_urb() calls
changed_operations: Changed goto target from 'error' to 'err_deregister' for pn533_finalize_setup() failure
Added pn533_unregister_device() call in err_deregister path
Added kfree(phy->ack_buffer) in error path
fix.post_fix_invariant: Device is properly unregistered before URBs are killed and freed, preventing use-after-free

functional_semantics.purpose: Verify an encrypted challenge pre-authentication request in Kerberos KDC
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes encrypted challenge data, attempts decryption with client keys, validates timestamp, and adds authentication indicators on success

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling a function with a NULL pointer argument when a previous error condition occurred
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing error propagation leading to use of uninitialized or NULL data
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function 'k5memdup0' was called unconditionally before checking if 'retval' indicated a previous error, potentially passing NULL or invalid data to subsequent operations
required_preconditions: Previous error condition set retval to non-zero
The 'realm' data structure exists but may be invalid due to error state

fix.strategy: Add error check before potentially dangerous operation
added_guards: Conditional check of retval before calling k5memdup0
changed_operations: Moved k5memdup0 call inside existing error checking pattern
fix.post_fix_invariant: No function is called with potentially invalid data when retval indicates previous failure

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse a public identifier literal (PubidLiteral) from HTML/XML input, extracting the text between matching quote characters.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function stores a pointer to the current input position and later uses it to extract a substring after advancing the input pointer. If an error occurs before reaching the closing quote, the stored pointer may become invalid (dangling) if the input buffer has been reallocated or freed.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Parsing a crafted XML/HTML document containing a PubidLiteral that triggers an error condition (e.g., missing closing quote).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use-after-free of a pointer into a potentially freed or reallocated input buffer.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function saves `CUR_PTR` (a pointer into the input buffer) at the start of the literal. It then advances `CUR_PTR` via `NEXT`. If an error occurs (missing closing quote) and the input buffer is freed or reallocated before the saved pointer is used, subsequent use of that pointer (e.g., in `xmlStrndup`) leads to use-after-free.
required_preconditions: The parser encounters a PubidLiteral (starting with " or ').
The literal is not properly terminated (missing closing quote).
The input buffer is freed or reallocated before the saved pointer is used (e.g., due to parser error recovery or buffer growth).

fix.strategy: Replace pointer arithmetic with offset-based calculation using the base pointer (`BASE_PTR`). Store the offset from the base at the start, and compute the string start address only when needed, using the still-valid base pointer.
added_guards: Check `CUR_PTR < BASE_PTR` to detect pointer underflow (safety check).
changed_operations: Replace saving `CUR_PTR` with saving `CUR_PTR - BASE_PTR` (offset).
Replace `CUR_PTR - q` pointer difference with incrementally tracked length (`len`).
Compute string start as `BASE_PTR + startPosition` instead of using saved pointer `q`.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The function never stores a direct pointer into the input buffer across potential buffer reallocations; it only stores offsets relative to the stable base pointer.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse hexadecimal data from a string format and store it in a fixed-size buffer.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads variable-length hexadecimal data from input string and writes it to a fixed-size local array without checking if the array bounds will be exceeded.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an input string containing more than 128 hexadecimal values (since each value writes 2 bytes to the array).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check during sequential writes to a fixed-size buffer.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The while loop condition checks only for input termination, not whether writing the next 2-byte value would exceed the array capacity.
required_preconditions: Input string contains more than 128 hexadecimal values separated by delimiters.
Each hexadecimal value is valid and parsed by strtol.

fix.strategy: Add a bounds check to the loop condition to prevent writing beyond array capacity.
added_guards: Loop condition changed from 'while (1)' to 'while (length <= sizeof(array) - 2)' to ensure space for next 2-byte write.
changed_operations: Loop termination condition modified to include buffer capacity check.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The loop will terminate before 'length' exceeds the array size minus 2, preventing buffer overflow.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing malformed or truncated OPL data

added_guards: Check that input length is at least sizeof(uint32_t) before reading prop_count
changed_operations: Moved prop_count declaration after length check
Added validation: if (len < sizeof(uint32_t)) return 0
fix.post_fix_invariant: prop_count is only read after verifying sufficient buffer exists to contain it

Reference counting manages DnsStream lifetime

fix.strategy: Take an explicit reference at function entry using cleanup attribute
added_guards: dns_stream_ref() call on userdata parameter
changed_operations: Changed DnsStream *s = userdata; to _cleanup_(dns_stream_unrefp) DnsStream *s = dns_stream_ref(userdata);
fix.post_fix_invariant: Stream reference count increased for duration of function, automatically cleaned up on return

changed_operations: Moved server_names increment and pointer advance inside zero-length check
Added logging for zero-length server name case
fix.post_fix_invariant: server_names count only increments for server name records with positive length; data_size decrements only when consuming positive-length data.

If validation failed, the function could return 1 (success) for the empty return path case even when the address contained invalid characters.

Remote attacker can initiate SMTP session

Large length value that when added to current position exceeds LONG_LONG_MAX

fix.strategy: Add overflow check before arithmetic operation.
added_guards: Check if (pos + length) would overflow by verifying pos <= LONG_LONG_MAX - length
changed_operations: Added overflow validation before calling lexer->setPos(pos + length)

functional_semantics.purpose: The function WriteOnePNGImage writes a PNG image, handling color quantization, palette building, transparency, and various PNG chunk generation.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function allocates memory for pixel data based on image dimensions, color type, and bit depth. The allocation size calculation uses rowbytes and GetPixelChannels(image) to determine the buffer size.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted image file that triggers a heap buffer overflow during PNG writing.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect buffer size calculation for pixel data allocation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The buffer size calculation used a fixed multiplier (256) instead of the actual number of pixel channels, leading to an undersized allocation.

The image triggers the vulnerable code path in WriteOnePNGImage.

fix.strategy: Correct the buffer size calculation to use the actual number of pixel channels.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse PDF objects from tokenized input, handling nested structures (arrays and dictionaries) with error recovery for malformed data.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Recursively parses nested structures without depth limitation, pushing new parsing contexts onto stacks for each opening token.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a PDF with excessively deeply nested arrays or dictionaries (direct objects).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unbounded recursion via stack growth.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The parser uses stacks (olist_stack, state_stack, offset_stack) to track nested parsing contexts. Each opening array or dictionary token unconditionally pushes a new frame onto these stacks. No limit exists on stack growth, allowing an attacker to cause stack exhaustion.
required_preconditions: The parser is invoked on attacker-controlled input.
The input contains a deeply nested structure (array or dictionary) composed of direct objects.
The nesting depth is sufficient to exhaust available stack memory.

fix.strategy: Enforce a maximum nesting depth limit before pushing a new context.
added_guards: Check if olist_stack.size() exceeds a threshold (500) before processing tt_array_open or tt_dict_open tokens. If exceeded, emit a warning, treat the token as a null object, and set the state to st_top to avoid further nesting.
changed_operations: Added conditional block around the stack-pushing logic for array/dictionary open tokens.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The depth of the olist_stack (and associated stacks) is bounded by a constant maximum (500).

required_preconditions: bParseHOSTNAMEandTAG is true
INTERNAL_MSG flag is not set
TAG field in the message contains more than CONF_TAG_MAXSIZE - 1 characters before a colon or space

fix.strategy: Tighten loop guard to ensure space for null terminator.
added_guards: i < CONF_TAG_MAXSIZE - 2
changed_operations: Changed loop condition from 'i < CONF_TAG_MAXSIZE' to 'i < CONF_TAG_MAXSIZE - 2'
fix.post_fix_invariant: The index 'i' will never reach or exceed CONF_TAG_MAXSIZE - 1, guaranteeing that the subsequent null-termination write occurs within the buffer bounds.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse creator metadata block from a PSP image file, extracting fields like title, artist, copyright, description, dates, and application info.

It assumes the read data contains a null terminator within the allocated buffer, but the file data may lack one.
required_preconditions: Malicious or malformed file with a creator block string field where the stored bytes do not contain a null byte within the declared length.

functional_semantics.purpose: Rename a file from one location to another, handling cross-filesystem moves by copying and deleting.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: During a cross-filesystem rename, a new file is created at the destination before the source is deleted. The new file initially has default permissions determined by the process umask.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A rename operation that fails within the same filesystem (errno == EXDEV), triggering the cross-filesystem copy path.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: A temporary file created during a cross-filesystem rename operation was briefly accessible with overly permissive default permissions.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When the rename system call failed with EXDEV (cross-device link), the function fell back to copying the file. The copy operation (php_copy_file) created the destination file with default permissions (influenced by the process umask). The file's original ownership (chown) and permissions (chmod) were restored *after* creation, creating a race condition window where the file existed with insecure permissions.
required_preconditions: The rename operation must be across different filesystems.
The fallback copy path must be executed.
An attacker must have the ability to access the file during the brief window between its creation and the permission/ownership restoration.

fix.strategy: Temporarily restrict the process umask to prevent the creation of a world-readable/writable file during the copy, then restore the original umask after the operation.
added_guards: Setting umask to 077 (disable read/write/execute for group and others) before creating the copy file, but only in non-threaded (non-ZTS) environments where umask is considered safe to modify.
changed_operations: The order of setting ownership (chown) and permissions (chmod) was maintained, but the operations are now only performed if the previous step succeeded. Error handling for EPERM was changed from causing failure to allowing continuation, as non-root users may not be able to perform these operations.
fix.post_fix_invariant: During the cross-filesystem copy, the newly created file is guaranteed (in non-ZTS builds) to have no group or other permissions (umask 077) from the moment of its creation until the explicit chmod, significantly narrowing the race condition window for unauthorized access.

functional_semantics.purpose: Replace a traffic classification filter node in network hardware offload module

Format is UNDEFINED (or falls through to that case)

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse and normalize authorization strings (authzTo values) in LDAP, handling multiple formats including DN patterns, group references, user IDs, and LDAP URLs.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted input strings to produce normalized authorization identifiers. The function allocates memory for normalized output and may free intermediate data structures.

vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'lud_dn' pointer was freed using 'ch_free()' in the cleanup section, but this pointer could have been reassigned to newly allocated memory from 'dnNormalize'/'dnPretty' earlier in the function. required_preconditions: Authorization string parsed as an LDAP URL

Function reaches cleanup section after successful normalization

fix.strategy: Use the same memory deallocator for all code paths that modify the pointer.
changed_operations: Replaced 'ch_free(ludp->lud_dn)' with 'slap_sl_free(ludp->lud_dn, ctx)' in cleanup section

functional_semantics.purpose: Perform elliptic curve scalar point multiplication (k * P) for cryptographic operations like ECDH key exchange.

vulnerability.abstract_cause: Non-constant-time implementation leaks secret scalar bits through control flow and memory access patterns.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The original Weierstrass curve multiplication used a double-and-add algorithm with conditional branches based on secret scalar bits, and lacked coordinate randomization for the starting point.
required_preconditions: Physical proximity for EM measurement
Use of Weierstrass curve model
Secret scalar not marked as secure

added_guards: Check if scalar is in secure memory for Weierstrass curves

Initialize result to neutral point (1,1,0) for Weierstrass
fix.post_fix_invariant: All curve models (Edwards, Montgomery, Weierstrass) use constant-time algorithms when processing secret scalars.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process network packets from a game server, handling various system messages including map changes, snapshots, and remote console commands.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses untrusted network data from a server, including fields that control memory writes (snapshot part data and sizes).

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving a malicious NETMSG_SNAP, NETMSG_SNAPSINGLE, or NETMSG_SNAPEMPTY packet with crafted NumParts, Part, or PartSize values.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of network-provided array/offset indices before using them in memory operations.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code used the server-controlled Part index and PartSize value in mem_copy without checking bounds against the destination buffer (m_aSnapshotIncommingData) and the MAX_SNAPSHOT_PACKSIZE constant. This could lead to out-of-bounds write.
required_preconditions: Client is in STATE_LOADING or later.
Server sends a snapshot packet with manipulated fields.

fix.strategy: Add comprehensive input validation before using the untrusted indices and sizes.
added_guards: Check NumParts is within [1, CSnapshot::MAX_PARTS].
Check Part is within [0, NumParts).
Check PartSize is within [0, MAX_SNAPSHOT_PACKSIZE].
changed_operations: Added a single conditional check combining all new validations, placed after Unpacker.GetRaw and before the mem_copy operation.
fix.post_fix_invariant: All server-controlled indices and sizes used in memory operations are validated against known bounds before use.

functional_semantics.purpose: XML deserialization handler for WDDX format, creating PHP data structures from XML elements.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses XML input containing boolean elements and creates corresponding PHP boolean values.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an empty boolean XML element (no 'value' attribute) during WDDX deserialization.

vulnerability.detailed_cause: When handling EL_BOOLEAN elements without attributes, the code path allocated a zval but did not properly initialize its value before pushing it onto the stack, leading to an invalid free later.
required_preconditions: WDDX deserialization enabled
Attacker-controlled XML input containing boolean element without value attribute

fix.strategy: Ensure consistent initialization of data structure before conditional branching.
changed_operations: Moved zval allocation and type initialization outside the conditional block for boolean handling
Used ZVAL_FALSE(ent.data) instead of ZVAL_FALSE(&ent.data) for consistency
fix.post_fix_invariant: The boolean entry's zval is always allocated and properly initialized (either with a value from attributes or FALSE) before being pushed onto the stack.

functional_semantics.purpose: The WriteOnePNGImage function writes a PNG image file, handling color space conversion, palette building, transparency processing, and PNG chunk generation.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function allocates memory for image processing and PNG structures. It uses setjmp/longjmp for error handling in libpng, which requires careful resource cleanup to avoid memory leaks.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PNG image file that causes an early failure path (e.g., during palette building or PNG structure allocation).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Memory leak due to missing resource cleanup in an error path.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When AcquireImageColormap fails (returns MagickFalse) during palette building, the function throws an exception but does not free the previously allocated image_info and image clones before returning.
required_preconditions: The image is being written as PNG8 or color-type 3 (palette-based).
The image has a colormap that is NULL or cannot be allocated (AcquireImageColormap fails).
The code path reaches the error check after attempting to acquire the colormap.

fix.strategy: Ensure proper cleanup of allocated resources before returning from the error path.
added_guards: Added cleanup of image_info and image clones via DestroyImageInfo and DestroyImage before returning MagickFalse.
changed_operations: Replaced ThrowWriterException with ThrowMagickException after destroying the cloned image resources.
Added explicit destruction of image_info and image in the error block.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If AcquireImageColormap fails, the cloned image and image_info are properly destroyed before the function returns, preventing memory leaks.

functional_semantics.purpose: Derive a unique key for a futex based on user address, distinguishing between private and shared mappings.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accesses page metadata (mapping, host inode) without sufficient synchronization, risking use-after-free.

vulnerability.abstract_cause: Race condition between checking page metadata and using it.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code accessed page->mapping and mapping->host without holding sufficient locks or using proper atomic/RCU patterns, allowing the underlying inode or page structure to be freed and reused.
required_preconditions: Shared futex (fshared=true)
File-backed mapping
Memory pressure or parallel truncation/hole-punching

fix.strategy: Use RCU protection and atomic reference counting for inode access, verify consistency of page->mapping before use.
added_guards: READ_ONCE(page->mapping) for atomic read
RCU read lock for inode access
atomic_inc_not_zero(&inode->i_count) to take a reference
Re-check page->mapping != mapping after RCU lock
changed_operations: Deferred page lock acquisition
Inode reference taken under RCU instead of relying on page lock
Added retry loops for inconsistent state
fix.post_fix_invariant: Inode accessed only after taking a reference via atomic_inc_not_zero under RCU protection; page->mapping validated before use.

functional_semantics.purpose: The function builds a sandboxed environment for a Flatpak application or runtime, preparing and executing a command within that sandbox.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function constructs a command line (via `bwrap`) to launch a sandboxed process. It processes caller-specified environment variables and passes them to the execution environment.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A malicious or compromised Flatpak app sets environment variables that are passed to the `flatpak run` command executing on the host system.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Untrusted environment variables from a sandboxed caller are passed to a host system command without sanitization.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The `flatpak-portal` service, when launching a new sandbox instance via `flatpak run`, passed environment variables from the sandboxed caller directly to the host's `flatpak run` command. These variables could contain values (like `LD_PRELOAD`) trusted by `flatpak run` to execute arbitrary code outside the sandbox.
required_preconditions: The attacker controls a sandboxed Flatpak application
The vulnerable `flatpak-portal` service is running
The service is used to launch a subprocess (e.g., via the portal's subprocess spawning functionality)

fix.strategy: Sanitize the environment before passing it to the host command by converting environment variables to explicit command-line arguments.
added_guards: A call to `flatpak_bwrap_envp_to_args(bwrap)` was inserted before bundling arguments for execution.
changed_operations: The environment vector (`envp`) is now explicitly converted to `--setenv` arguments for the bwrap command line, preventing arbitrary environment variables from the caller's context from being passed directly to the host's execution environment.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The environment seen by the executed host command (`flatpak run`) is now controlled and constructed from the sanitized argument list, not directly inherited from the untrusted caller's environment.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse a SASL authorization identity string (uauthzid) into its components: user, mechanism, and realm.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function modifies the input string in-place by inserting null terminators and shifting component pointers. It assumes the input buffer is writable and has sufficient space for pointer adjustments.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malformed SASL authorization identity string.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: An invalid pointer dereference leading to a free of uninitialized or incorrect memory.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function could leave the 'mech' pointer uninitialized (zeroed) when the input lacks a mechanism part (no '.' after 'u'). Later code paths that check '!BER_BVISNULL(mech)' could then operate on this invalid/zeroed pointer, leading to an invalid free.
required_preconditions: The input string does not contain a mechanism specifier (no '.' character after the leading 'u').
The code path that later frees or uses the 'mech' pointer is executed.

fix.strategy: Ensure the 'mech' and 'realm' output parameters are consistently initialized in all code paths before they are potentially used.
changed_operations: Explicitly zero the 'mech' pointer (BER_BVZERO) in the else branch where no mechanism is found, matching the existing zeroing of 'realm'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The 'mech' and 'realm' output parameters are always initialized (either to point to substrings or to zero/NULL) before the function returns, regardless of the input format.

functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses untrusted network data from remote access point, copies variable-length WMM parameter data into fixed-size kernel buffer.

WMM feature is enabled/used

fix.strategy: Add bounds check before copy operation.
added_guards: Compare (wmm_param_ie->vend_hdr.len + 2) against maximum allowed size (sizeof(struct ieee_types_wmm_parameter))
fix.post_fix_invariant: memcpy length argument never exceeds destination buffer size.

functional_semantics.purpose: Retrieve cookies from a cookie jar that apply to a given URI, handling expiration and HTTP-only flags.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates the host field of the input URI before processing. If validation fails, returns NULL instead of proceeding.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling the function with a URI containing an empty hostname string.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient validation of a string input allowed processing to proceed when the string was empty.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The check `if (!uri->host)` only verified the host pointer was non-NULL, but did not verify the string it pointed to was non-empty. An empty string ('\0' first character) passed this check.

The string pointed to by uri->host has a length of zero (first character is '\0').

fix.strategy: Strengthened the input validation guard to also check for an empty string.
added_guards: !uri->host[0]
changed_operations: Changed validation from `if (!uri->host)` to `if (!uri->host || !uri->host[0])`.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The function only proceeds if uri->host is both a non-NULL pointer and points to a non-empty string.

fix.strategy: Correct inverted comparison operator in length validation check

vulnerability.triggering_action: Concurrent context destruction operations
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use-after-free due to race condition between context lookup and removal
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The context was looked up without holding the IDR lock, then removed while another thread could access it
required_preconditions: Multiple threads operating on the same context
Concurrent context destruction calls

fix.strategy: Synchronize IDR removal with lookup by holding the IDR lock during the entire operation
added_guards: IDR lock acquisition before removal
IDR lock release after removal
changed_operations: Moved IDR removal to occur under lock protection
Removed separate context lookup function
fix.post_fix_invariant: Context removal from IDR is atomic and synchronized

functional_semantics.purpose: Decrypt and authenticate TLS/DTLS ciphertext records using CBC mode with HMAC.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes CBC padding and verifies the MAC (HMAC) to authenticate the record. The timing of the MAC verification and padding validation can leak information about the correctness of the MAC and padding.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malformed CBC-encrypted TLS/DTLS record with invalid padding or MAC.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Timing side-channel during the MAC verification and padding validation steps.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function performed MAC verification (memcmp) and padding byte validation in a variable-time manner. The execution time differed based on how many padding bytes were checked and whether the MAC comparison failed early. This allowed an attacker to statistically analyze timing differences to distinguish between invalid padding and an invalid MAC, ultimately leading to plaintext recovery (the 'Lucky Thirteen' attack).
required_preconditions: Use of TLS 1.1/1.2 or DTLS 1.0/1.2 with CBC-mode ciphersuites.
Network attacker capable of sending crafted packets and measuring response times.

fix.strategy: Make the timing of MAC verification and padding processing independent of the content of the received ciphertext.
added_guards: Added a minimum size check for ciphertext before decryption (tag_size+1).
changed_operations: Changed padding validation loop to always iterate over a fixed number of bytes (up to 256) from the ciphertext, using bitwise operations to accumulate failure state without branching.
Replaced the early-return on padding length check with a uniform failure path.
Added a dummy waiting operation (dummy_wait) to equalize timing before returning a decryption failure, ensuring the total processing time is constant regardless of failure cause.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The time taken to process any record (valid or invalid) is approximately constant, independent of the plaintext, padding values, or MAC correctness.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process a RemoteFX tile set message containing encoded image tiles, including quantization tables and tile data.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses a network packet containing variable-length fields (quantization values, tile data lengths) and uses those lengths to advance a stream pointer.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a maliciously crafted tile set message with invalid tile data length fields.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read due to insufficient validation of length fields before using them to calculate stream pointer positions.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function read tile data length fields (YLen, CbLen, CrLen) from the input stream and used them to advance the main stream pointer via Stream_Seek without verifying that the seek operation would stay within the stream's bounds. This could cause the stream pointer to move past the valid data, leading to out-of-bounds reads in subsequent operations.
required_preconditions: The attacker can supply or influence the tile set message data.
The message contains a tile with YLen, CbLen, or CrLen values that cause the calculated stream position to exceed the actual available data.

fix.strategy: Replace unconditional pointer advancement with bounded checks and use a substream for tile data parsing.
added_guards: Added a check that blockLen is at least 6 (header) + 13 (tile header fields) before proceeding.
Replaced Stream_Seek calls with Stream_SafeSeek calls that validate the seek does not exceed stream bounds.
Created a substream (wStream sub) for parsing tile data to isolate length validation.
changed_operations: Changed from reading blockType and blockLen from the main stream (s) to reading them from a newly initialized substream.
Changed from using Stream_Seek(s, tile->YLen) to if (!Stream_SafeSeek(&sub, tile->YLen)) { rc = FALSE; break; } (and similarly for CbLen, CrLen).
Added validation that Stream_GetRemainingLength(&sub) is sufficient for blockLen - 6 after reading the header.
fix.post_fix_invariant: All seek operations using length values read from the packet are validated to ensure they do not move the stream pointer beyond the available data. Tile data parsing is isolated within a substream bounded by the declared block length.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse XCF file header to extract version information
