Version string occupying full 14-byte buffer without null terminator

fix.strategy: Add null-termination check before accessing array element
added_guards: Check that id[13] == '\0' before processing version
changed_operations: Modified conditional from 'id[9] == 'v'' to 'id[9] == 'v' && id[13] == '\0''
fix.post_fix_invariant: Version parsing only occurs when the 14th byte contains null terminator

functional_semantics.purpose: Read and parse X Window Dump (XWD) image files, converting them to ImageMagick's internal format.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses file headers containing size fields, allocates memory based on those fields, and processes color-map entries.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted XWD file with a maliciously large 'ncolors' field in its header.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing integer overflow check before memory allocation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'header.ncolors' field from the file was cast to 'size_t' and used directly to calculate allocation size ('length * sizeof(*colors)') without verifying that the multiplication wouldn't overflow the maximum representable value.
required_preconditions: The attacker controls the 'ncolors' field in the XWD file header.
The value is large enough to cause 'length * sizeof(*colors)' to exceed SIZE_MAX.

fix.strategy: Add an explicit overflow check before the allocation.
added_guards: A check that 'length > ((~0UL)/sizeof(*colors))' to ensure the requested allocation size does not overflow.
changed_operations: Added a conditional throw if the overflow check fails, before the call to 'AcquireQuantumMemory'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The allocation size for the color-map array is guaranteed not to overflow the size_t type.

functional_semantics.purpose: Allocate and initialize SPI transfer structures and buffer for burst mode data acquisition
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates two kernel memory objects (adis->xfer array and adis->buffer) sequentially without proper cleanup if the second allocation fails

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling adis_update_scan_mode_burst() when kzalloc() fails but kcalloc() succeeded
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing cleanup of previously allocated resources during error handling
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function allocated adis->xfer with kcalloc() successfully, then attempted to allocate adis->buffer with kzalloc(). When kzalloc() failed, the function returned -ENOMEM without freeing the previously allocated adis->xfer
required_preconditions: kcalloc() succeeds
kzalloc() fails

fix.strategy: Add cleanup of previously allocated resources in the error path
added_guards: kfree(adis->xfer) when adis->buffer allocation fails
changed_operations: Set adis->xfer = NULL after freeing it in error path
fix.post_fix_invariant: If adis->buffer allocation fails, any previously allocated adis->xfer is freed before returning

functional_semantics.purpose: Update the Path MTU (PMTU) for an IPv6 route when receiving an ICMPv6 Packet Too Big message.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: When the reported MTU is less than the IPv6 minimum MTU (1280 bytes), the code sets the route's MTU to the minimum and enables fragmentation for packets sent via this route.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving a forged ICMPv6 Packet Too Big (PTB) message reporting an MTU smaller than 1280 bytes.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: The system unnecessarily enabled fragmentation in response to an invalid MTU report.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code responded to an ICMPv6 PTB message with an MTU < IPV6_MIN_MTU by setting the route MTU to IPV6_MIN_MTU AND setting the RTAX_FEATURE_ALLFRAG flag, which triggered the generation of IPv6 atomic fragments for all subsequent packets on that route.
required_preconditions: IPv6 is in use.
The system honors received ICMPv6 PTB messages.
The attacker can send a forged ICMPv6 PTB message to the target.

fix.strategy: Stop enabling fragmentation when adjusting the MTU to the minimum in response to an invalid ICMPv6 PTB message.
changed_operations: Removed the code that set the RTAX_FEATURE_ALLFRAG flag when mtu < IPV6_MIN_MTU.
fix.post_fix_invariant: Receiving an ICMPv6 PTB message with an MTU < IPV6_MIN_MTU will no longer cause the system to enable fragmentation for the affected route.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse PNG text chunks (tEXt, zTXt, iTXt) by extracting text data from chunk buffers
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted PNG file data containing variable-length fields without sufficient bounds checking before pointer arithmetic

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PNG image file with malformed text chunk data
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Heap-based buffer over-read due to insufficient validation of chunk size before accessing data
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Pointer arithmetic and memory accesses performed before verifying that the chunk buffer contains sufficient data for the expected structure
required_preconditions: Untrusted PNG input
Chunk size smaller than expected for its type
Code path reaches vulnerable pointer arithmetic

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds checks before performing pointer arithmetic and data accesses
added_guards: Size validation using Safe::add before accessing data
Explicit checks that computed sizes don't overflow
Validation that computed offsets don't exceed buffer bounds
changed_operations: Added enforce() calls for minimum size requirements
Replaced unsafe string construction with bounded string_from_unterminated
Added overflow checks for arithmetic operations
fix.post_fix_invariant: All pointer arithmetic and buffer accesses are preceded by validation that the operation stays within allocated buffer bounds

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode TIFF image data using libtiff library
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates buffer memory based on TIFF tile size for tiled images

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a TIFF image with tiled format
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in buffer size calculation leading to undersized allocation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: TIFFTileSize() returns a tsize_t value that may exceed INT_MAX, causing overflow when assigned to state->bytes (int type) and subsequent undersized realloc
required_preconditions: TIFF image uses tiled format
Tile size calculation exceeds INT_MAX

fix.strategy: Add overflow check before buffer allocation
added_guards: Check if tile size exceeds INT_MAX before assignment to int variable
changed_operations: Added overflow validation for TIFFTileSize() result
fix.post_fix_invariant: Tile size is validated to not overflow signed integer before buffer allocation

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse ISO 8601 date strings into time_t values, handling optional hyphen separators by removing them.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted input strings without validating that the string has sufficient length before accessing character offsets.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Passing a crafted ISO 8601 date string that is shorter than expected to functions like xmlrpc_set_type or xmlrpc_decode.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read due to insufficient input validation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function accesses character offsets (e.g., text[i+4], text[i+6]) using hardcoded indices without first verifying that the input string is long enough to contain those offsets.
required_preconditions: The input string contains a hyphen, triggering the hyphen-removal path, OR the input string lacks a hyphen, bypassing that path.
The string length is less than the maximum offset accessed (e.g., less than 16 characters for the seconds field at index 15).

fix.strategy: Add bounds checking for each character access and validate parsed field ranges.
added_guards: Changed the XMLRPC_IS_NUMBER macro invocations to check the correct offset (e.g., text[i+4] instead of text[i]) for month, day, hour, minute, and second fields.
Added a range check for the parsed month (tm.tm_mon) to ensure it is between 0 and 11 after decrementing.
changed_operations: Updated the index argument passed to XMLRPC_IS_NUMBER in multiple loops to match the actual character being used in the subsequent arithmetic.
fix.post_fix_invariant: Each character accessed for parsing is checked to be a digit, and the parsed month value is validated to be within the expected range.

functional_semantics.purpose: Look up or create a fragment queue in a hash table for IP fragment reassembly
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Manages reference counts and timer modifications while holding locks

vulnerability.triggering_action: Concurrent access to fragment hash table under heavy CPU load
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Race condition between adding to LRU list and releasing locks
vulnerability.detailed_cause: inet_frag_lru_add() called after spin_unlock() and read_unlock(), creating window where queue could be accessed/modified while being added to LRU
required_preconditions: SMP system
Heavy CPU load
Large series of fragmented ICMP Echo Request packets

fix.strategy: Move LRU addition inside critical section before releasing locks
changed_operations: Reordered inet_frag_lru_add() to execute before spin_unlock()
fix.post_fix_invariant: LRU list addition occurs while holding both hash bucket lock and read lock

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse X Window Dump (XWD) image files.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads and validates a file header containing image metadata, including a bitmap_bit_order field that specifies bit ordering (LSBFirst or MSBFirst).

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted XWD image file where the header's bitmap_bit_order field is set to a value that is neither LSBFirst nor MSBFirst.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of an enumeration field in untrusted input.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code did not check that the header.bitmap_bit_order field contained a valid value (MSBFirst or LSBFirst) before assigning it to ximage->bitmap_bit_order and later using it. This could lead to an integer division by zero elsewhere in the program (as indicated by the CWE-369 and CVE description).
required_preconditions: The attacker supplies a malicious XWD file.
The file's header passes other basic format checks.
The header's bitmap_bit_order field is set to an invalid value (not 0/MSBFirst or 1/LSBFirst).

fix.strategy: Add an explicit guard to reject invalid bitmap_bit_order values.
added_guards: A check that header.bitmap_bit_order is either MSBFirst or LSBFirst.
changed_operations: Added a validation step for the bitmap_bit_order field before proceeding with image initialization.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The bitmap_bit_order field in the XWD header is guaranteed to be a valid, expected value before being used in subsequent operations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize and attach device tree test case data during kernel boot for unit testing
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory for test case data, parses device tree structure, and attaches it to the live device tree

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling of_fdt_unflatten_tree() that returns NULL (fails to parse the device tree blob)
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Memory leak
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When of_fdt_unflatten_tree() fails and returns NULL, the function returns an error code without freeing the previously allocated 'unittest_data' buffer
required_preconditions: of_fdt_unflatten_tree() must fail
kmemdup() must have succeeded earlier

fix.strategy: Add cleanup for allocated memory before returning from error path
added_guards: kfree(unittest_data) before returning -ENODATA when unittest_data_node is NULL
changed_operations: Added memory deallocation in the error return path
fix.post_fix_invariant: All dynamically allocated memory is freed before returning from error conditions

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse Ogg XiphComment metadata from binary data
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads length fields from untrusted input to allocate memory and copy data

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted Ogg file with manipulated vendorLength field
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer type mismatch enabling out-of-bounds read
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Using signed int for vendorLength allows negative values to bypass bounds checking, leading to buffer overflow
required_preconditions: Untrusted input source
No validation of length field sign

fix.strategy: Change variable type to enforce unsigned interpretation
changed_operations: Changed vendorLength from int to uint
fix.post_fix_invariant: Length fields are always interpreted as unsigned integers

functional_semantics.purpose: State machine handling network connections and data reading/writing for memcached.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes incoming network packets, including parsing command headers and reading variable-length data bodies.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving a packet with a large body length value.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer signedness error leading to negative length being interpreted as large positive value.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'rlbytes' field (remaining bytes to read) was a signed integer. When set to a large value from network data, it could become negative due to overflow/wrapping, but was treated as unsigned in comparisons and operations.
required_preconditions: Binary protocol is used
Attacker can send crafted packets

fix.strategy: Add explicit validation check before using the length value.
added_guards: Check if rlbytes < 0 and close connection if true
changed_operations: Added validation before buffer copy operations
fix.post_fix_invariant: rlbytes must be non-negative before being used as a length parameter.

functional_semantics.purpose: Handles session-based upload progress tracking for multipart form data processing.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Manages cleanup of upload progress data when session.upload_progress.cleanup is disabled.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A file upload fails while upload progress tracking is enabled with session.upload_progress.cleanup disabled.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Null pointer dereference during cleanup of non-existent upload progress data.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When upload fails, the cleanup path attempts to access and modify progress->data without checking if it was initialized.
required_preconditions: Upload progress tracking enabled
session.upload_progress.cleanup set to 0 (disabled)
File upload failure occurs

fix.strategy: Add guard condition to check if progress data was initialized before attempting cleanup operations.
added_guards: Check !Z_ISUNDEF(progress->data) before SEPARATE_ARRAY and related operations
changed_operations: Wrapped cleanup operations in MULTIPART_EVENT_END case with Z_ISUNDEF check
fix.post_fix_invariant: Progress data cleanup only occurs if the data structure was properly initialized.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse NE (New Executable) file format entry point table to extract executable entry addresses.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes variable-length bundle structures from a binary entry table, reading bytes and words at calculated offsets without bounds checking.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Reading from bin->entry_table at offsets derived from untrusted data (bundle_length, bundle_type, segnum) without validating that the offset remains within the allocated buffer.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check before accessing array or buffer.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The loop processes an entry table by reading a bundle_length byte, then iterates bundle_length times, each iteration advancing the offset (off) by reading and skipping bytes. The offset can advance beyond the allocated entry_table buffer, leading to out-of-bounds read when accessing bin->entry_table + off.
required_preconditions: The input NE file has a malformed or crafted entry table where the sum of bundle lengths and skipped bytes exceeds the actual EntryTableLength or the underlying buffer size.
The entry_table pointer points to a heap-allocated buffer.

fix.strategy: Add a guard condition before reading each bundle to ensure sufficient data remains in the underlying buffer.
added_guards: Check if bin->entry_table + off + 32 is >= r_buf_size(bin->buf) before reading bundle_length and bundle_type.
changed_operations: Added a bounds check at the start of the while loop's iteration.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The offset 'off' is guaranteed not to advance beyond the available buffer data when reading the bundle header fields.

functional_semantics.purpose: Compute a hash key for XML qualified names using prefix and name strings
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accesses character arrays using computed offsets without bounds checking

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling the function with specific prefix length (plen) and name length (len) values that cause negative array offset calculation
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer arithmetic underflow leading to out-of-bounds array access
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The expression 'len - (plen + 1 + 1)' can produce a negative value when plen is large relative to len, resulting in access to memory before the name array
required_preconditions: plen parameter value causes len - (plen + 2) to be negative
name parameter points to a valid array

fix.strategy: Add bounds checking to prevent negative offset calculation
added_guards: Check if offset calculation results in negative value before array access
changed_operations: Replaced direct offset calculation with conditional logic: if (offset < 0) offset = len - (10 + 1)
fix.post_fix_invariant: Array offset is guaranteed to be non-negative before access

functional_semantics.purpose: Save a potential simple key token during YAML parsing
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Asserts that a required simple key is only considered when simple keys are allowed

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing YAML input with line-wrapping
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Invalid assumption about parser state invariants
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Assertion that parser->simple_key_allowed must be true when required is true failed under certain line-wrapping conditions
required_preconditions: Parser in block context
Current column matches indentation level
Line-wrapping in input

fix.strategy: Remove the assertion that was found to be incorrect
changed_operations: Assertion commented out
fix.post_fix_invariant: Parser continues execution without crashing when the assertion would have failed

functional_semantics.purpose: Write audio sample data to a WAV file, converting floating-point samples to integer format based on bits-per-sample setting.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates a temporary conversion buffer for sample format transformation before writing to file.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing 24-bit audio samples (bytesPerSample == 3) with buffer size calculation that could be insufficient.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient buffer allocation for type-punning operation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The buffer size calculation '(numBytes + 3) & -4' rounds up to nearest multiple of 4, but the 24-bit sample processing writes 4 bytes via '*((int*)temp2) = _swap32(value)' while advancing pointer by only 3 bytes, potentially causing buffer overflow on final iteration.
required_preconditions: Processing 24-bit audio samples
Number of elements requires buffer allocation at boundary condition

fix.strategy: Increase buffer allocation padding to ensure safe 4-byte writes for 24-bit samples.
changed_operations: Changed buffer size calculation from '(numBytes + 3) & -4' to 'numBytes + 7'
fix.post_fix_invariant: Allocated buffer is at least 7 bytes larger than needed for sample data, ensuring 4-byte writes cannot overflow even for 24-bit samples.

functional_semantics.purpose: Write an image in MSL (Magick Scripting Language) format by cloning the input image and processing it with a script.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Creates a cloned image object but does not properly destroy it before returning, leading to resource retention.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Writing an image in MSL format.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Failure to release allocated resources (memory) before function return.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The cloned image object (msl_image) is not destroyed after ProcessMSLScript completes, causing a memory leak.
required_preconditions: MSL image writing is invoked.
CloneImage succeeds in creating a new image object.

fix.strategy: Explicitly destroy the cloned image object after use and before returning.
changed_operations: Added call to DestroyImageList on msl_image after ProcessMSLScript.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The cloned image object is always destroyed before the function returns, regardless of the success or failure of ProcessMSLScript.

functional_semantics.purpose: Error handling function that catches exceptions, formats error messages with source code context, and populates error information in a context structure.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes exception data including source code pointers to generate formatted error output. Accesses potentially untrusted source code data from exception objects.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an exception containing source code position data where the source pointer is null or invalid.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read when accessing source code buffer without validating pointer validity.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function attempted to read from e.pstate.src pointer without checking if it was null before performing pointer arithmetic and character iteration operations.
required_preconditions: An exception is thrown with pstate.src set to null or invalid pointer
The exception contains valid line and column values
The error handling code path reaches the source code formatting section

fix.strategy: Add null check before accessing source pointer to prevent dereferencing invalid memory.
added_guards: Check that e.pstate.src != nullptr before processing source code
changed_operations: Added null check condition to existing line/column validation
Changed pointer iteration logic from while loops to for loops with null terminator checks
fix.post_fix_invariant: Source pointer is validated before any dereference or pointer arithmetic operations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Select text inside matching quote characters (like 'i"' or 'a"' motion in Vim).
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function processes a line buffer and iterates over character positions to find quote boundaries. It assumes the line buffer is null-terminated and that iteration indices stay within valid bounds.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Performing a visual text-object motion (like vi' or va') on a line where the visual selection's end column is beyond the actual line length (e.g., because the line was shortened after the visual area was selected).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: A loop iterating over a buffer without checking for the buffer's end (null terminator) within the loop body.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The while loop `while (i <= col_end) if (line[i++] == quotechar) ...` increments `i` and accesses `line[i]` without verifying that `i` is still a valid index (i.e., that `line[i]` is not the null terminator). If `col_end` is >= the string length, the loop reads past the end of the string.
required_preconditions: A visual selection exists on the current line (`!vis_empty`).
The visual selection's end column (`col_end`) is greater than or equal to the length of the current line (i.e., points to or beyond the null terminator).
This state can occur if the line buffer was modified (shortened) after the visual area was initially selected but before the text-object motion is invoked.

fix.strategy: Add an explicit bounds check inside the iteration loop to stop if the end of the string is reached.
added_guards: A check `if (line[i] == NUL) break;` before the quote comparison inside the while loop.
changed_operations: The loop structure changed from a single-statement while to a block, with the null-check inserted before the character comparison.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The loop now guarantees that `line[i]` is accessed only when `i` is a valid index (pointing to a character before the null terminator).

functional_semantics.purpose: Read data and file descriptors from a socket using Unix fd passing mechanism.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes incoming file descriptors, validates count against limit, and must properly close excess or truncated descriptors to prevent resource exhaustion.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving a message where control data (file descriptors) is truncated (MSG_CTRUNC flag set).
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Resource leak due to failure to clean up partially received resources during error handling.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When MSG_CTRUNC indicates truncated control data, the error path returned without closing file descriptors that were already successfully received and stored in the output buffer.
required_preconditions: Unix fd passing support
Malicious or malformed message causing control data truncation
Access to send messages to the target service

fix.strategy: Ensure all acquired resources are released before returning from error path.
changed_operations: Added loop to close already-received file descriptors before returning error when MSG_CTRUNC is detected
fix.post_fix_invariant: All successfully received file descriptors are closed when control data truncation occurs, preventing file descriptor leak.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse Visual Basic for Applications (VBA) project strings from a file to identify and process specific string patterns.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Dynamically allocates and reallocates a buffer for reading data, and frees memory in multiple conditional branches.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A second call to free() on the same buffer pointer.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Failure to nullify a pointer after freeing the memory it points to in one execution path.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: In the branch where 'read_uint16' fails, the code frees 'buf' but does not set 'buf' to NULL. The function later reaches the loop's end or a 'break', where 'if(buf) free(buf)' executes again.
required_preconditions: The function enters the loop.
'read_uint16' fails after a buffer has been allocated and the 'name' check has passed.

fix.strategy: Ensure the buffer pointer is set to NULL immediately after being freed in the vulnerable branch to prevent a subsequent redundant free.
added_guards: Setting 'buf = NULL;' after 'free(buf);' in the specific failure branch.
changed_operations: The 'free(buf);' operation in the 'read_uint16' failure branch was extended to also assign NULL to 'buf'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: After 'buf' is freed in any branch within the loop, its pointer is set to NULL, guaranteeing the cleanup at the function's end will not double-free it.

functional_semantics.purpose: Read BMP image files, parsing headers and pixel data to create an internal image representation.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory buffers based on calculated image dimensions and compression type, then reads file data into those buffers.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted BMP file with manipulated header fields.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in buffer size calculation leading to insufficient memory allocation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The calculation `(size_t) image->rows * MagickMax(bytes_per_line, image->columns+256UL) * sizeof(*pixels)` could overflow when `image->rows` is large, causing `AcquireVirtualMemory` to allocate a buffer smaller than expected. Subsequent `ReadBlob` operations write beyond the allocated buffer bounds.
required_preconditions: Malformed BMP header with large image height value
Compression type BI_RGB or BI_BITFIELDS

fix.strategy: Prevent integer overflow by separating the multiplication operations.
changed_operations: Changed `AcquireVirtualMemory((size_t) image->rows, MagickMax(bytes_per_line, image->columns+256UL) * sizeof(*pixels))` to `AcquireVirtualMemory(image->rows, MagickMax(bytes_per_line, image->columns+256UL) * sizeof(*pixels))` (removed cast)
fix.post_fix_invariant: Buffer allocation size calculation avoids integer overflow by letting the memory allocation function handle the row count multiplication internally.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process group membership SIDs to identify valid POSIX groups and missing groups requiring download.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Determines which groups are considered valid for access control decisions based on cached group information.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a group membership chain containing a non-POSIX group.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect filtering of group types during membership resolution.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function skipped non-POSIX groups when found in cache, but this filtering was not applied consistently when groups were downloaded and processed later, allowing non-POSIX groups in chains to bypass access restrictions.
required_preconditions: Group membership chain contains non-POSIX group
System uses group membership for access control

fix.strategy: Remove early filtering of non-POSIX groups at cache lookup stage, deferring proper handling to later stages.
changed_operations: Removed SYSDB_POSIX attribute from query
Removed check for is_posix != NULL && strcmp(is_posix, "FALSE") == 0
fix.post_fix_invariant: All groups in cache are processed regardless of POSIX attribute at this stage.

functional_semantics.purpose: Cache user credentials for offline authentication when automatic ticket renewal and offline authentication are configured.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Stores authentication tokens (passwords) in system database for later offline use. During ticket renewal, the authentication token contains a credential cache pathname rather than the actual password.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Automatic Kerberos ticket renewal with offline authentication configured.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect credential material stored during authentication state transition.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: During ticket renewal operations (SSS_CMD_RENEW), the authentication token (pd->authtok) contains a pathname to the credential cache file rather than the user's actual password. This pathname was being cached as the password for offline authentication.
required_preconditions: Automatic ticket renewal enabled
Offline authentication configured
System configured to cache passwords for offline use

fix.strategy: Exclude renewal operations from password caching to prevent storing incorrect credential material.
added_guards: Explicit check for SSS_CMD_RENEW command before caching password
Conditional debug message only for non-renewal operations when password is null
changed_operations: Removed SSS_CMD_RENEW from cases that trigger password caching
Added explicit break for SSS_CMD_RENEW case
fix.post_fix_invariant: Credential cache pathnames are never stored as passwords during ticket renewal operations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize an X Output Method (XOM) object by loading font set configuration resources and building required data structures.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accumulates string lengths from font data names to allocate a buffer for storing concatenated names.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Integer overflow when accumulating string lengths leads to undersized buffer allocation.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Signed integer overflow in length accumulation variable.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The variable 'length' (declared as signed int) accumulates strlen() results across multiple iterations. If the total exceeds INT_MAX, it overflows to a negative value, causing Xmalloc() to allocate insufficient memory.
required_preconditions: Controlled or malicious font configuration data
Accumulated string lengths exceeding INT_MAX

fix.strategy: Change variable type to unsigned integer to prevent signed overflow.
changed_operations: Changed 'length' variable type from 'int' to 'unsigned int'
fix.post_fix_invariant: Length accumulation cannot overflow to negative values; unsigned overflow wraps modulo 2^N but allocation size remains consistent with accumulated byte count.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse XML data in chunks, handling leftover data between buffers
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory for leftover XML data when buffer needs expansion

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing XML input where buffer expansion calculation overflows
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in buffer size calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Signed integer multiplication (len * 2) can overflow when len is large
required_preconditions: XML_CONTEXT_BYTES not defined
bufferPtr equals bufferEnd
nLeftOver > bufferLim - buffer
Large len value causing overflow

fix.strategy: Convert to unsigned multiplication and validate result fits in signed type
added_guards: Check if bytesToAllocate > 0 before allocation
changed_operations: Changed len * 2 to (unsigned)len * 2U
Added intermediate unsigned calculation
fix.post_fix_invariant: Buffer allocation size calculation uses unsigned arithmetic to prevent overflow

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode PCD image format using Huffman tables for luminance and chrominance data.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory for Huffman tables, processes image data, and handles corrupted input by throwing exceptions.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a PCD image with an invalid plane value in the default switch case.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Memory leak due to missing resource cleanup before error exit.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When the default case in the plane switch statement is triggered (invalid plane value), the function throws an exception without first freeing previously allocated Huffman tables (pcd_table) and buffer memory.
required_preconditions: Image processing reaches the plane determination code
Image data contains an invalid plane value (not 0, 2, or 3)
Huffman tables have been successfully allocated earlier in the function

fix.strategy: Ensure resource cleanup occurs before throwing exception in error path.
changed_operations: Added memory deallocation for pcd_table array and buffer in the default case of the plane switch statement before throwing exception
fix.post_fix_invariant: All allocated memory (pcd_table arrays and buffer) is properly freed before function exit, whether through successful return or error exception.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process HTTP requests for a web application
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Generates HTTP response headers

vulnerability.triggering_action: Rendering web application content in an iframe
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing security header
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Absence of X-Frame-Options header in HTTP responses
required_preconditions: Web application serves content
Attacker can embed application in iframe

fix.strategy: Add security header to prevent framing
added_guards: X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN header
changed_operations: Header insertion added to response generation
fix.post_fix_invariant: All responses include X-Frame-Options header

functional_semantics.purpose: Fetch a row of data from a prepared statement result set in a database driver
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Handles BLOB/TEXT column data by reallocating buffers when fetched data exceeds initial allocation

vulnerability.triggering_action: Fetching BLOB/TEXT column data that exceeds initial buffer allocation in server-side prepared statements
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use-after-free due to inconsistent state between data structures

Check if pos exceeds data size during iteration
Check for malformed comment format

functional_semantics.purpose: Write an image in GIF format, handling colormaps, transparency, and various GIF extensions.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates two memory buffers (global_colormap and colormap) for GIF encoding. If either allocation fails, the function must clean up any successfully allocated buffer before throwing an exception.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted file that causes one of the two memory allocations to fail while the other succeeds.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing cleanup of partially allocated resources in an error path.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When the check `if ((global_colormap == (unsigned char *) NULL) || (colormap == (unsigned char *) NULL))` triggered an exception, the code did not free the other buffer that might have been successfully allocated. This resulted in a memory leak of either the global_colormap or colormap buffer.
required_preconditions: The function attempts to allocate two separate memory buffers.
The first allocation succeeds but the second fails, or vice versa.
The error path throws an exception without cleaning up the successfully allocated buffer.

fix.strategy: Add conditional cleanup before throwing the exception to free any buffer that was successfully allocated.
added_guards: Before throwing the ResourceLimitError exception, check if global_colormap is not NULL and free it.
Before throwing the ResourceLimitError exception, check if colormap is not NULL and free it.
changed_operations: Replaced a direct ThrowWriterException call with a block that performs cleanup then throws.
fix.post_fix_invariant: If either memory allocation fails, all previously allocated buffers in that allocation block are freed before the function exits via exception.

functional_semantics.purpose: Compute bidirectional text embedding levels according to Unicode Bidirectional Algorithm.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes arrays of character types and bracket types to determine text directionality levels, used for layout in applications like GNOME/GTK+ text rendering.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing crafted text content containing bidirectional formatting characters.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Buffer overflow due to insufficient bounds checking when incrementing isolate level counter.

required_preconditions: Input contains bidirectional isolate formatting characters (FSI, LRI, RLI)
Isolate nesting exceeds or approaches array size limit

fix.strategy: Add bounds check before array access and conditional increment.
added_guards: Check isolate_level < FRIBIDI_BIDI_MAX_EXPLICIT_LEVEL-1 before incrementing
changed_operations: Moved isolate_level increment to after bounds check
Array access uses post-increment value only when bounds check passes
fix.post_fix_invariant: isolate_level index never exceeds array bounds when accessing base_level_per_iso_level

functional_semantics.purpose: Read and render a text caption into an image using the Pango text layout library.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function processes user-provided image metadata (filename or option) to generate a caption string, which is then parsed and rendered. It allocates memory for the image surface based on calculated dimensions.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling SetImageProperty with a NULL property pointer.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing NULL check before using a pointer returned from a function.

The returned NULL value is used without validation.

fix.strategy: Add a NULL check before using the returned pointer.

fix.strategy: Add a NULL check before using the potentially NULL return value.
added_guards: A check 'if (label != (char *) NULL)' was added before calling SetImageProperty and DestroyString.
changed_operations: The unconditional calls to SetImageProperty and DestroyString were moved inside the new NULL-check guard.
fix.post_fix_invariant: SetImageProperty is only called with a non-NULL label string.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse Type 1 charstring bytecode to build glyph outlines.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Interprets a bytecode stream containing operators and operands, maintains a stack, handles subroutine calls, and manages a flex feature state machine for constructing curves.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malformed font charstring where the 'add flex vectors' othersubr (case 2) is invoked, but intermediate opcodes prevent the 'num_flex_vectors' counter from reaching the expected value before an outline point addition is attempted.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of internal builder state before performing an operation that assumes sufficient capacity.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: In the 'add flex vectors' handler (others case 2), the code increments 'num_flex_vectors' and, for certain index values, calls 't1_builder_add_point'. However, if other opcodes appear between flex operations, 'num_flex_vectors' may not be incremented, but the point addition still proceeds without checking if the builder has room for a new point.
required_preconditions: A font file containing a Type 1 charstring using the flex feature (callothersubr with subr_no 1, then 2).
The charstring includes opcodes between flex operations that do not increment 'num_flex_vectors'.
The builder's point array is near its capacity.

fix.strategy: Add a capacity check before adding a point in the flex vector handler.
added_guards: A call to 't1_builder_check_points(builder, 1)' before 't1_builder_add_point' in the 'add flex vectors' case.
changed_operations: Wrapped the point addition in the flex vector handler (case 2) with a check for available point capacity.
fix.post_fix_invariant: When adding a point during flex feature processing, the builder is first checked to ensure it has capacity for at least one additional point.

The SQL type parameter indicates a numeric type.
The formatted error message exceeds 63 characters plus null terminator.

fix.strategy: Replace unsafe fixed-buffer sprintf with dynamic string construction.
changed_operations: Changed err_msg from a fixed char array to a pointer.
Replaced sprintf call with dynamic allocation using newSVpvf and SvPVX.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The error message string is allocated with sufficient size for its content.

Ability to connect a malicious USB device
Device descriptor with invalid endpoints configuration

fix.strategy: Add comprehensive validation of USB endpoint data structures before any access
added_guards: Check serial->num_port_pointers against required count
Verify serial->port[i] elements exist
Validate read_urb and write_urb pointers in each port
changed_operations: Added early validation loop before any port access
Changed return behavior to -ENODEV on validation failure
fix.post_fix_invariant: All port array accesses and urb pointer dereferences occur only after verifying array bounds and pointer validity

functional_semantics.purpose: Discover and initialize a SAS expander device connected to a parent device's PHY.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates and adds resources (port, rphy, device) to kernel data structures. If subsequent discovery fails, it must clean up all allocated resources to prevent leaks.

vulnerability.triggering_action: The function sas_discover_expander(child) returns a non-zero error code.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Resource leak due to incomplete cleanup on an error path.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When sas_discover_expander fails, the cleanup code deletes the rphy, removes the child from the dev_list, and puts the child device reference. However, it omits deleting the sas_port (phy->port) that was allocated and added earlier in the function.
required_preconditions: A SAS expander device discovery attempt fails after its port and rphy have been successfully allocated and registered.

fix.strategy: Extend the existing error cleanup path to include deletion of the previously allocated and added sas_port.
changed_operations: Added sas_port_delete(phy->port); and phy->port = NULL; to the error cleanup block.
fix.post_fix_invariant: On the error path, all resources allocated in the function (child device, rphy, and port) are properly released.

functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates user permissions, copies user data to kernel, validates parameters, and frees allocated memory on error paths

functional_semantics.purpose: Construct TLS 1.3 pre-shared key extension data for ClientHello, handling both resumption tickets and external PSK credentials.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Computes and appends cryptographic binders (authentication tags) for PSK identities, stores derived keys in session state, and manages temporary key material.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A use-after-free occurs when the function's cleanup path frees a key datum that was already moved into session->key.binders array.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Double-free or use-after-free of a heap-allocated key buffer due to aliased ownership.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function transfers ownership of a key buffer (rkey or user_key) to the session's binder array by setting the key's data pointer to NULL, but the cleanup block still calls a freeing function on the same datum, which now has a NULL data pointer but may have been partially freed or accessed elsewhere.
required_preconditions: The function reaches the cleanup label after a key buffer has been assigned to session->key.binders[].psk.
The key datum's data pointer was set to NULL after the assignment, but the datum structure itself is still passed to a freeing function.
The freeing function does not properly handle a datum with a NULL data pointer, or the buffer was already freed elsewhere.

fix.strategy: Eliminate the ownership transfer pattern by not setting the key's data pointer to NULL after assignment to the session structure, allowing the cleanup function to safely free only if the key still owns the buffer.
changed_operations: Removed the lines that set rkey.data = NULL and user_key.data = NULL after assigning them to session->key.binders[].psk.data.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The cleanup function _gnutls_free_temp_key_datum will free the key buffer only if it still belongs to the local datum variable, avoiding double-free.

functional_semantics.purpose: USB Abstract Control Model (ACM) driver probe function that initializes USB CDC ACM devices (e.g., USB serial adapters).

Missing validation of interface pointers obtained from USB descriptor indices can lead to NULL pointer dereference.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Physically proximate attacker connects a malicious USB device lacking proper control or data endpoint descriptors.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: NULL pointer dereference due to insufficient validation of interface pointers obtained from USB descriptor indices.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When handling the NO_UNION_NORMAL quirk path, the code calls usb_ifnum_to_if() to obtain interface pointers but proceeds to use them without checking if they are NULL. A malicious USB device can provide descriptor indices that don't correspond to valid interfaces.
required_preconditions: USB device with NO_UNION_NORMAL quirk flag set
Device descriptor indices 0 or 1 don't correspond to valid interfaces
Device lacks proper control or data endpoint descriptors

fix.strategy: Add explicit NULL check after obtaining interface pointers in the quirk-handling path before proceeding.
added_guards: NULL check for data_interface and control_interface pointers after usb_ifnum_to_if() calls in NO_UNION_NORMAL quirk path
changed_operations: Added validation: if (!data_interface || !control_interface) return -ENODEV;
fix.post_fix_invariant: Interface pointers obtained from USB descriptor indices are validated before use in all code paths.

functional_semantics.purpose: Perform memory copy between local user-space buffer and remote hypervisor partition memory via an ioctl interface.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parses regular expression patterns by tokenizing input characters, handling escape sequences, and recognizing special syntax elements like quantifiers, character classes, anchors, and backreferences.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A NULL pointer dereference occurs when the function returns an error code (e.g., ONIGERR_INVALID_GROUP_NAME) and the caller (onig_error_code_to_str) attempts to use a NULL pointer from the environment.

fix.post_fix_invariant: When returning error codes that may be processed by onig_error_code_to_str, the scanning environment contains properly initialized error string pointers to prevent NULL dereferences.

functional_semantics.purpose: Retrieve a property value from an image or image info structure based on a property name string.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function dereferences the 'image' pointer in multiple property-specific code paths without first verifying that 'image' is non-NULL for those specific cases.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling GetMagickProperty with a property string that requires accessing the 'image' parameter (e.g., "interlace", "profile:icc", "profiles") while passing a NULL image pointer.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing NULL pointer guard for a specific input case within a larger function that has a general NULL check.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function's top-level logic asserts that either 'image' or 'image_info' is non-NULL, and it contains a general debug-logging check for 'image' being NULL. However, individual property-handling case blocks (e.g., for 'interlace', 'profile:icc', 'profiles') directly dereference 'image' fields (e.g., image->interlace) without first checking if 'image' is NULL for that specific property path.
required_preconditions: The 'image' parameter is NULL.
The 'image_info' parameter is non-NULL.
The 'property' string matches a case that directly accesses 'image' fields (e.g., "interlace", "profile:icc", "profiles").
The property string is longer than a single character (so the single-letter property handler is not used).

fix.strategy: Add missing NULL checks for the 'image' parameter at the beginning of each property-specific code block that dereferences 'image'.
added_guards: Added WarnNoImageReturn macro call before dereferencing 'image' in the 'interlace' property case.
Added WarnNoImageReturn macro call before dereferencing 'image' in the 'profile:icc'/'profile:icm' property case block.
Added WarnNoImageReturn macro call before dereferencing 'image' in the 'profiles' property case block.
changed_operations: Inserted WarnNoImageReturn("\"%%[%s]\"", property) in the 'interlace' case before accessing image->interlace.
Inserted WarnNoImageReturn("\"%%[%s]\"", property) in the 'profile:icc'/'profile:icm' case before calling GetImageProfile.
Inserted WarnNoImageReturn("\"%%[%s]\"", property) in the 'profiles' case before calling ResetImageProfileIterator.

functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory for PAM responses, some of which are passed to external PAM library for deallocation

vulnerability.abstract_cause: Null pointer dereference due to missing validation of array index and structure field

functional_semantics.purpose: Read and decode MATLAB .mat image files, handling various data types, compression, and multi-dimensional matrices.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses a complex binary format with multiple nested structures, allocates memory based on file-supplied dimensions, and may create temporary decompressed image objects.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted MATLAB file that triggers an unsupported cell type error.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use-after-free due to incorrect cleanup logic when an error occurs.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: In the error handling path for an unsupported cell type, the code attempts to close and delete a secondary image object (image2) without ensuring it is distinct from the primary image object (image). This can lead to accessing a freed object if image2 == image.
required_preconditions: The file triggers the unsupported cell type check.
The secondary image object (image2) points to the same object as the primary image (image).

fix.strategy: Add a guard to only close and delete the secondary image object if it is not the same as the primary image object.
added_guards: if ((image2 != (Image*) NULL) && (image2 != image))
changed_operations: Conditional cleanup of image2
fix.post_fix_invariant: The secondary image object is only destroyed if it exists and is distinct from the primary image object, preventing use-after-free.

functional_semantics.purpose: The phpinfo() function displays configuration and environment information about the PHP runtime.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function prints the values of certain PHP variables (PHP_SELF, PHP_AUTH_TYPE, PHP_AUTH_USER, PHP_AUTH_PW) from the symbol table. These variables can contain sensitive information like authentication credentials.

vulnerability.triggering_action: An attacker accesses the phpinfo() output page.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Type confusion leading to information disclosure.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code assumed that specific variables in the symbol table were of string type. If an attacker could cause these variables to be stored as a different type (e.g., integer), the code would incorrectly interpret the memory as a string pointer, potentially printing adjacent memory contents.
required_preconditions: The phpinfo() page is accessible.

The attacker can influence the type of the target variables (PHP_SELF, PHP_AUTH_TYPE, PHP_AUTH_USER, PHP_AUTH_PW) in the symbol table, possibly through other request parameters or server configuration.

fix.strategy: Add a type check before using the variable's value.
added_guards: A check that the zval's type is IS_STRING (Z_TYPE_PP(data) == IS_STRING) was added before dereferencing it as a string.
changed_operations: The hash table lookup operations for the four sensitive variables were modified to include the type guard.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The value is only printed if the variable exists in the symbol table *and* is of the expected string type.

functional_semantics.purpose: Finalize XML/HTML markup parsing and validate document structure completeness
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Handles end-of-parse validation for various incomplete document states, including error reporting

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling g_markup_parse_context_end_parse() when parser is in specific close-tag states
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing null check before dereferencing context->tag_stack
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function current_element(context) dereferences context->tag_stack without checking if it's NULL in close-tag error cases
required_preconditions: Parser state is STATE_AFTER_CLOSE_TAG_SLASH, STATE_INSIDE_CLOSE_TAG_NAME, or STATE_AFTER_CLOSE_TAG_NAME
context->tag_stack is NULL

fix.strategy: Add conditional check before calling current_element() in close-tag error cases
added_guards: if (context->tag_stack != NULL)
changed_operations: Split error reporting into two cases: with and without valid tag_stack
fix.post_fix_invariant: current_element() is only called when context->tag_stack is non-NULL

functional_semantics.purpose: Transmit network packets using DMA descriptors
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Checks available space in transmit descriptor ring buffer before queuing packets

vulnerability.triggering_action: Sending network traffic continuously for approximately ten minutes
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient buffer space check
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The space check after queue stop used num_frag instead of num_frag+1, potentially allowing queue wake-up with insufficient space
required_preconditions: Network device active
Heavy traffic load
Transmit descriptor ring near capacity

fix.strategy: Consistent buffer space calculation
changed_operations: Changed second temac_check_tx_bd_space call parameter from num_frag to num_frag+1
fix.post_fix_invariant: Both space checks use the same fragment count calculation

functional_semantics.purpose: Validate that a file path does not refer to a reserved Windows name (like .git) in a way that could bypass security checks.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function checks if a given path starts with a reserved name (e.g., '.git') and then examines subsequent characters to determine if the path is safe (returns true) or should be rejected (returns false).

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a file path that contains a reserved name followed by a colon character.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incomplete validation of path separators and stream specifiers after a reserved name.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The original validation only rejected paths where the character immediately after the reserved name was a backslash ('\\'). It did not reject paths where that character was a colon (':'), which on NTFS can denote an Alternate Data Stream.
required_preconditions: The system is Windows or uses an NTFS-like filesystem.
The path contains a reserved name (e.g., '.git').
The reserved name is immediately followed by a colon character.

fix.strategy: Extend the validation guard to cover an additional dangerous character.
added_guards: Check if the character immediately after the reserved name is a colon (':') and reject the path if true.
changed_operations: The condition `if (path[start] == '\\')` was changed to `if (path[start] == '\\' || path[start] == ':')`.
fix.post_fix_invariant: A path starting with a reserved name is rejected if the next character is either a backslash (directory separator) or a colon (NTFS stream separator).

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse IMAP sequence sets containing comma-separated ranges
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Iterates through sequence numbers, modifying input string by replacing delimiters with null terminators

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an IMAP sequence set ending with a comma
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When substr_end points to a comma delimiter, the code writes null terminator but doesn't advance substr_end past it, causing next iteration to read beyond string boundary
required_preconditions: $imap_qresync feature enabled
IMAP sequence set ends with comma

fix.strategy: Ensure string pointer advances past replaced delimiter
changed_operations: Changed substr_end null termination to increment pointer: *(iter->substr_end++) = '\0'
fix.post_fix_invariant: substr_end always points to valid position after null terminator replacement

functional_semantics.purpose: Compute bidirectional text embedding levels for Unicode text using the FriBidi algorithm
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes UTF-8 text input, allocates arrays based on character count, and iterates through text to collect bidi type information

vulnerability.triggering_action: Passing invalid UTF-8 strings to the function
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Buffer overflow due to mismatch between loop iteration count and allocated array size
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The loop iterates based on byte positions (p < text + length) while arrays are allocated based on character count (n_chars). Invalid UTF-8 sequences can cause g_utf8_next_char to advance incorrectly, leading to more iterations than allocated array elements
required_preconditions: Invalid UTF-8 input text
Length parameter that doesn't match valid UTF-8 boundaries
Application calls pango_itemize or similar with malformed input

fix.strategy: Add bounds check within the iteration loop to prevent array overrun
added_guards: if (i == n_chars) break;
changed_operations: Added early loop termination when iteration count reaches allocated array size
fix.post_fix_invariant: Loop iterations never exceed n_chars, ensuring array accesses stay within bounds regardless of UTF-8 validity

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse color specification strings from XPS documents, handling different color formats including hex, sc#, and ContextColor.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted input string to extract color component values into a caller-provided samples array. The ContextColor format includes a space-separated profile name followed by comma-separated numeric component values.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a ContextColor string with a large number of comma-separated component values.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Lack of validation on the count of parsed color components before writing to fixed-size output array.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function calculates 'n' as count_commas(p) + 1, then writes up to 'n' float values into the 'samples' array. The caller-provided 'samples' array has a fixed maximum capacity (implied by FZ_MAX_COLORS), but the function wrote beyond this capacity when n exceeded it.
required_preconditions: Input string uses ContextColor format
String contains more comma-separated component values than the system's maximum allowed (FZ_MAX_COLORS)

fix.strategy: Add bounds check to limit number of parsed components to system maximum.
added_guards: Check if n > FZ_MAX_COLORS after counting commas
If exceeded, warn and clamp n to FZ_MAX_COLORS
changed_operations: Added conditional clamping of 'n' before writing to samples array
fix.post_fix_invariant: Number of color components written to samples array never exceeds FZ_MAX_COLORS.

functional_semantics.purpose: Read a specified number of bytes from a guest file via QEMU Guest Agent
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory based on user-provided count parameter, reads file content into buffer, encodes result as base64

vulnerability.triggering_action: Send crafted QMP command with guest-file-read containing large count value
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in memory allocation calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Missing upper bound check on count parameter before using it in g_malloc0(count+1)
required_preconditions: Guest agent socket accessible
Valid file handle
Count value large enough to cause overflow when adding 1

fix.strategy: Add upper bound validation before memory allocation
added_guards: count >= UINT32_MAX check
changed_operations: Parameter validation range extended
fix.post_fix_invariant: count parameter must be non-negative and less than UINT32_MAX before memory allocation

functional_semantics.purpose: Read file content from guest system via QEMU Guest Agent
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates buffer based on user-provided count value, reads file data into buffer, encodes result as base64

vulnerability.triggering_action: Sending crafted QMP command with guest-file-read containing large count value
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in buffer allocation size calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Missing upper bound check on count parameter before allocation
required_preconditions: Guest agent socket accessible
Valid file handle provided

fix.strategy: Add upper bound validation on input parameter
added_guards: count >= UINT32_MAX check
changed_operations: Extended conditional check for count validity
fix.post_fix_invariant: count must be non-negative and less than UINT32_MAX before allocation

functional_semantics.purpose: Allocate memory for a netfilter table information structure with additional size for rule data
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Calculates total allocation size by adding structure size to user-provided size parameter

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling IPT_SO_SET_REPLACE setsockopt with a large size value
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in size calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Addition of size_t sz = sizeof(*info) + size can wrap around when size is sufficiently large, making sz smaller than sizeof(*info)
required_preconditions: 32-bit platform
size parameter close to maximum unsigned integer value

fix.strategy: Add overflow check before allocation
added_guards: if (sz < sizeof(*info)) return NULL;
fix.post_fix_invariant: Total allocation size is guaranteed to be at least as large as the base structure size

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse a JBIG2 text region segment from a PDF file, which involves reading region information, symbol dictionaries, and constructing a bitmap from symbol instances.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accumulates a total symbol count (numSyms) by summing sizes of referenced symbol dictionary segments without overflow checking.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a JBIG2 text region segment that references multiple symbol dictionaries whose combined size causes an integer overflow in the numSyms counter.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing overflow check during arithmetic accumulation of untrusted input.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The variable 'numSyms' is incremented by the size of each referenced symbol dictionary segment using simple addition ('numSyms += segSize'). If the total exceeds the maximum value representable by the unsigned integer type, it wraps around, leading to an undersized allocation and subsequent out-of-bounds memory access.
required_preconditions: The input file is maliciously crafted with JBIG2 text region segments referencing symbol dictionaries.
The sum of the sizes of the referenced symbol dictionaries exceeds 2^N - 1 (where N is the number of bits in the unsigned integer type used for numSyms).

fix.strategy: Replace the unchecked addition with a checked addition that detects overflow and aborts processing.
added_guards: A call to a checked addition function (checkedAdd) that returns a boolean indicating success/failure due to overflow.
changed_operations: Replaced 'numSyms += segSize' with 'if (unlikely(checkedAdd(numSyms, segSize, &numSyms))) { error(...); return; }'
fix.post_fix_invariant: The 'numSyms' variable is guaranteed not to overflow during accumulation. If an overflow would occur, an error is reported and function execution stops.

functional_semantics.purpose: Allocate and configure channels for macvlan interfaces on a network interface
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Dynamically allocates kernel memory for channel structures and adds them to a list; cleans up on failure

vulnerability.triggering_action: i40e_setup_channel() returns false (failure) after successful memory allocation
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Resource leak due to missing cleanup of allocated memory on partial failure
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When i40e_setup_channel() fails after kzalloc() succeeds, the allocated channel structure is not freed before jumping to error handling
required_preconditions: Memory allocation succeeds
i40e_setup_channel() fails

fix.strategy: Explicitly free the allocated channel structure before error path when channel setup fails
added_guards: kfree(ch) call before goto err_free
changed_operations: Added cleanup of channel allocation on i40e_setup_channel() failure
fix.post_fix_invariant: Every successfully allocated channel structure is either properly initialized and added to list, or explicitly freed before error path

functional_semantics.purpose: Allocate a custom-sized memory region for regional allocator
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates memory of specified size and stores that size for later use

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling regional_create_custom with size argument that causes integer overflow when aligned up
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in size calculation before memory allocation validation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The ALIGN_UP macro performed on the size parameter could overflow before the size check against sizeof(struct regional)
required_preconditions: Size parameter passed to ALIGN_UP macro causes integer overflow
Overflowed size still passes sizeof(struct regional) check

fix.strategy: Perform size alignment before validation check
changed_operations: Moved ALIGN_UP operation before size validation
fix.post_fix_invariant: Size validation uses aligned size value

functional_semantics.purpose: Store a temporary copy of a ZRTP packet header in a fixed-size buffer

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a ZRTP packet with a large length field
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unbounded copy into fixed-size buffer
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The length parameter for memcpy is calculated from untrusted packet data without validation against buffer size
required_preconditions: Packet length field controlled by remote attacker
Calculated length exceeds buffer size

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds check before copy operation
added_guards: Length comparison against buffer size
Clamping of copy length to maximum buffer size
changed_operations: Added conditional truncation of copy length
Changed length variable type from int32_t to uint32_t
fix.post_fix_invariant: Copy length never exceeds destination buffer size

functional_semantics.purpose: Process and decode raw image data from various camera formats, allocating buffers for pixel data based on decoder type.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates and manages multiple memory buffers for image data, with complex pointer aliasing between different buffer representations.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malformed Foveon or sRAW image file.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Double free vulnerability due to incorrect pointer management during buffer ownership transfer.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: In the LEGACY decoder path, imgdata.rawdata.raw_alloc was allocated and assigned, then imgdata.image was set to point to the same allocation. Later, imgdata.image was nulled while imgdata.rawdata.color_image was set to point to the same raw_alloc buffer. This created ambiguity about which pointer owned the allocation, potentially leading to multiple deallocation attempts.
required_preconditions: LIBRAW_DECODER_LEGACY flag is set
Processing specific image formats (Foveon or sRAW)
Error or exception path that triggers cleanup

fix.strategy: Clarify buffer ownership by separating allocations and eliminating shared ownership.
changed_operations: In LEGACY decoder path: raw_alloc is set to 0/null instead of being allocated
imgdata.image receives its own allocation via calloc()
During recovery: raw_alloc and color_image are explicitly set to point to imgdata.image's allocation before imgdata.image is nulled
fix.post_fix_invariant: Each buffer pointer has unambiguous ownership; no single allocation is referenced by multiple owning pointers that could be independently freed.

functional_semantics.purpose: The did_set_string_option function validates and processes changes to string options in Vim. It checks option values for validity, performs necessary side effects, and returns error messages if validation fails.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function validates user-supplied option values before applying them. It includes security checks such as preventing changes to certain options in secure/sandbox mode (P_SECURE flag) and validating file names (P_NFNAME flag).

vulnerability.triggering_action: Setting the 'keymap', 'filetype', or 'syntax' options to a specially crafted value via a modeline or other input.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of option values before they are used in subsequent operations.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function did_set_string_option lacked validation for the 'keymap', 'filetype', and 'syntax' option values. These options were passed to other functions (like keymap_init() and autocmd handlers) without checking if the values contained only safe characters, potentially allowing arbitrary code execution.
required_preconditions: Vim opens a file containing a malicious modeline
The modeline sets 'keymap', 'filetype', or 'syntax' to a crafted value
Secure mode is not enabled (or the option doesn't have P_SECURE flag)

fix.strategy: Add validation checks for specific options before processing them.
added_guards: Added 'if (!valid_filetype(*varp)) errmsg = e_invarg;' for 'keymap' option
Added 'if (!valid_filetype(*varp)) errmsg = e_invarg;' for 'filetype' option
Added 'if (!valid_filetype(*varp)) errmsg = e_invarg;' for 'syntax' option
changed_operations: For 'keymap': validation added before calling keymap_init()
For 'filetype': validation added before triggering FileType autocommand
For 'syntax': validation added before triggering Syntax autocommand
fix.post_fix_invariant: The 'keymap', 'filetype', and 'syntax' option values are validated using valid_filetype() before being processed, preventing malicious values from reaching downstream operations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Open a timer instance (master or slave) for ALSA sound subsystem
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Manages timer instance creation, validation, and cleanup with shared resource access

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling snd_timer_close_locked on a partially initialized or wrong timer instance
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use-after-free due to variable reuse after refactoring
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'timeri' variable was reused for different purposes after refactoring, leading to snd_timer_close_locked being called on an incorrect instance
required_preconditions: Master timer instance opening path
Exclusive flag check failure on existing timer instance

fix.strategy: Separate variable usage to avoid confusion between different timer instances
changed_operations: Introduced separate variable 't' for checking existing instance flags

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse command line arguments for sudo/sudoedit, determining execution mode and flags.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Handles argument parsing for privilege escalation tool; validates flag combinations and mode transitions.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Invoke sudoedit with '-s' flag and a command-line argument ending with a single backslash character.

vulnerability.detailed_cause: The 'valid_flags' variable was not properly restricted for edit mode, permitting the '-s' flag (shell mode) to be combined with edit mode, leading to unexpected code paths during argument processing.
required_preconditions: Program invoked as sudoedit or with -e flag
-s flag present
Command-line argument ending with backslash

fix.strategy: Define and enforce mode-specific valid flag sets using named constants.
added_guards: EDIT_VALID_FLAGS constant for edit mode
LIST_VALID_FLAGS constant for list mode
VALIDATE_VALID_FLAGS constant for validate mode
changed_operations: Set valid_flags to EDIT_VALID_FLAGS when mode becomes MODE_EDIT
Set valid_flags to LIST_VALID_FLAGS when mode becomes MODE_LIST
Set valid_flags to VALIDATE_VALID_FLAGS when mode becomes MODE_VALIDATE

functional_semantics.purpose: Process the tail of an IKEv1 packet, handling decryption, payload parsing, and validation.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates payload types and ordering against expected state, logs and rejects malformed packets, and handles encrypted vs. unencrypted packet flows.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Sending a specially-crafted IKEv1 Informational Exchange packet.

vulnerability.detailed_cause: When logging an error message for an unexpected payload type, the code dereferenced `st->st_state->name` after a check that `st` could be NULL. The NULL check was present earlier in the function but not consistently enforced at all error logging sites.
required_preconditions: Unencrypted packet
Unexpected payload type in message
State (`st`) is NULL

fix.strategy: Replace the dereferenced state pointer with a safe reference to a state name from the state machine context, which is guaranteed to be valid.
changed_operations: Changed `st->st_state->name` to `finite_states[smc->state]->name` in the error log message for unexpected payload types.

functional_semantics.purpose: Read and parse Windows Metafile (WMF) image format, converting vector graphics to raster images.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates and uses external library resources (libwmf API handle) to parse potentially malicious input files. The function contains multiple error handling paths that must properly clean up allocated resources before returning.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malformed WMF file that causes early failure in certain libwmf API calls.

vulnerability.detailed_cause: When specific libwmf API functions (wmf_api_create, wmf_bbuf_input, wmf_scan, wmf_size, wmf_play) fail, the error handling code calls wmf_api_destroy(API) before throwing an exception, but in some cases other cleanup operations accessing API-dependent data occur after the destruction.
required_preconditions: Malformed WMF input file
Failure occurs in specific libwmf API calls
Debug logging may be enabled

fix.strategy: Reorder cleanup operations to ensure the API handle is destroyed only after all API-dependent cleanup is complete.
changed_operations: Moved wmf_api_destroy(API) calls to occur after all other cleanup operations that might access API-dependent data
Ensured consistent ordering across all error paths
fix.post_fix_invariant: The API handle is never destroyed while cleanup code still needs to access API-dependent data structures.

functional_semantics.purpose: Configures zone update policy rules (allow/deny) for dynamic DNS updates based on identity, match type, and resource record types.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses update-policy configuration statements to create a security table that controls which identities can modify which DNS records in a zone.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a zone update-policy configuration where a matchtype value maps to the internal 'dns_ssumatchtype_subdomain' type.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect mapping between configuration semantics and internal enforcement logic.

Other matchtypes like 'subdomain' also map to the same internal type but have different semantics regarding the target name field.

A statement uses a matchtype like 'subdomain' (not 'zonesub')
The statement grants update privileges

functional_semantics.purpose: Find the position of the most significant set bit (first one from left) in a non-negative integer.

Caller provides negative integer
