functional_semantics.purpose: Read and parse a PWP image format file, extracting embedded SFW images to temporary files for further processing.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Writes extracted image data to a temporary file using fputc without checking for write failures.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted image file that causes fputc to fail during write operations.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unchecked error return from output function.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The fputc function's return value is ignored, allowing write failures to go undetected while the program continues execution.
required_preconditions: A temporary file must be successfully opened
The program must be processing image data

fix.strategy: Add explicit check of fputc return value against expected written character.
added_guards: if (fputc(c,file) != c) break;
changed_operations: fputc call now has its return value compared to the written character
fix.post_fix_invariant: Loop terminates if fputc fails to write the expected character.

functional_semantics.purpose: Convert a raw pixel data row into ImageMagick's internal pixel representation based on bits-per-pixel depth.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes input pixel data without validating that computed color indices are within the allocated colormap bounds.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted image file that produces out-of-bounds color indices.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check before using a computed index to access an array.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function used computed color indices to access the 'colormap' array without verifying they are less than 'image->colors' (the allocated colormap size).
required_preconditions: Input image data produces a color index >= image->colors
The colormap array is allocated with size image->colors

fix.strategy: Add bounds checks before colormap array accesses.
added_guards: Conditional check 'if (index < image->colors)' before each 'SetPixelViaPixelInfo(image, image->colormap+(ssize_t) index, q)' call
changed_operations: Replaced unconditional colormap access with guarded access
fix.post_fix_invariant: Colormap is only accessed when the computed index is within the allocated bounds.

functional_semantics.purpose: Allocate a 2D data array based on property values
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Calculates allocation size from user-controlled property values without validation

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted file with manipulated NUMBER_OF_FIELDS or NUMBER_OF_SETS properties
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in size calculation leading to heap buffer overflow
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Multiplication of (nSamples+1) and (nPatches+1) can overflow 32-bit integer range when values are large
required_preconditions: User provides input file
File contains NUMBER_OF_FIELDS and NUMBER_OF_SETS properties
Property values cause overflow when incremented and multiplied

fix.strategy: Add bounds validation before allocation calculation
added_guards: Check nSamples and nPatches are non-negative
Check values do not exceed 0x7ffe
fix.post_fix_invariant: nSamples and nPatches are within safe bounds before multiplication

functional_semantics.purpose: Read device state data from kernel space to user space
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Copies kernel buffer content to user-provided buffer with bounds checking

vulnerability.triggering_action: User-space read operation on the yurex device
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Incorrect bounds checking during user-space copy
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The original code used copy_to_user with a calculation (bytes_read - *ppos) that didn't properly consider the user-provided count parameter
required_preconditions: Local attacker access to the device file
Device in connected state

fix.strategy: Replace manual bounds checking with a standard kernel helper function
changed_operations: Replaced custom copy_to_user logic with simple_read_from_buffer
fix.post_fix_invariant: All user-space copies are bounded by both kernel buffer size and user-provided count parameter

functional_semantics.purpose: Verify a PKCS#1 v1.5 signature by decrypting it with RSA public key and extracting the hash value.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function accepts a signature, decrypts it, and attempts to parse the PKCS#1 v1.5 padded structure to extract the embedded hash.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a forged X.509 certificate containing a crafted RSA signature.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient validation of the structure and metadata of a PKCS#1 v1.5 signature after decryption.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The original code only searched for a null byte to locate the start of the ASN.1 metadata and hash, without verifying the overall structure length, the padding bytes, the ASN.1 Object Identifier, or the hash length. This allowed crafted signatures with incorrect metadata to be accepted.
required_preconditions: Small RSA public exponents are in use (eases signature forgery).

fix.strategy: Enforce strict structural validation of the entire PKCS#1 v1.5 signature block.
added_guards: Check total signature length is sufficient for required fields.
Verify the block starts with '0x00 0x01'.
Verify all padding bytes are '0xFF'.
Verify the separator byte after padding is '0x00'.
Verify the ASN.1 metadata matches the expected hash algorithm.
Use the expected hash length from metadata to extract the hash.
changed_operations: Replaced heuristic search for data start with deterministic parsing based on known structure.
Added input parameter 'sig_type' to specify expected hash algorithm for metadata verification.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The signature is only accepted if its decrypted block conforms exactly to the PKCS#1 v1.5 format for the specified hash algorithm, including correct padding and ASN.1 metadata.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse and validate modifier state predicates from XKB keymap expressions
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes user-supplied keymap expressions to resolve modifier masks and match operations

vulnerability.triggering_action: Supplying a crafted keymap file with a no-op modmask expression
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of a pointer before dereference
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function allowed expr->action.args to be NULL when expr->expr.op was EXPR_ACTION_DECL, but later passed this NULL pointer to ExprResolveModMask
required_preconditions: Local attacker access
Ability to supply crafted keymap file
Parser processes the file

fix.strategy: Add early validation to reject NULL arguments
added_guards: Check for !expr->action.args in EXPR_ACTION_DECL case
changed_operations: Extended conditional to require non-NULL args
fix.post_fix_invariant: expr->action.args is guaranteed non-NULL when EXPR_ACTION_DECL path proceeds

functional_semantics.purpose: Resolve left-hand side expressions to extract element, field, and index components from a parsed expression tree.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function returns boolean success/failure and writes results to output pointer parameters. Callers may use output values without checking the return value.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Parsing a crafted keymap file containing invalid atoms in field reference or array reference expressions.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of return values from helper functions before treating them as valid pointers.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function called xkb_atom_text() which can return NULL for invalid atoms, but the function returned true without checking those return values. Callers could dereference the NULL pointers stored in output parameters.
required_preconditions: A crafted keymap file with invalid atoms is supplied
The parser reaches EXPR_FIELD_REF or EXPR_ARRAY_REF cases

fix.strategy: Add explicit NULL checks for all xkb_atom_text() return values before returning success.
added_guards: *elem_rtrn != NULL
*field_rtrn != NULL
expr->array_ref.element != XKB_ATOM_NONE && *elem_rtrn == NULL
changed_operations: Changed EXPR_FIELD_REF return from unconditional true to check both element and field
Added two checks in EXPR_ARRAY_REF case before returning true
fix.post_fix_invariant: When function returns true, all non-NULL output string pointers point to valid strings.

functional_semantics.purpose: Copy and validate key aliases from parsing information to a keymap structure
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes an array of alias definitions, validates them against existing keys, and allocates memory for valid aliases

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted keymap file containing invalid aliases
vulnerability.abstract_cause: NULL pointer dereference
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Accessing a pointer that was never initialized when no aliases pass validation
required_preconditions: num_key_aliases == 0 after validation
key_aliases pointer remains NULL
Code attempts to iterate through key_aliases array

fix.strategy: Move iteration logic inside the conditional block that checks for positive alias count
changed_operations: Relocated the alias copying loop inside the 'if (num_key_aliases > 0)' block
fix.post_fix_invariant: The alias copying loop only executes when memory has been successfully allocated for the aliases array

functional_semantics.purpose: Append a multi-keysym list to an existing expression's keysym list
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Frees memory associated with the 'append' parameter after concatenating its contents

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted keymap file
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Invalid memory deallocation due to incorrect pointer casting
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The FreeStmt function was called with a pointer to the address of 'append' rather than the pointer itself, causing an invalid free
required_preconditions: Local attacker can supply a crafted keymap file
xkbcommon parses the malicious file

fix.strategy: Correct pointer argument passed to memory deallocation function
changed_operations: Changed FreeStmt argument from '&append' to 'append'
fix.post_fix_invariant: The pointer passed to FreeStmt matches the type expected by the function

functional_semantics.purpose: Lexical analyzer for parsing keymap files, tokenizing input stream into symbols like keysyms, strings, identifiers, and special characters.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes input characters sequentially, with loops that continue while certain conditions hold. Missing termination checks in loops can cause infinite processing.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Parsing a crafted keymap file containing a keysym literal (enclosed in '<' and '>') that never contains the closing '>' character and also never reaches end-of-line.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Infinite loop due to missing loop termination condition.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The loop 'while (peek(s) != '>' && !eol(s))' for parsing LHS keysym literals only checked for the closing '>' and end-of-line, but not for end-of-file. If input ends before either condition is met, the loop would never terminate.
required_preconditions: Local attacker can supply or influence keymap file parsing.
Keymap file contains a keysym literal starting with '<' but no subsequent '>' or newline before file ends.

fix.strategy: Add missing termination condition to prevent infinite loop.
added_guards: eof(s)
changed_operations: Modified loop condition in LHS keysym parsing from 'while (peek(s) != '>' && !eol(s))' to 'while (peek(s) != '>' && !eol(s) && !eof(s))'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: All character consumption loops in the lexer now explicitly check for end-of-file condition alongside other termination criteria.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse and compile a keymap file containing multiple sections, validating required sections are present and compiling each.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Iterates through a linked list of file sections, validates their types, collects them into an array, and later accesses them by array index for compilation.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted keymap file containing a geometry section.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: A NULL pointer dereference during the compilation phase.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function's first loop collects valid file sections into an array indexed by file_type. A geometry section (FILE_TYPE_GEOMETRY) is considered invalid and is not added to the array, leaving files[FILE_TYPE_GEOMETRY] as NULL. However, the later compilation loop iterates over all types from FIRST_KEYMAP_FILE_TYPE to LAST_KEYMAP_FILE_TYPE and attempts to access files[type]->name without checking if files[type] is NULL for the geometry type.
required_preconditions: A keymap file containing a geometry section is supplied as input.

fix.strategy: Change the validation logic to explicitly handle and ignore the geometry section type, preventing it from being incorrectly classified as a required keymap section.
added_guards: An explicit check for file->file_type == FILE_TYPE_GEOMETRY during the initial section collection loop.
changed_operations: Changed the error handling for an out-of-range file_type: for geometry, log a verbose message and continue; for other invalid types, log an error and continue.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The geometry section type is explicitly filtered out during the collection phase, ensuring it is never placed into the 'files' array and is therefore not required to be present during the later validation and compilation loops.

functional_semantics.purpose: Verify RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 signatures by checking padding format and extracting the signature payload.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Validates RSA signature padding structure but initially only checked boundary bytes, not the content of padding bytes.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Signature verification with forged padding that has correct boundary bytes but incorrect internal padding values.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient validation of cryptographic padding structure.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function only verified the first two bytes (0x00, 0x01) and the separator byte after padding (0x00), but did not validate that all padding bytes between them were 0xFF as required by PKCS#1 v1.5.
required_preconditions: Using RSA with small public exponents
RAW RSA keys in IKEv2 signature verification

fix.strategy: Added explicit validation that all padding bytes between the header and separator are 0xFF.
added_guards: Loop counting 0xFF bytes in padding region
Comparison ensuring count equals expected padding length
changed_operations: Added padding content verification before returning success
fix.post_fix_invariant: All padding bytes between 0x01 and the 0x00 separator must be 0xFF.

functional_semantics.purpose: Select and configure Spectre variant 2 mitigations for x86 CPUs.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Enables CPU features and sets up mitigations (retpoline, RSB filling, IBPB, IBRS) based on CPU capabilities, vendor, and command-line input.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A context switch on a CPU affected by Spectre v2.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient mitigation of speculative execution side-channel attacks.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The RSB (Return Stack Buffer) was not always filled upon a context switch, leaving a window for userspace-to-userspace SpectreRSB attacks.
required_preconditions: CPU is affected by Spectre v2 (X86_BUG_SPECTRE_V2).
Spectre v2 mitigation is enabled (e.g., retpoline).
A context switch occurs.

fix.strategy: Unconditionally enable RSB filling on context switch when Spectre v2 protection is active.
changed_operations: Removed the conditional check for PTI, SMEP, or Skylake-era CPU before enabling RSB_CTXSW.
Made the call to `setup_force_cpu_cap(X86_FEATURE_RSB_CTXSW)` unconditional (within the scope of Spectre v2 being enabled).
fix.post_fix_invariant: If Spectre v2 mitigation is enabled, the RSB is always filled on context switch.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse a smart-protocol 'ng' packet containing a reference name and message separated by space
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted network input without validating length before pointer arithmetic and string operations

vulnerability.triggering_action: Remote attacker sends a crafted 'ng' packet lacking a null terminator after the reference name
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds read due to insufficient input length validation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Using strchr on untrusted input without verifying the input contains the expected delimiter, allowing pointer arithmetic beyond buffer bounds
required_preconditions: Network input is attacker-controlled
Packet length is insufficient for expected format

fix.strategy: Add explicit length checks before pointer manipulation and replace strchr with bounded memchr
added_guards: Check total length before skipping prefix
Check remaining length before searching for delimiter
Check remaining length before searching for newline
changed_operations: Replaced strchr with memchr to respect length bounds
fix.post_fix_invariant: All pointer arithmetic and delimiter searches respect explicitly tracked remaining length

functional_semantics.purpose: Authenticate a client using host-based authentication by verifying a cryptographic signature
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes authentication packets containing user identity and cryptographic material

vulnerability.triggering_action: Receiving an authentication request with an invalid user name
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Early termination of authentication processing before completing packet parsing
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function checked for invalid user context and returned immediately, before fully parsing the entire authentication packet
required_preconditions: Authentication request uses host-based method
User context is invalid

fix.strategy: Delay early return until after packet parsing is complete
added_guards: Moved user validity check after packet parsing operations
changed_operations: Reordered operations to parse entire packet before checking user validity
fix.post_fix_invariant: Packet parsing always completes regardless of user validity

functional_semantics.purpose: Authenticate a user via public key authentication in SSH
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes public key authentication requests, validates keys, checks user validity, and sends authentication responses

vulnerability.triggering_action: Sending a malformed authentication packet with an invalid user
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Early bailout before full packet parsing leaks user existence information
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function checked for invalid user (authctxt->valid) before fully parsing the incoming authentication packet, allowing timing differences that reveal whether a user exists
required_preconditions: Attacker can send authentication packets
Server uses public key authentication

fix.strategy: Delay user validity check until after packet is fully parsed
added_guards: Moved authctxt->valid check after packet parsing in both signature and non-signature paths
changed_operations: Reordered operations to parse complete packet before checking user validity
fix.post_fix_invariant: Packet parsing completes before any user existence checks are performed

functional_semantics.purpose: Retrieve information about a symbolic link
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Accesses filesystem metadata without checking path restrictions

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling linkinfo() function with a path
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing access control check
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function performed filesystem operations without validating the path against open_basedir restrictions
required_preconditions: Windows platform
open_basedir configuration enabled
Path argument points outside allowed directories

fix.strategy: Add path validation before filesystem access
added_guards: open_basedir check on the directory portion of the path
changed_operations: Added directory extraction and validation step before stat operation
fix.post_fix_invariant: linkinfo() validates path against open_basedir before accessing filesystem

functional_semantics.purpose: Iterate over text to identify emoji sequences and determine their presentation type (emoji vs. text).
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes UTF-8 encoded Unicode text character by character, using lookahead for certain sequences. Invalid or malformed sequences could cause infinite loops or crashes.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing crafted text containing invalid Unicode sequences.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Lack of progress guarantee in iteration loop under certain input conditions.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The iterator could stall (iter->start == iter->end) when processing specific character sequences, such as variation selectors (e.g., VC15 followed by VC16), causing no forward movement in the text buffer.
required_preconditions: Input contains specific Unicode sequences (like VC15 followed by VC16) that trick the emoji classification logic.
The iterator's start and end pointers become equal.

fix.strategy: Enforce progress by advancing the end pointer when a stall is detected.
added_guards: A check for (iter->start == iter->end) before returning TRUE.
changed_operations: Added forced advancement: iter->end = g_utf8_next_char(iter->end) when stall condition is met.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The iterator always advances by at least one character before returning TRUE, preventing infinite loops.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse KWAJ archive file headers, reading optional header sections based on flag bits.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Reads variable-length strings from file with maximum length constraints, copies them into fixed-size buffers, and seeks file position based on string length.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a KWAJ file header with filename or extension strings that lack null terminators within their maximum allowed length.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Out-of-bounds write due to incorrect handling of unterminated strings.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code assumed filename (9 bytes) and extension (4 bytes) strings read from the file would be null-terminated. When strings filled the entire allocated length without a null terminator, the string copy loop would write one byte past the allocated buffer while appending a null terminator later in the code.
required_preconditions: Malicious KWAJ file with filename or extension header flags set
Filename exactly 9 bytes with no null terminator, or extension exactly 4 bytes with no null terminator

fix.strategy: Explicitly reject strings that occupy maximum length without null termination, and adjust file seeking logic.
added_guards: Check if read string fills buffer without null terminator and return error
Verify minimum read length of 2 bytes for strings
changed_operations: Changed from unconditional 9/4 byte reads to checking actual bytes read
Changed seeking logic to account for partial reads
Removed redundant null terminator assignment
fix.post_fix_invariant: Filename strings must be null-terminated within their maximum length, and extension strings must be null-terminated within their maximum length.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse TLS extensions from a ServerHello message during TLS handshake.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Allocates and stores extension data (e.g., EC point formats) in the session object for later use.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a ServerHello with an EC point formats extension during session resumption.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Race condition due to unsafe concurrent modification of shared session data.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function unconditionally overwrites the session's EC point format list, even when resuming a session (s->hit is true). In a multithreaded environment, another thread might be using the same session object concurrently, leading to a use-after-free or double-free if the list is freed while in use.
required_preconditions: Multithreading enabled
Session resumption (s->hit true)
Server sends EC point formats extension

fix.strategy: Skip modification of session data during resumption.
added_guards: if (!s->hit) condition around allocation/copy of EC point format list
changed_operations: Moved session->tlsext_ecpointformatlist allocation and copy inside a conditional block
fix.post_fix_invariant: Session data is only modified on a full handshake, not during resumption.

functional_semantics.purpose: Write audio metadata tag for MOV container format
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Computes audio format parameters including division by channel count

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing crafted audio file with zero channels
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Divide-by-zero
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Division by track->par->channels when channels=0
required_preconditions: Audio track with channels=0
Version=1 code path execution

fix.strategy: Prevent zero-channel tracks from entering vulnerable code path
added_guards: Check for zero channels in version selection logic
changed_operations: Modified version selection condition
fix.post_fix_invariant: Version 1 code path not reachable when channels=0

functional_semantics.purpose: Generate a filename for a header cache based on a given path.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Constructs a cache filename by appending a suffix to an input path without validating or sanitizing the path input.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a newsrc entry containing '/' characters in a component that becomes part of a cache pathname.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Unsafe path construction allowing special characters in input to affect filesystem path resolution.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function concatenates a user-controlled path string with a fixed suffix without restricting '/' characters, enabling directory traversal or unsafe interaction with cache pathnames.
required_preconditions: User-controlled input is passed as the path parameter.
The constructed path is used to access or create filesystem objects.

fix.strategy: Replace the hardcoded suffix with a macro (HC_FEXT) and rename the function to reflect its specific protocol context (POP instead of NNTP), implying a more controlled suffix definition.
changed_operations: Changed the appended suffix from a literal ".hcache" to a macro reference HC_FEXT.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The cache filename suffix is defined centrally via HC_FEXT, potentially allowing stricter control over the generated filename format.

functional_semantics.purpose: Convert ASN.1 object identifier to text representation
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Writes formatted text to caller-provided buffer with length limit

vulnerability.triggering_action: Reading output from functions that use OBJ_obj2txt with pretty printing
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing null-termination guarantee in output buffer
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Function could return without ensuring null terminator in output buffer when buffer space exhausted
required_preconditions: Pretty printing enabled
Caller reads beyond valid data in buffer

fix.strategy: Ensure null-termination at every buffer modification point
added_guards: Initialize buffer with null terminator early
Add explicit null termination after each character write when buffer space remains
changed_operations: Changed buffer initialization from conditional to unconditional when buffer exists
Added explicit null assignment after writing single characters
fix.post_fix_invariant: Buffer is always null-terminated after any write operation

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse IMAP FETCH response fields including FLAGS, UID, INTERNALDATE, RFC822.SIZE, BODY, and RFC822.HEADER
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Copies untrusted input from network response into fixed-size stack buffer without bounds checking

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an IMAP FETCH response with a long INTERNALDATE or RFC822.SIZE field
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Stack buffer overflow
vulnerability.detailed_cause: While loops copying characters into tmp buffer lack bounds checks against buffer size
required_preconditions: Network attacker can send malicious IMAP response
INTERNALDATE or RFC822.SIZE field exceeds SHORT_STRING length

fix.strategy: Add bounds checking to copy loops
added_guards: ptmp != (tmp + sizeof(tmp) - 1)
changed_operations: Modified INTERNALDATE copy loop condition
Modified RFC822.SIZE copy loop condition
fix.post_fix_invariant: No more than sizeof(tmp)-1 bytes will be written to tmp buffer

functional_semantics.purpose: Process POP3 UIDL response lines to map message sequence numbers to unique identifiers
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses server-provided UIDL lines containing index and UID, creates or updates header entries

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a UIDL response line with a zero-length UID string
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of input length before use
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function processes UIDL lines without checking if the UID string has zero length after whitespace trimming
required_preconditions: Server sends UIDL response with valid index but empty UID
Client processes the malformed response

fix.strategy: Add explicit length check before processing UID string
added_guards: Check that strlen(line) != 0 after whitespace trimming
changed_operations: Added early return with error when UID length is zero
fix.post_fix_invariant: UID string must have non-zero length before being used in comparisons or stored

functional_semantics.purpose: Subscribe or unsubscribe from an IMAP mailbox, with optional local configuration tracking.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Constructs and executes an IMAP SUBSCRIBE/UNSUBSCRIBE command, and when ImapCheckSubscribed is enabled, also creates a local configuration line containing the mailbox path for tracking subscriptions.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a malicious mailbox path containing backquote characters when ImapCheckSubscribed is enabled.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Untrusted input (mailbox path) was embedded into a configuration command string without proper sanitization for the shell metacharacters of the configuration parser.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The `snprintf` call constructing the `mbox` string for `mutt_parse_rc_line` directly embedded the user-controlled `path` variable, which could contain backquote characters. These characters were not escaped, allowing them to be interpreted as command execution metacharacters by the configuration parser.
required_preconditions: The `ImapCheckSubscribed` configuration option is enabled.
The function is called with a malicious mailbox path containing backquote characters.

fix.strategy: Properly quote/escape the untrusted mailbox path before embedding it into the configuration command string.
changed_operations: Replaced the single `snprintf` that embedded `path` with a two-step operation: first, `snprintf` writes the static command prefix; second, `imap_quote_string` properly escapes the `path` content before appending it.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The user-controlled mailbox path is now correctly escaped before being passed to the configuration parser, preventing interpretation of embedded metacharacters.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse IMAP STATUS command responses containing mailbox status information like message counts, UID validity, and unseen messages.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes IMAP literal strings where the server provides a length count followed by the actual mailbox name data.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing an IMAP STATUS response containing a mailbox name as a literal with a length count.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check when using a length value to advance a buffer pointer.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function imap_get_literal_count() extracts a length value from the IMAP protocol, but before the fix, the code assumed the buffer contained at least that many bytes without verification.
required_preconditions: IMAP server sends a STATUS response with a literal mailbox name
The literal count value exceeds the actual buffer length
The program reaches the code path handling literals

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds check before using the length to compute pointer offsets.
added_guards: Check that strlen(idata->buf) >= litlen before advancing pointer
changed_operations: Added validation that buffer length is sufficient for the claimed literal length
fix.post_fix_invariant: Pointer arithmetic using litlen only occurs when the buffer contains at least litlen bytes.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse ASN.1 DER-encoded bit string data, extracting length information and copying content
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Calculates bit length from parsed byte length and a trailing unused bits count, copies data to output buffer

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing crafted ASN.1 data with negative bit length
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing validation of derived value before use
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Bit length calculation (*bit_len = len_byte * 8 - der[len_len]) could produce zero or negative value, which was not validated before subsequent operations
required_preconditions: Input contains crafted ASN.1 data
der[len_len] value causes len_byte * 8 - der[len_len] ≤ 0

fix.strategy: Add validation check for derived value
added_guards: Check if calculated bit length is positive
changed_operations: Added early return with error when *bit_len ≤ 0
fix.post_fix_invariant: Bit length is guaranteed positive before any data copying or further processing

functional_semantics.purpose: Validate PNG chunk length against implementation limits
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Calculates maximum allowed chunk size, with special handling for IDAT chunks that considers image dimensions and encoding overhead

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted PNG file
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in size calculation
vulnerability.detailed_cause: Multiplication of width, channels, and bit depth factors without proper casting to size_t before arithmetic operations

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize ownership (UID/GID) and permission bits for a new inode, respecting parent directory's SGID setting.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: When creating a file in an SGID directory, the file's group ownership is set to the directory's group. For directories, the SGID bit is always inherited. For non-directories, SGID inheritance depends on additional conditions.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A non-group member creates a plain file (not a directory) in a directory that is both SGID to a group and writable by that user.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: The SGID bit was incorrectly inherited on plain files created in SGID directories, regardless of the creator's group membership or capabilities.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The original code unconditionally set the new inode's GID to the parent directory's GID when the parent had S_ISGID set, and only added the S_ISGID bit to the mode for directories. It did not clear S_ISGID for non-directory files when the creator lacked appropriate group membership or capabilities.
required_preconditions: Parent directory has SGID bit set and is writable by a user
The user creating the file is not a member of the directory's group
The created file is a plain file (not a directory)

fix.strategy: Add a conditional check to strip the SGID bit from non-directory files when the creator lacks the right group membership and lacks the CAP_FSETID capability.
added_guards: Check if the file is not a directory
Check if the mode has both S_ISGID and S_IXGRP set
Check if the creator is not in the group of the new inode's GID
Check if the creator lacks CAP_FSETID capability relative to the directory's UID/GID
changed_operations: Added conditional clearing of S_ISGID bit from mode for non-directory files under specific conditions
fix.post_fix_invariant: A plain file created in an SGID directory by a non-group member without CAP_FSETID will not inherit the SGID bit, preventing unintended group execution.

functional_semantics.purpose: Decode MPEG-4 picture header by parsing start codes and dispatching to appropriate decoding functions based on the start code type.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses a stream of bits to identify structured elements (start codes) and sets decoder state (profile, level) based on parsed values. The state influences subsequent decoding paths and assumptions.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a crafted AVI file containing a VOS (Visual Object Sequence) start code.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: A parsed value (profile) is used to set critical decoder state before a validation check is performed on the value.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function `mpeg4_decode_profile_level` is called, which parses profile and level values from the bitstream. The returned profile value is immediately used in a conditional (`s->avctx->profile == FF_PROFILE_MPEG4_SIMPLE_STUDIO`) to set `s->studio_profile = 1`. However, the validation of the profile/level pair (`s->avctx->level > 0 && s->avctx->level < 9`) occurs *after* the profile has already been used. If the parsed profile is invalid (e.g., NULL or out-of-range), the dereference `s->avctx->profile` in the condition could trigger a NULL pointer dereference.
required_preconditions: The input bitstream contains a VOS_STARTCODE.

The bitstream following the start code contains an invalid or malformed profile value that causes `mpeg4_decode_profile_level` to leave `s->avctx->profile` in an undefined/dangerous state (e.g., NULL).
The decoder is in a state where `s->studio_profile` is not already set.

fix.strategy: Validate parsed data before using it to update critical state. Decouple the validation logic from the stored context fields.
added_guards: Store the parsed profile and level in local variables first.
Perform all validation checks on the local variables.
Only update the decoder's context (`s->avctx->profile`, `s->avctx->level`) after successful validation.
Added a new check to reject mixes of studio and non-studio profiles.
changed_operations: Changed the signature/call of `mpeg4_decode_profile_level` to return values via output parameters (`int *profile, int *level`).
The condition `s->avctx->profile == FF_PROFILE_MPEG4_SIMPLE_STUDIO` was changed to use the local `profile` variable.
The condition `s->avctx->level > 0 && s->avctx->level < 9` was changed to use the local `level` variable.
Added an assertion (`av_assert0`) later in the function to reinforce the invariant that `studio_profile` implies a specific profile.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The decoder's `s->avctx->profile` and `s->avctx->level` fields are only assigned after the parsed values have been validated. The `studio_profile` flag is only set if the validated profile is `FF_PROFILE_MPEG4_SIMPLE_STUDIO` and the validated level is within range 1-8.

fix.strategy: Eliminate double-fetch by preserving the validated header and copying only the remaining user data after the header.

vulnerability.detailed_cause: The condition for selecting the high-precision IDCT for the MPEG4 Simple Studio Profile relied on checking `avctx->profile == FF_PROFILE_MPEG4_SIMPLE_STUDIO`. However, the `idct_add` and `idct` function pointers were left uninitialized (NULL) when this condition was true, because only `idct_put` was assigned in that branch.

Profile is incorrectly detected as FF_PROFILE_MPEG4_SIMPLE_STUDIO

changed_operations: Changed the condition for selecting the high-precision IDCT function pointer from checking the AVCodecContext fields to checking a field within the IDCTDSPContext itself.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The initialization of IDCT function pointers no longer directly depends on the AVCodecContext's profile field during the init function execution; the profile-specific decision is made elsewhere and passed via the context structure.

functional_semantics.purpose: The OP_GETUPVAR instruction retrieves a value from an upvalue (a variable from an outer lexical scope) in the mruby virtual machine.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Executing the OP_GETUPVAR bytecode instruction with a 'B' argument (stack index) that is greater than or equal to the environment's stack length.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Integer overflow in the calculation of the environment nesting level ('c' argument) leads to retrieving an incorrect environment pointer, which may be NULL or point to a different, potentially freed, environment object.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function `uvenv(mrb, c)` is called with argument 'c'. If 'c' is large enough to cause an integer overflow within `uvenv`, the function may return NULL or a pointer to an unexpected `REnv` struct. The subsequent access `e->stack[b]` is performed without checking if 'e' is non-NULL and if 'b' is within bounds, leading to a use-after-free or out-of-bounds read.
required_preconditions: Deep scope nesting that generates a large 'c' argument for OP_GETUPVAR.
The 'c' argument must be large enough to cause an integer overflow in the environment level calculation.
The 'b' argument (stack index) must be within the bounds of the incorrectly retrieved environment's stack (if non-NULL) to avoid an immediate crash, potentially leading to use-after-free.

fix.strategy: Reorder and strengthen the bounds check. Ensure the environment pointer is valid AND the index is within bounds before accessing the stack.
added_guards: Check that the environment pointer 'e' is not NULL.
Check that the stack index 'b' is less than `MRB_ENV_STACK_LEN(e)` before performing the access `e->stack[b]`.
changed_operations: The condition for the access changed from 'if (!e) { ... } else { *regs_a = e->stack[b]; }' to 'if (e && b < MRB_ENV_STACK_LEN(e)) { *regs_a = e->stack[b]; } else { *regs_a = mrb_nil_value(); }'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The OP_GETUPVAR instruction will only dereference `e->stack` if 'e' is a valid pointer and the index 'b' is within the allocated stack bounds for that environment. Otherwise, it assigns nil to the target register.

functional_semantics.purpose: Handle the INT3 debug exception (breakpoint interrupt) in the kernel.

A debug exception condition (e.g., data breakpoint) pending
Execution of a MOV SS or POP SS instruction followed immediately by a kernel entry instruction like INT3

fix.strategy: Remove the debug stack usage accounting calls that were unsafe under the deferred exception scenario, as the handler does not actually use the Interrupt Stack Table (IST) for the INT3 exception.
changed_operations: Removed the debug_stack_usage_inc() call
Removed the debug_stack_usage_dec() call
fix.post_fix_invariant: The INT3 handler no longer modifies the debug stack usage counter, eliminating a potential corruption point when the exception is delivered deferred after a MOV SS/POP SS sequence.

File contains a 'ds64' chunk
Chunk size field value is less than sizeof(DS64Chunk) but passes the >= sizeof(DS64Chunk) check

fix.strategy: Enforce exact size matching for fixed-size chunk structures.
added_guards: Require chunk_header.ckSize to be exactly sizeof(DS64Chunk) for the initial read
changed_operations: Changed read size from chunk_header.ckSize to sizeof(DS64Chunk) for DS64Chunk reads
Changed wrapper addition size from chunk_header.ckSize to sizeof(DS64Chunk)
fix.post_fix_invariant: For fixed-size chunk structures, the read operation transfers exactly the size of the destination buffer, preventing buffer over-read.

vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check on a stack index before push operation.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code incremented the stack index 'stackidx' and stored an entry pointer in 'jumpstack[stackidx++]' without first verifying that 'stackidx' was less than the allocated stack size ('private->stacksize').

fix.strategy: Add a bounds check before pushing onto the jump stack to prevent overflow.
added_guards: if (unlikely(stackidx >= private->stacksize)) { verdict = NF_DROP; break; }
changed_operations: Encapsulated the 'jumpstack[stackidx++] = e;' operation within the new bounds check guard.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The stack index 'stackidx' is guaranteed to be less than 'private->stacksize' whenever 'jumpstack[stackidx++]' is written to.

fix.strategy: Enforce a minimum safe size for the scratch buffer allocation, independent of user-configurable runtime parameters.
added_guards: DEBUGASSERT(UPLOAD_BUFSIZE >= nread);
changed_operations: Changed scratch buffer allocation size from '2 * data->set.buffer_size' to '2 * UPLOAD_BUFSIZE'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The allocated scratch buffer size (2 * UPLOAD_BUFSIZE) is guaranteed to be at least twice the size of any input data chunk, as UPLOAD_BUFSIZE is a compile-time constant defining the maximum upload chunk size.

functional_semantics.purpose: Process a batch of pages to remove them from the mlocked state and update the system's NR_MLOCK accounting.

required_preconditions: The attacker must have local user privileges.
The attacker can call mlockall and munlockall system calls.

fix.strategy: Initialize the delta to -nr (assuming all pages were mlocked) and increment it for each page found to not be mlocked during the processing loop.
changed_operations: Changed the initialization and calculation of delta_munlocked. It is now initialized to -nr, and within the loop, for pages where TestClearPageMlocked fails (page was not mlocked), delta_munlocked is incremented.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The delta_munlocked value accurately reflects the net change to the NR_MLOCK counter: it decrements only for pages that were successfully removed from the mlocked state.

functional_semantics.purpose: Retrieve a network namespace by its ID from a given network namespace's ID registry.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function looks up a network namespace (peer) by ID and increments its reference count if found.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Concurrent deletion of the found network namespace after lookup but before reference count increment.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Use-after-free due to race condition between namespace lookup and reference acquisition.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function retrieved a pointer to a network namespace (peer) from an IDR (ID Registry) and then called get_net(peer) to increment its reference count. However, between the idr_find lookup and the get_net call, another thread could have removed the namespace from the IDR and decremented its reference count to zero, causing its memory to be freed. The subsequent get_net would then operate on freed memory.
required_preconditions: Concurrent execution where one thread calls get_net_ns_by_id while another deletes the same network namespace.

fix.strategy: Replace the unconditional reference count increment with a conditional one that checks if the object is still alive.
changed_operations: Replaced get_net(peer) with peer = maybe_get_net(peer).
fix.post_fix_invariant: The returned pointer, if non-NULL, points to a network namespace whose reference count has been safely incremented from a non-zero value, or is NULL if the namespace was being destroyed.

functional_semantics.purpose: Copy a huge page from user space to kernel space and map it into a target process's address space, handling both shared and private mappings.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function maps huge pages into virtual memory addresses. For shared mappings (VM_SHARED), it adds pages to a file-backed page cache. It must ensure pages are not mapped beyond the valid range of the backing file.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Calling hugetlb_mcopy_atomic_pte with a destination address (dst_addr) that corresponds to an index (idx) beyond the current size of the backing file for a shared huge page mapping.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Missing bounds check on file offset during page insertion.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: When adding a page to a shared (file-backed) huge page mapping, the function calculated the page index within the file but did not validate that this index was within the current file size. This allowed mapping a page beyond the file's end, which could later trigger an internal consistency check (BUG) when the kernel tried to reconcile the mapping with the file size.
required_preconditions: Operation on a shared huge page mapping (VM_SHARED flag set in dst_vma->vm_flags).
The calculated page index (idx) must be greater than or equal to the number of huge pages that fit in the current file size.

fix.strategy: Add bounds checks before adding the page to the cache and before finalizing the page table entry mapping.
added_guards: Check if idx >= (i_size_read(mapping->host) >> huge_page_shift(h)) before calling huge_add_to_page_cache.
Re-check the same condition after acquiring the page table lock but before setting the page table entry.
changed_operations: Moved mapping and idx variable declarations to function scope.
Added size calculation and bounds check in the VM_SHARED block before cache addition.
Added a second size calculation and bounds check after acquiring the page table lock.
fix.post_fix_invariant: For shared huge page mappings, a page is never mapped at a file offset that exceeds the current size of the backing file.

functional_semantics.purpose: Read a length-prefixed network packet with timeout handling

vulnerability.triggering_action: Killing child process after it has already terminated

Client can establish IPC connection

vulnerability.abstract_cause: Buffer overflow due to missing bounds check
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function calculates the number of output bytes needed (nsamples * sizeof(uint16)) and sets sp->stream.avail_out accordingly, but does not verify that this value is less than or equal to the allocated buffer size (sp->tbuf_size)
required_preconditions: Input image triggers PixarLog decoding path
Decompressed data size exceeds sp->tbuf_size

fix.strategy: Add explicit bounds check before decompression
added_guards: if (sp->stream.avail_out > sp->tbuf_size) return (0);
fix.post_fix_invariant: The amount of data to be decompressed (sp->stream.avail_out) never exceeds the allocated buffer size (sp->tbuf_size)

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse CHM file headers and directory structure, extracting file entries and system metadata.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Processes untrusted CHM file input, including reading and interpreting various header fields, chunk counts, and file entry data from the file.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Opening a specially crafted CHM file containing malformed system file entries.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient validation of system file name length before performing fixed-length memory comparisons.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The code performed memcmp operations with hardcoded lengths (e.g., 31L, 8L, 11L, 72L) on system file names without first verifying that the actual name_len matched those expected lengths. This could lead to reading beyond the allocated buffer bounds if the name was shorter than the comparison length.
required_preconditions: A CHM file with a system file entry (name starting with '::')
The system file name length is shorter than the hardcoded length used in memcmp
The file passes initial signature and basic format checks

fix.strategy: Add explicit length checks before performing memory comparisons.
added_guards: Check name_len equals expected length before each memcmp
Replace hardcoded length arguments in memcmp with the actual name_len variable
changed_operations: Changed from memcmp(&name[2], &content_name[2], 31L) to (name_len == 40 && memcmp(name, content_name, 40) == 0)
Changed from memcmp(&name[33], &content_name[33], 8L) to integrated into the above check
Similar changes for control_name, spaninfo_name, and rtable_name comparisons
fix.post_fix_invariant: All memory comparisons on system file names are preceded by verification that the actual name length matches the expected length for that specific system file type.

added_guards: Check current_element->string != NULL in loop condition
Check current_element->string == NULL after loop to return NULL
fix.post_fix_invariant: Function will not dereference NULL string pointer in strcmp or case_insensitive_strcmp

functional_semantics.purpose: Process IOCTL requests for a Windows kernel driver, handling various operations related to volume mounting, configuration retrieval, and system encryption.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The driver validates IOCTL input buffer sizes and performs parameter validation for certain operations. It handles user-supplied data from IRP buffers and performs operations like file opening, reading, and device enumeration.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A user-mode process sends a TC_IOCTL_GET_SYSTEM_DRIVE_CONFIG IOCTL request with a malformed DevicePath string.

vulnerability.detailed_cause: The driver accepted arbitrary DevicePath strings from user mode without validating their format or length. These strings were passed to kernel functions like RtlInitUnicodeString and ZwCreateFile, potentially causing stack-based buffer overflows.

Ability to send IOCTL requests to the driver
Malformed DevicePath string exceeding expected constraints

fix.strategy: Added strict validation of the DevicePath parameter format before processing.
added_guards: Length validation using RtlUnalignedStringCchLengthW

Length bounds checking (28-30 characters)
Memory comparison against expected patterns

Moved buffer allocation (TCalloc) after successful validation
fix.post_fix_invariant: The DevicePath parameter must match the exact format \\Device\\HarddiskXXX\\Partition0 where XXX is 0-255, and the total length must be between 28-30 characters.

functional_semantics.purpose: Parse Rockridge extensions (SUSP) in ISO9660 filesystem entries to extract extended file attributes.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Iterates over extension entries in a buffer, validating entry structure and length fields before processing. Returns success/failure status.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a specially crafted ISO9660 file with malformed Rockridge extension entries.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Infinite loop due to insufficient validation of entry length field.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The loop increment `p += p[2]` uses the entry's length field `p[2]` without ensuring it's non-zero. A zero-length entry causes no pointer advancement, resulting in infinite iteration.
required_preconditions: Input buffer contains an extension entry with length field `p[2] = 0`
Entry passes initial sanity checks (first two chars 'A'-'Z', length >=4, p+p[2] <= end)

fix.strategy: Detect and reject zero-length entries by adding a post-loop check for progress.
added_guards: Track whether any entry was processed (`entry_seen` flag)
After loop, require at least one entry processed to return success
changed_operations: Added `entry_seen` initialization
Set `entry_seen = 1` after each successful entry increment
Added fallback error return when no entries seen
fix.post_fix_invariant: Loop must process at least one valid entry to return success; zero-length entries cause error return instead of infinite loop.

functional_semantics.purpose: Retrieve uncompressed data from a 7zip archive, handling both copy mode (direct data access) and packed mode (decompressed data access).
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function reads archive data and returns pointers to buffers containing uncompressed content. It must ensure returned data does not exceed available uncompressed bytes.

vulnerability.triggering_action: Opening a specially crafted 7zip file that triggers the copy mode code path.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: Insufficient data validation when reading ahead in copy mode.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The function called __archive_read_ahead with a hardcoded value of 1 instead of the 'minimum' parameter, potentially returning less data than expected by subsequent logic.
required_preconditions: Archive is in copy mode (codec == _7Z_COPY and codec2 == (unsigned long)-1)
Crafted file triggers this code path

fix.strategy: Ensure sufficient data is read by passing the 'minimum' parameter to __archive_read_ahead instead of a hardcoded value.
changed_operations: Changed __archive_read_ahead(a, 1, &bytes_avail) to __archive_read_ahead(a, minimum, &bytes_avail)
fix.post_fix_invariant: The function now reads at least 'minimum' bytes when in copy mode, matching the packed mode behavior.

functional_semantics.purpose: Trace a Bézier curve by computing intermediate points and adding them to a primitive path.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: The function allocates memory for coefficients and point arrays, performs calculations on coordinate data, and updates a primitive info structure that is part of a larger drawing context.

vulnerability.triggering_action: A use-after-free occurs when the function accesses the 'primitive_info' pointer after it may have been invalidated by a memory reallocation in a called function.
vulnerability.abstract_cause: A pointer to a memory location within a dynamically allocated array is used after that array may have been reallocated and moved, leaving the pointer dangling.
vulnerability.detailed_cause: The local variable 'primitive_info' is calculated from 'mvg_info->primitive_info' and 'mvg_info->offset' at the start of the function. Later, the function 'CheckPrimitiveExtent' is called, which, based on its name and context, likely performs memory management on the 'mvg_info->primitive_info' array (e.g., reallocating it). After this call, the previously calculated 'primitive_info' pointer is used without being refreshed, potentially pointing to freed memory.
required_preconditions: The 'CheckPrimitiveExtent' function must trigger a reallocation of the '*mvg_info->primitive_info' array.
The reallocation must cause the original memory block to be freed or moved.
The function must proceed to use the stale 'primitive_info' pointer after the reallocation.

fix.strategy: Refresh the local 'primitive_info' pointer after any function call that may invalidate it by re-calculating it from the master pointer and offset.
changed_operations: Moved the line 'primitive_info=(*mvg_info->primitive_info)+mvg_info->offset;' to a position after the call to 'CheckPrimitiveExtent' and before the subsequent code that uses 'primitive_info'.
fix.post_fix_invariant: The local 'primitive_info' pointer is guaranteed to be valid (not dangling) for all uses after the point where 'CheckPrimitiveExtent' is called, as it is recalculated from the potentially updated master pointer.

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize decoder context for VQA video format, parsing header data and allocating buffers.
functional_semantics.security_relevant_behavior: Parses width and height from untrusted extradata, validates dimensions, and allocates buffers based on calculated sizes.

required_preconditions: Malformed VQA file with width/height values that cause integer overflow
Valid VQA header size
Supported VQA version

fix.strategy: Replace generic image size check with specialized dimension validation function.
changed_operations: Replaced av_image_check_size() with ff_set_dimensions()
fix.post_fix_invariant: Width and height values are properly validated to prevent integer overflow in subsequent buffer size calculations.

functional_semantics.purpose: Encrypt data using block cipher with buffering for partial blocks

vulnerability.triggering_action: Processing a large amount of input data when internal buffer contains existing data

required_preconditions: Internal buffer contains data (ctx->buf_len > 0)
Large input data size causing integer overflow

fix.strategy: Replaced addition-based comparison with subtraction-based comparison
added_guards: Check if (block_size - buffer_length) > input_length instead of checking if (buffer_length + input_length) < block_size
changed_operations: Changed overflow-prone addition to safe subtraction
fix.post_fix_invariant: Buffer length plus copied input data never exceeds block size without integer overflow

functional_semantics.purpose: Initialize and configure an HSR (High-availability Seamless Redundancy) network device, adding master and slave ports.

Image height small enough that curY increment exceeds height within a pass
Decoding reaches a pass where curY >= height

changed_operations: Removed conditional pass increments from within switch cases
Moved pass advancement and curY reset to separate switch block inside while loop

Image height small enough that curY increment exceeds height before next pass boundary check

changed_operations: Removed height checks from individual case statements
Added iterative pass advancement when curY exceeds height
